Excluding pre-existing sciatic palsies, any complication occurred in two of eight acetabulum-first (25.0%) versus eight of 12 pelvic ring-first patients (66.7%; p = 0.170), driven by post-traumatic osteoarthritis (12.5% vs 41.7%).

**CONCLUSION**: Concomitant pelvic ring injury significantly compromises anatomical acetabular reduction. Where precise pelvic ring reduction is achievable, pelvic ring-first fixation remains appropriate; where it is not, acetabulum-first or temporary pelvic stabilization followed by definitive fixation should be considered to avoid fixing the acetabulum onto a malreduced pelvic ring.

articles.title: A Mobile Application Improves Paramedic Performance in Simulated Trauma Care: A Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Clinical performance during prehospital trauma care varies among emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, particularly during high-stress critical responses. We developed a mobile application providing real-time access to local treatment protocols, decision support tools, and instructional procedure videos to supplement standard practice. We evaluated whether use of the application improved paramedic performance during simulated trauma scenarios.

**METHODS**: We conducted a crossover randomized controlled trial between July 2025 and February 2026 comparing standard care alone with standard care plus the mobile application during two high-fidelity trauma simulations (one adult and one pediatric). Paramedics, working in pairs, were block randomized to one of four sequences, varying both the scenario order and the application use. Performance was assessed using predefined critical actions; completing all critical actions was required to successfully complete the scenario. A generalized linear mixed model with a binomial distribution and logit link function was used for each paramedic pair to estimate the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for successfully completing a scenario with or without the application.

**RESULTS**: Of 112 paramedics, 98 (88%) participated, forming 49 pairs. One pair withdrew before study completion, leaving 48 pairs for analysis. For scenarios using the application, 17/48 (35.4%) successfully completed the scenario compared to 3/48 (6.3%) for scenarios not using the application, adjusted odds 8.28 (95% CI 2.21-31.09). Among scenarios using the application, 10/25 (40%) adult scenarios and 7/23 (30.4%) pediatric scenarios met successful completion criteria compared to 3/23 (13%) adult and 0/25 (0%) pediatric with standard practice alone. User experience survey results demonstrated that participating paramedics assessed the application as being practical to use and valuable for clinical care.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Use of the mobile decision support application improves odds of performing high-quality clinical care in simulated trauma patient scenarios. Further studies are needed to evaluate performance and usability in a field environment.

articles.title: Five-Year Experience with Automated Head Up Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Automated head-up position cardiopulmonary resuscitation (AHUP-CPR), the combination of a head and thorax positioning device, active compression-decompression CPR, and an impedance threshold device, lowers intracranial pressure and increases cerebral blood flow and neurologically favorable survival in animal models versus conventional CPR (C-CPR).

**METHODS**: This prospective, observational, investigator-initiated registry study reports 5-year multi-center outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) from areas served by emergency medical services (EMS) agencies that implemented AHUP-CPR as their routine first-responder standard of care. Adults with non-traumatic OHCA were initially treated with immediate conventional (C-CPR) followed by rapid transition to AHUP-CPR. The primary study focus was on patients who survived to hospital discharge with favorable neurological function (HD-FN). Additional analyses included assessment of sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge (HD), outcomes based upon the presenting rhythm, and impact of covariates on HD-FN.

**RESULTS**: Ten EMS agencies serving 1.5 million people across nine U.S. states contributed data to the AHUP-CPR Registry. A total of 3,709 OHCA patients met enrollment criteria. Across five years, (2020-2024), the average (± SD) interval from 9-1-1 call receipt-to-professional CPR was 9.62 ± 5.78 min. Incidence of ROSC, HD, and HD-FN were 29.5%, 13.1%, and 10.5%, respectively. The incidence of HD-FN for patients presenting with a shockable rhythm meeting Utstein criteria, pulseless electrical activity, or asystole were 33.9%, 11.8%, and 2.0%, respectively. Among 391 neurologically favorable survivors, 91% had a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 (normal or near normal brain function) at HD. The average age of the survivors was 56.8 ± 16.3 years. Age, interval from 9-1-1 call to professional CPR, witnessed status, and initial rhythm were the most significant predictors of HD-FN using multivariable Poisson regression.

**CONCLUSIONS**: In this 5-year observational registry study, use of AHUP-CPR for the treatment of OHCA was associated with survival to HD of 13.1% and HD-FN of 10.5% in the overall cohort, which comprised patients presenting in shockable rhythms, PEA, and asystole. Drawn from 3,709 OHCA patients treated across diverse EMS systems, these findings provide the largest clinical practice-based characterization to date of the outcomes associated with early transition to AHUP-CPR.

articles.title: Prehospital Resource Utilization After Video-Assisted Versus Telephone-Only Emergency Calls: A Post Hoc Analysis of the CAM-VISION Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To examine whether video assistance during emergency calls reduced actual prehospital resource utilization across the complete response pathway compared with telephone-only calls.

**METHODS**: This post hoc analysis included 18,745 calls from the cluster-randomized CAM-VISION parent trial (NCT05742412; 8,124 video; 10,621 telephone only). Outcomes were assessed at call level according to telecommunicator allocation and included unit dispatch, pathway progression, number of units, and cumulative unit time. Effects were estimated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) accounting for clustering by telecommunicator.

**RESULTS**: Initial unit dispatch occurred in 69.4% of video-group calls and 73.9% of telephone-only calls (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% confidence intervals (CI) (-10.0 to 1.0). Among calls with no unit initially dispatched, subsequent unit dispatch was uncommon (5.1% vs 5.5%). Across the complete response pathway, 71.0% versus 75.3% received at least 1 unit (risk difference, -4.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.6 to 0.8), and 69.3% versus 73.8% had a unit reach the scene (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.0 to 1.0). More than 1 unit was dispatched in 23.3% versus 25.0%. Mean units per call were 1.005 versus 1.054 (mean difference, -0.049; 95% CI, -0.148 to 0.049); mean cumulative unit time was 52.8 versus 54.3 minutes (mean difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -6.2 to 3.1). Overall, differences in initial dispatch were concentrated in ambulance use.

**CONCLUSIONS**: No statistically significant absolute differences in conventional prehospital resource utilization were observed. Point estimates were consistently lower in the video group, primarily through fewer initial dispatches, and subsequent dispatch did not materially offset this numerical difference.

articles.title: Is Social Vulnerability Associated with Discharge Disposition After Trauma Laparotomy?
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Social vulnerability may influence rehabilitation discharge after trauma independent of functional recovery needs. We evaluated whether neighborhood-level social vulnerability was associated with rehabilitation discharge and whether this association persisted when discharge appropriateness was assessed using objective mobility scores.

**STUDY DESIGN**: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included adult trauma laparotomy patients receiving physical therapy from 01/2020-06/2023. Social vulnerability was assessed using the social vulnerability index (SVI) and area deprivation index (ADI). Rehabilitation appropriateness was defined using an Activity Measure for Post-Acute Care (AM-PAC) score ≤16. Primary and secondary outcomes were rehabilitation discharge and mobility-informed rehabilitation appropriateness, respectively. Associations were evaluated using binomial regression adjusted for prespecified covariates.

**RESULTS**: Among 572 patients, 119 (20.8%) were discharged to rehabilitation, and 103 (18%) had AM-PAC scores ≤16. Median SVI was 0.75 and ADI was 63.0. Greater social vulnerability was associated with lower odds of rehabilitation discharge (SVI: aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.06-0.53, P<0.01), whereas ADI was not (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.98-1.00, P=0.21). When accounting for AM-PAC scores, neither SVI (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.39-2.88, P=0.91) nor ADI (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.99-1.01, P=0.27) was associated with appropriate rehabilitation discharge.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Greater social vulnerability was associated with lower rehabilitation discharge rates after trauma laparotomy, but not with mobility-informed rehabilitation discharge. Incorporating objective mobility assessments into discharge planning may help identify rehabilitation needs while limiting the influence of social factors.

articles.title: Association of Walch glenoid morphology and fracture patterns in proximal humeral fractures.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Proximal humeral fracture (PHF) assessment focuses on fracture pattern, bone quality, and patient factors, whereas glenoid morphology-central to biomechanics in glenohumeral arthritis and instability-is overlooked. We hypothesized that glenoid morphology consistent with Walch type B (posterior decentring) is independently associated with complex, tuberculum-involving PHFs.

**METHODS**: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study analysed 919 patients with a PHF and shoulder computed tomography (CT). Two blinded shoulder-subspecialized orthopedic trauma surgeons independently classified all cases; agreement was quantified with Cohen's κ. Fractures were classified by the Neer and AO/OTA systems and glenoid morphology by the Walch classification. The primary outcome-tuberculum involvement (Neer IV/V)-was analysed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age at trauma, sex, and osteoarthritis.

**RESULTS**: The cohort comprised 919 patients (72.6% female; median age at trauma 69 years). The Walch distribution in this CT-selected cohort was type A 42.7%, B 54.4%, C 2.7%, and D 0.2%; osteoarthritis was present in 59.5%. Walch agreement was moderate (κ = 0.53), with disagreement concentrated at the A1↔B1 decentring boundary (p < 0.001). Walch type B was independently associated with tuberculum involvement (adjusted OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.56-2.74; adjusted RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.17-1.45; both p < 0.001) and with greater AO/OTA fracture complexity (adjusted ordinal OR 1.60, p < 0.001). Female sex was independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.05-1.97, p = 0.023); age and osteoarthritis were not significant.

**CONCLUSION**: In this CT-selected study population, glenoid morphology consistent with Walch type B was independently associated with complex, tuberculum-involving proximal humeral fractures. The association was statistically robust but clinically modest (AUC 0.62), and Walch type B morphology represented one of several correlates of fracture pattern rather than a standalone predictor. Glenoid morphology may therefore be worth recording during CT and fracture-pattern assessment; these hypothesis-generating findings are not sufficient to modify current treatment algorithms, but support the inclusion of glenoid parameters in future risk models and prospective studies.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level III retrospective cohort study prognostic study.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Suprascapular Nerve Block Versus Intravenous Fentanyl for Analgesia in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department With Traumatic Scapular Fractures.
articles.abstract:
**STUDY OBJECTIVE**: To compare the analgesic efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block with intravenous fentanyl in patients with traumatic scapular fractures.

**METHODS**: We conducted an open-label randomized controlled pilot trial in the emergency department (ED) of a Level I trauma center in North India. Adults with traumatic scapular fractures and Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale scores of 7 and higher, were randomly assigned to ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block or intravenous fentanyl (1 μg/kg). Pain scores were assessed at baseline and 30, 60, 120, 240, and 360 minutes. Secondary outcomes included rescue analgesia and adverse events.

**RESULTS**: Sixty patients were randomly assigned to the 2 groups. Median baseline pain score was 10 in both groups. Pain scores were consistently lower with suprascapular nerve block, with median scores of 3 (interquartile [IQR] 2 to 5) versus 7 (IQR 6 to 8) at 30 minutes. Between-group differences were 4 (95% confidence interval [CI], 3 to 4) at 30 and 60 minutes, 2 (95% CI, 2 to 2) at 120 and 240 minutes, and 1 (95% CI, 1 to 2) at 360 minutes. Rescue analgesia was less frequent with suprascapular nerve block (13% versus 79%; risk difference, -66% [95% CI, 47.5 to 85.2]). Drowsiness was more common with fentanyl (12 versus 2 participants); hypotension occurred in 1 fentanyl recipient and paresthesia in 1 suprascapular nerve block recipient.

**CONCLUSION**: In this pilot randomized trial, ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block provided greater and sustained pain relief, reduced rescue analgesia, and fewer systemic adverse effects than intravenous fentanyl in adults with traumatic scapular fractures. Larger multicenter trials are needed to confirm these findings and evaluate cumulative opioid use and longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Trauma undertriage at a University Hospital in North Norway: the need to look beyond mechanism of injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Early multidisciplinary management through trauma team activation (TTA) improves outcomes for severely injured patients. Previous studies at the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) Tromsø conducted in 2006 and 2013, using Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥ 16 as reference, found high rates of undertriage at 32% and 28% respectively. The aim of this study was to assess the current undertriage at UNN Tromsø using both ISS ≥ 16 and the New Injury Severity Score (NISS) ≥ 16 as reference.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively reviewed trauma patients admitted to UNN Tromsø in 2018 and 2023. The study included all patients met with TTA as well as all severely injured patients that did not receive TTA during the period. Data were obtained from the local trauma registry and electronic medical records. Undertriage was defined as patients with ISS ≥ 16 and no TTA, and NISS ≥ 16 and no TTA.

**RESULTS**: A total of 527 trauma patients were included. Undertriage based on ISS was 15% overall for 2018 and 2023. When NISS ≥ 16 was applied, the undertriage increased to 18% (31/171). A total of 63% of undertriaged patients fulfilled one or more national TTA criteria but was not admitted with TTA. Low-energy falls were the predominant mechanism of injury (73%) among undertriaged patients. A total of 70% of undertriaged patients had single region injuries, and 40% had organ failure.

**CONCLUSIONS**: The undertriage rate at UNN Tromsø was 15% in 2018 and 2023, still exceeding the recommended level of < 5% according to American College of Surgeons-Committee on Trauma. Undertriage appears largely related to the system's non-compliance with trauma criteria, and injuries sustained in low-energy trauma mechanisms. Use of NISS identifies a larger group of potentially undertriaged patients, including more patients with organ failure who may benefit from TTA.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med

articles.title: Is it necessary to distally lock all pertrochanteric cephalo-medullary fixation in the geriatric population?
Cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered prehospital thrombolysis for ST elevation myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Guidelines recommend prehospital thrombolysis for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) if trained clinicians can interpret 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) on site. The Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) has a well-established prehospital reperfusion program under which all paramedics are trained in prehospital STEMI diagnosis on 12-lead ECG and administering thrombolysis in the field to eligible patients. Whilst the clinical benefits of this treatment are proven, its cost-effectiveness remains to be established.

**METHODS**: We developed a decision-analytic microsimulation model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered thrombolysis for prehospital STEMI in the state of Queensland, Australia. The comparator was a hypothetical counterfactual group of patients who were clinically eligible for prehospital thrombolysis but received an alternate treatment pathway. The analysis was conducted from a health provider (Queensland Government) perspective. A lifetime time horizon was used. Input values of the acute phase were derived from our prehospital and linked hospital database of all STEMI patients receiving prehospital thrombolysis from QAS paramedics between January 2022 and December 2024. Input values of the long-term phase were obtained from published literature. Cost was expressed in Australian dollars (AUD) and United States dollars (USD) in 2026 value, and effectiveness in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs).

**RESULTS**: Prehospital thrombolysis improved outcomes at a cost of AUD 16,750.22 per QALY gained (95% uncertainty range AUD 15,477.48 - 18,422.84) or USD 11,725.15 (USD 10,834.24 - 12,895.99). In the sensitivity analysis, the cost-effectiveness of prehospital thrombolysis was robust to changes in input values.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Paramedic-administered thrombolysis in the field for prehospital STEMI, compared with no such treatment, represents value for money.

articles.title: A Lighter Approach to Language Access: Virtual Interpreter Utilization in Emergency Medical Services (EMS).
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) may create communication barriers during prehospital care. Although on-demand interpreter services are often available to emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, utilization may be limited by device accessibility, workflow barriers, and clinician adoption. Our objective was to evaluate whether implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with increased utilization of virtual interpreter services during prehospital care.

**METHODS**: We conducted an observational retrospective pre-post cohort study of virtual interpreter service utilization within a large multistate Midwest EMS agency. On June 1, 2025, the agency issued smartphones (Apple iPhone 16, ∼6 ounces) to all clinicians, providing continuous access to virtual audio and video interpreter services (LanguageLine Solutions). Previously, interpreter services were accessed using large Toughbook laptops (∼6.1 pounds). Interpreter utilization was compared between pre-implementation (October 30, 2024, to May 31, 2025) and post-implementation (June 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025) periods. Interpreter requests per 100 encounters were compared using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

**RESULTS**: Interpreter requests increased from 104 pre-implementation (0.19 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.15-0.23) to 326 post-implementation (0.57 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.51-0.63; RR= 3.04, 95% CI: 2.44-3.79; p < 0.001). Audio requests increased from 68 calls (0.12 per 100 encounters) to 271 calls (0.47 per 100 encounters; RR = 3.86, 95% CI: 2.96-5.03; p < 0.001). Video requests increased from 36 calls (0.06 per 100 encounters) to 55 calls (0.10 per 100 encounters), although the observed increase did not reach statistical significance (RR= 1.48, 95% CI: 0.97-2.25; p = 0.066). The most commonly requested languages were Spanish (n = 153, 36%), Somali (n = 146, 34%), and Arabic (n = 41, 10%).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with a threefold increase in virtual interpreter utilization. This increase was driven primarily by audio interpretation, while the observed increase in video utilization did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that improving point-of-care accessibility of interpreter services through lightweight mobile devices may facilitate greater utilization during prehospital encounters with patients with LEP.

articles.title: Research on the morphology and injury mechanism of pilon fractures.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Understanding the relationship between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures is essential for optimizing preoperative planning and surgical outcomes. To investigate the associations between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures and to provide a theoretical basis for precision diagnosis and treatment.

**METHODS**: This retrospective study included 192 patients with high-energy Pilon fractures treated at Lianyungang Second People's Hospital between January 2010 and December 2024. Using a standardized "trauma history-first plus imaging cross-validation" protocol, patients were categorized into 5 groups: dorsiflexion, varus, valgus, plantarflexion, and neutral. Two senior orthopedic surgeons (≥ 10 years of experience) independently and blindly assessed anteroposterior and lateral tibiofibular radiographs, CT scans, and three-dimensional reconstructions. Evaluated parameters included fibular fracture level and type, tibial fragment distribution, fracture angle, and Topliss classification. Interobserver reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Group comparisons were performed using the chi-square (χ²) test or Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was defined as P < 0.05.

**RESULTS**: Among the 192 patients, 154 (80.2%) were male and 38 (19.8%) were female. The mean (SD) age was 43.38 (12.56) years (range, 14-71 years). Interobserver agreement was substantial for injury mechanism classification (κ = 0.82; 95% CI, 0.75-0.89) and core morphological assessments (κ = 0.87; 95% CI, 0.81-0.93). Fracture morphology differed significantly among mechanism groups (P < 0.05). Dorsiflexion injuries were characterized by the "medial + anterolateral + Die-punch" fragment pattern (45.0%; 95% CI, 23.1%-66.9%), fracture angles > 90° (65.0%), and coronal Y-shaped fractures (25.0%). Varus injuries predominantly showed the "anterolateral + posterolateral + medial + Die-punch" pattern (32.5%) and simple sagittal split fractures (40.0%). Valgus injuries were associated with comminuted fibular fractures (64.3%) and coronal V/Y-shaped tibial fractures (35.7%). Plantarflexion injuries typically involved posterolateral fragments (61.5%) and fracture angles > 90° (80.8%). Neutral injuries were characterized by complex multifragmentary comminuted fractures with Die-punch collapse (33.7%).

**CONCLUSION**: There is a significant and reproducible association between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures. This mechanism-based morphological characterization may provide an objective reference for preoperative assessment and individualized surgical planning. The clinical utility and prognostic value of this classification framework still need to be verified in further prospective studies with clinical outcome endpoints.

articles.title: Critically ill trauma in Portugal: a multicenter intensive care cohort study of frailty, organ dysfunction, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Multicenter data on critically ill trauma patients admitted to Portuguese intensive care units (ICUs) are lacking. We aimed to characterize their epidemiology, injury profile, organ dysfunction trajectories and outcomes, and to evaluate the prognostic performance of severity and frailty measures.

**METHODS**: Multicenter retrospective cohort study within the National Intensive Care Registry (RNMI) of adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to an ICU as a direct consequence of trauma (1 October-31 December 2024) in 32 of 50 voluntarily participating Portuguese ICUs; not nationally representative. SAPS II, ISS, TRISS, the Clinical Frailty Scale, daily SOFA scores, organ support, quality of life and mortality were collected. Prognostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis, multivariable logistic regression, calibration, and mixed-effects modelling of serial SOFA.

**RESULTS**: 457 patients were included; median age 61 years (IQR 45-74), 72.0% male. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (46.9%). Traumatic brain injury (32.9%) and thoracic trauma (21.4%) predominated. Observed ICU and hospital mortality were 11.0% and 15.3%, respectively. SOFA scores were consistently higher in non-survivors from day one. SAPS II showed the highest discrimination for hospital mortality (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.825-0.924), followed by TRISS (0.758) and the Clinical Frailty Scale (0.702). SAPS II, day-1 SOFA, and frailty were independently associated with hospital mortality. SAPS II over-predicted mortality (observed/expected 0.64), whereas TRISS showed a non-significant tendency to under-predict it (1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.72).

**CONCLUSIONS**: In this multicenter cohort from 32 voluntarily participating ICUs, patients were older, with frequent falls, neurotrauma and thoracic injury, and moderate mortality. Organ dysfunction trajectories and frailty were associated with hospital mortality, but incremental predictive value was not assessed; both merit inclusion in future trauma registry frameworks.

articles.title: Influence of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics on aseptic bone flap resorption: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Aseptic bone flap resorption (ABFR) remains a common complication after autologous cranioplasty following decompressive craniectomy (DC), with reported prevalences varying widely-often reported between 10% and 30%-likely due to inconsistent follow-up. Data on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in pathogenesis of ABFR are scarce. Aim of the present study was therefore to identify potential risk factors, with a particular focus on CSF drainage procedures.

**METHODS**: In this retrospective single-center study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent DC followed by autologous cranioplasty from 2015 to 2022. We collected demographics, clinical details, perioperative variables, and CSF interventions. Univariate and multivariate analyses identified associations, with subgroup focus on patients completing structured follow-up.

**RESULTS**: ABFR was diagnosed in 39/259 patients (15.1%), resulting in 38/101 (37.6%) in the 6-months follow-up cohort. Changes in CSF dynamics such as preoperative lumbar CSF drainage (p = 0.035) were identified as a risk factor, whereas ventriculoperitoneal shunt pressure adjustment was not associated with an increased risk of ABFR. After differentiation of the direction of adjustment, pressure reduction was not associated with ABFR. Especially preoperative lumbar CSF drainage remains an independent risk factor (p = 0.023) in multivariate analysis.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Without structured imaging follow-up, ABFR rates are likely underestimated. CSF dynamic alterations beyond shunt presence alone may represent a relevant risk factor for ABFR. Our findings emphasize that primary alloplastic cranioplasty could be considered in at least a subgroup of patients.

articles.title: Trauma-associated cardiac arrest - insights and results from a German rescue helicopter station.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: In comparison with cardiac arrest attributable to other causes, trauma-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest has low survival rates, but survivors often show good neurological recovery. This study aimed to provide a deeper understanding of trauma-associated cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in terms of trauma mechanisms, injury patterns, CPR measures, and outcomes.

**METHODS**: In this retrospective single-center study, emergency physician reports on trauma-associated CPRs performed by the Christoph 22 helicopter emergency medical service (HEMS) from 2013 to 2023 at the study site in Ulm were analyzed using the chi-square test and binary logistic regression.

**RESULTS**: In total, 126 cases of prehospital trauma-associated CPR at the Ulm HEMS site were included. Four patients (3.2%) survived, with all four showing good neurological recovery. The most common cause of trauma was motorcycle accident. The patients most frequently presented with traumatic brain injury (TBI) (69.6%) and/or chest injuries (79.2%). Chest decompression was performed in 93.9% of the patients with chest injuries. TBI was the only injury to show a (negative) association with 30-day survival (1.1% vs. 7.9%; p = 0.049), this observation was independent of whether the TBI was isolated or occurred in combination with pelvic, abdominal, and/or chest injuries.

**CONCLUSION**: In this study on trauma-associated CPR, the survival rate remained low, but the neurological recovery of survivors was often good. TBI, both isolated and in combination with chest, abdomen, and/or pelvic injuries, seemed to be a prognostically unfavorable factor. However, with only four long-term survivors, it is hardly possible to draw reliable conclusions.

articles.title: Carboxypeptidase B1: A novel, targetable contributor to thromboembolic complications in severe acute pancreatitis?
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with increased thrombotic risk. Systemic release of pancreatic proteases in SAP may alter susceptibility to endogenous fibrinolysis, but this remains unexplored. Pancreatic carboxypeptidase B1 (CPB1) is a protease activated by trypsin that shares cleavage specificity with thrombin-activatable fibrinolysis inhibitor, which cleaves C-terminal lysine residues off fibrin, impairing co-localization of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and plasminogen and rendering clots resistant to fibrinolysis. We hypothesized that circulating CPB1 would be elevated in SAP patients and contribute to fibrinolytic resistance.

**METHODS**: Plasma and clinical data were prospectively collected from SAP patients (n=15), matched critically ill controls without pancreatitis (n=13), and healthy controls (n=4) with IRB approval and informed consent. CPB1 levels were measured through ELISA. Clot lysis assays assessed fibrinolysis in response to tPA. Healthy control plasma was tested with and without porcine pancreas CPB1 to assess the effect of CPB1 on fibrinolysis. Transition midpoints (TM's) were defined as the time to 50% clot lysis. Clinical data were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher exact tests. Assay results were analyzed using Kruskall-Wallis test. Significance was set at P<0.05.

**RESULTS**: Demographics were similar between groups. SAP patients had markedly elevated CPB1 levels (154.0 [58.4-388.0] ng/mL) compared with sick (7.0 [4.1-15.6] ng/mL, P<0.0001) and healthy controls (4.0 [2.1-4.4], P<0.001). Healthy control plasma supplemented with porcine pancreas CPB1 demonstrated complete disruption of fibrinolysis compared with healthy plasma without CPB1. SAP patients had the highest resistance to tPA-induced fibrinolysis, with significantly higher baseline TMs than critically ill controls (42.0 [21.7-126.6] vs. 22.8 [18.3-33.7], P=0.04).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Patients with SAP have uniquely elevated circulating levels of CPB1, which may contribute to thromboembolism in SAP through fibrinolytic resistance. Further investigation into targeted CPB1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in SAP is warranted to potentially reduce development of organ failure and mortality.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: N/A (Basic Science).

articles.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology.
articles.abstract:
**IMPORTANCE**: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear.

**OBJECTIVE**: To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies.

**DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS**: This case-control study included 4 biorepositories based in the US that contributed CSF and plasma samples from participants with and without tauopathies, many of whom had antemortem biofluid samples paired with autopsy or genetically defined neuropathology. Samples were analyzed between August 2023 and December 2025. Data analysis occurred from August 2024 to July 2026.

**EXPOSURE**: CSF and plasma eMTBR-tau243 concentrations measured using a mass spectrometry-based assay.

**MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES**: Outcomes included mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (eg, AD and CTE) based on autopsy, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with MAPT variants (FTLD-MAPT), and CTE stage. Differences in biomarker levels between groups were evaluated using analysis of variance or analysis of covariance, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the discriminative performance of fluid eMTBR-tau243.

**RESULTS**: Among the 229 participants (196 with CSF samples and 55 with plasma samples [22 with both]), mean (SD) age at fluid sample collection was 63 (13) years and 108 (47%) were female. Median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 10 patients with AD (0.459 [0.246-0.801] fmol/mL) compared with 29 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.002 [0.001-0.005] fmol/mL) (adjusted P < .001), but other autopsy-confirmed non-AD tauopathies (which included 52 individuals with conditions including progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration) did not demonstrate an increase (0.015 [0.008, 0.039] fmol/mL). Six symptomatic FTLD-MAPT variant carriers with mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (R406W, V337M, and G389R) had increased median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 (0.140 [0.055-0.174] fmol/mL) compared with 15 4R tauopathy variant carriers including N279K and P301L (0.004 [0.001-0.044] fmol/mL) (P = .001). Median (IQR) plasma eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 11 patients with CTE (1.93 [0.42-3.68] fmol/L) compared with 20 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.29 [0.05-0.62] fmol/L) (adjusted P = .007), but did not increase as high as among 14 patients with AD (11.25 [2.29-19.38] fmol/L). Plasma eMTBR-tau243 distinguished CTE stage III and IV from controls (AUC, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.92-1.00), but not CTE stage I from controls (AUC, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97).

**CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE**: This study found that plasma and CSF eMTBR-tau243 were increased in mixed 3R/4R tauopathies including AD, high-stage CTE, and a subset of genetic FTLD-MAPT, compared with cognitively unimpaired controls. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine the clinical utility of eMTBR-tau243 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for CTE and other tauopathies beyond AD.

articles.title: Impact of antibiotic prophylaxis on the occurrence of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia in trauma patients (antiVAP): a propensity score-weighted, retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Short-course antibiotic prophylaxis has been associated with a reduced risk of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in selected populations, particularly patients with acute brain injury. However, its role in severely injured trauma patients remains controversial.

**METHODS**: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study, conducted in 15 French trauma centres, included severely injured adults who required mechanical ventilation initiated within 24 h of admission and continued for at least 48 h. Propensity score-based analyses assessed the association between early antibiotic prophylaxis (initiated within the first 24 h of management and continued for up to 72 h) and patient outcomes. The primary outcome was early-onset VAP; secondary outcomes included late-onset VAP, extrapulmonary infections, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, and 30-day mortality.

**RESULTS**: A total of 1,321 trauma patients were included. Antibiotic prophylaxis was administered to 746 patients (56%), with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid used in more than 90% of cases. Early-onset VAP occurred in 240 of 746 patients (32%) who received antibiotic prophylaxis and in 195 of 575 (34%) who did not. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with early-onset VAP (weighted odds ratio [wOR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.22; p = 0.48). A cause-specific Cox model accounting for the competing risk of death before day 7 yielded similar results (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.71-1.07; p = 0.19). Antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with improve of secondary outcomes.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis in severely injured trauma patients was not associated with a reduced risk of early-onset VAP.

**CLINICALTRIALS**: Gov ID NCT07059039 - Registration date: July, 10th 2025.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury and renal replacement therapy: a critical synthesis of metabolic derangements and nutritional implications.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects up to 50% of critically ill patients and is frequently complicated by severe metabolic derangements, requiring the initiation of replacement therapy (RRT) in 10-15% of cases. Despite substantial progress in the diagnosis of AKI and optimisation of RRT delivery, the nutritional management of these patients remains an underexplored area.

**MAIN BODY**: AKI is increasingly recognised as a systemic metabolic disorder extending beyond impaired renal clearance. Key metabolic alterations include mitochondrial dysfunction, dysregulated gluconeogenesis, increased proteolysis and altered amino acid metabolism, with accelerated nitrogen wasting. These abnormalities are further amplified by acute systemic stress states, including sepsis, systemic inflammation, trauma, burns, liver dysfunction and multiorgan failure. RRT introduces additional metabolic consequences through extracorporeal losses of amino acids and micronutrients. Conversely, citrate anticoagulation, glucose-containing dialysate, and lactate-buffered solutions represent sources of clinically relevant calories. Current nutritional recommendations are largely extrapolated from heterogeneous intensive care populations. Available evidence suggests that AKI primarily influences energy balance rather than energy expenditure, which appears broadly comparable to that of other critically ill populations. While evidence specific to AKI is limited, protein provision of approximately 1.2-1.3 g/kg/day is generally recommended during critical illness. However, higher intakes of up to 1.7-2.5 g/kg/day may be considered in patients receiving RRT to offset extracorporeal amino acid losses and increased protein catabolism. In this setting, emerging concepts such as metabolic tolerance and biomarker-guided metabolic phenotyping may facilitate individualised nutritional strategies.

**CONCLUSIONS**: AKI, particularly when requiring RRT, is associated with profound and dynamic metabolic disturbances that substantially influence energy and protein requirements, thereby making nutrition an integral component of organ support therapies. Future research should evaluate precision nutrition strategies that tailor nutritional support to the phase of critical illness, measured energy expenditure, metabolic tolerance, and RRT-related nutrient losses and gains. Such studies should prioritise patient-centred outcomes, including physical function and recovery, in addition to nutritional and metabolic endpoints.

articles.title: Task-specific gait biomechanics following unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Patients treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury may experience residual functional limitations. It remains unclear how these limitations manifest during tasks with different biomechanical demands. This exploratory study compared task-specific gait biomechanics between patients after fixation and healthy controls.

**METHODS**: In this prospective cross-sectional observational study, 11 patients after unilateral iliosacral screw fixation (mean age 68.73 ± 9.89 years; 10 women) were compared with 21 healthy controls (52.48 ± 20.36 years; 11 women). Participants performed level walking, stair climbing, and step crossing using an Xsens MVN inertial motion capture system. Pelvic kinematics and model-estimated muscle activation and joint contact forces were evaluated using Computed MyoGraphy. Repeated trials were analyzed using participant-level random-intercept mixed models adjusted for age and sex. Pelvic rotation during stair climbing was the primary outcome; other outcomes were secondary or exploratory.

**RESULTS**: Pelvic rotation during stair climbing was lower in patients (adjusted difference -5.45°, 95% CI -7.98 to -2.92°; within-family FDR-adjusted q = 0.0003). Contralateral pelvic tilt during step crossing was greater (adjusted difference 1.44°, 95% CI 0.46-2.41°; q = 0.011). No statistically significant group differences were detected in the analyzed level-walking parameters, thoracic counter-rotation, lower-limb muscle activation, or hip joint contact-force asymmetry. Model-estimated peak L5-S1 joint contact force during stair climbing was lower in patients (adjusted difference -0.70 × body weight; q = 0.001).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Patients after posterior pelvic ring injury treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation showed task-specific differences in pelvic movement during demanding locomotor activities. The findings support including stair and step tasks in functional assessment, but do not establish that fixation caused the observed differences. Small sample size, demographic imbalance, and the absence of patient-reported outcomes limit clinical interpretation.

articles.title: Whole blood transfusion in adult patients with traumatic brain injury: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Whole blood (WB) transfusion may improve outcomes in trauma patients compared with component therapy, but evidence in traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains limited. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of WB transfusion in adults with TBI requiring transfusion.

**METHODS**: We searched PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ICTRP for studies published from January 2006 through August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized trials and observational studies using propensity score matching or inverse probability of treatment weighting. Random-effects meta-analysis with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was performed for mortality. Component-specific transfusion requirements were summarized qualitatively.

**RESULTS**: Five studies were included in the systematic review, and four studies were included in the mortality meta-analysis. WB transfusion was not clearly associated with lower mortality (RR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.62-1.16; P = 0.19; I

**CONCLUSIONS**: Current evidence is insufficient to determine whether WB transfusion reduces mortality after TBI because of the limited number of studies, clinical and methodological heterogeneity, risk of bias, and imprecision. Further randomized trials in clearly defined TBI populations are needed.

articles.title: Effect of airway assistant training on intubation time during simulated prehospital airway management: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Challenging airways are common in the out-of-hospital setting, where delays or failure to secure the airway can result in significant morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this pilot study aimed to determine whether training paramedics in the role of airway assistant improves intubation time during a simulated regurgitating airway using suction-assisted laryngoscopy and airway decontamination (SALAD).

**METHODS**: Twelve qualified paramedics were randomly allocated to one of two groups (n = 6) and paired with intensive care paramedics (ICPs). Airway assistants in Group 1 completed a one-hour airway assistant training program, whereas airway assistants in Group 2 received no training. Participants completed a standardized, timed simulation using a continuously regurgitating mannequin designed to replicate the challenges of out-of-hospital intubation. The primary outcome was time to successful intubation, defined as passage of the endotracheal tube through the vocal cords with cuff inflation.

**RESULTS**: Airway assistant training significantly reduced intubation time. The untrained group recorded a median intubation time of 102.5 seconds (IQR 36), compared with 53 seconds (IQR 19) in the trained group. Group comparisons demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in intubation time (

**CONCLUSIONS**: In this pilot study, training paramedics to perform the airway assistant role significantly reduced intubation time in a simulated regurgitating airway. These preliminary findings suggest that incorporating structured airway assistant training into prehospital education programs may improve airway management performance in challenging environments. Given the small sample size and simulated setting, larger studies are required to confirm these findings and determine whether the observed benefits translate to clinical practice.

articles.title: Intraoperative visualization with 3D fluoroscopy for posterior pelvic fixation is associated with lower cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Achieving optimal screw positioning in posterior pelvic ring (PR) fracture fixation is critical for fracture stability and safety. Formerly, our institution used intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy followed by postoperative computed tomography (CT) to assess fracture reduction and screw placement. Introduction of the 3D mobile C-arm enables immediate volumetric intraoperative assessment, may improve intraoperative visualization, and may alter conventional imaging requirements. This study compared cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure between cases performed with intraoperative 3D fluoroscopy (3DF) against standard intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy (2DF), including postoperative CT utilization.

**METHODS**: A retrospective review was conducted on patients treated for posterior PR fractures at a level 1 trauma center between 2014 and 2023. Utilization of 3DF or plain-film fluoroscopy, and any intraoperative screw changes were documented. Rates and details of postoperative complications and subsequent reoperations were recorded for patients with > 3 months follow-up. Radiation doses for 3DF, 2DF, and postoperative CT were extracted from radiology reports.

**RESULTS**: Among 245 patients (mean age 47.2, 52.2% male) undergoing fixation for posterior PR fractures, 89 (36.3%) had 3DF intraoperatively, while 156 (63.7%) had 2DF. 27 patients (8 3DF, 19 2DF, p = 0.443) had screws changed intraoperatively, primarily to modify screw path (n = 16, 59.3%), to achieve better purchase/reduction (n = 5, 18.5%), to modify screw size (n = 3, 11.1%), to change screw type (n = 2, 7.4%), and failure to advance screw (n = 1, 3.7%). Mean radiation dose for the 3DF group was significantly lower (179.2 mGy vs 526.1 mGy, p < 0.001). When excluding postoperative CT dose (n = 194), intraoperative-only radiation remained lower with 3DF (median 79.1 (IQR 51.5-148.7) vs 318.0 (IQR 71.6-751.5) mGy; p < 0.001). Among 119 patients with > 3 months follow-up, reoperation was less frequent with 3DF (9.5% vs 31.2%, p = 0.012), predominantly for symptomatic implant removal.

**DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION**: Intraoperative 3DF was associated with lower cumulative radiation exposure compared to traditional fluoroscopy with routine postoperative CT, and intraoperative dose alone was also lower. Reoperation was less frequent in the 3DF group, but most reoperations were implant removals for symptomatic or planned indications. These findings highlight the potential of 3DF as a practical radiation efficient quality assurance tool in posterior pelvic fixation.

articles.title: Effect modification by arterial pH on the association between extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation and neurological outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with shockable rhythm: A multicenter registry study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Arterial pH on emergency department (ED) arrival predicts outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but its effect on the association between extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) and neurological outcomes is unclear. We evaluated this association in patients with an initial shockable rhythm and assessed whether pH modified it.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively analyzed the Korean Cardiac Arrest Research Consortium registry. Adults with presumed cardiac-origin OHCA, an initial shockable rhythm, ED cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and arterial blood gas data measured after ED arrival were included. Exposure was ECPR initiated in the ED; the primary outcome was favorable neurological outcome at discharge (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2). Arterial pH was categorized as low (≤6.85), medium (>6.85 and <7.05), or high (≥7.05). Multivariable logistic regression assessed ECPR-by-pH interaction, with optimal 1:2 propensity score matching as a sensitivity analysis.

**RESULTS**: Of 2183 patients, 213 (9.8%) received ECPR and 154 (7.1%) had a favorable neurological outcome. The association between ECPR and favorable outcome differed across pH categories (p for interaction = 0.004): adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 7.34 (95% confidence interval [CI], 2.84-18.98) in the low-pH group, 2.07 (95% CI, 1.06-4.03) in the medium-pH group, and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.37-1.94) in the high-pH group. The propensity score-matched analysis showed a similar pattern (p for interaction = 0.036).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Initial arterial pH modified the association between ECPR and neurological outcome after OHCA with an initial shockable rhythm. The association was strongest at low pH and not observed at high pH. Arterial pH may inform ECPR evaluation but should not determine treatment thresholds.

articles.title: Defining organized cardiac motion and cardiac standstill in cardiac arrest using point of care ultrasound: A Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
**AIM**: There are no widely accepted definitions of organized cardiac motion (OCM) and cardiac standstill (CS) using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) during cardiac arrest. We aimed to define these terms and provide guidance on the clinical application of these findings.

**METHODS**: Statements defining OCM and CS were developed by a steering committee of experts after a comprehensive literature review aided by a librarian. A diverse panel of 20 experts was convened. Using Delphi methodology, the panel came to a consensus on definitions of OCM and CS after three rounds of voting.

**RESULTS**: The panelists voted on 64 total statements pertaining to OCM and CS in cardiac arrest: 29 defining OCM, 23 defining cardiac standstill, and 12 examining clinical implications of OCM and CS. We defined OCM as coordinated contraction with change in left ventricular chamber size. Coordinated contraction with any change of the right ventricle may also be used if visualization of the left ventricle was not possible. Ventricular fibrillation, agonal motion, and isolated valvular movement were deemed not consistent with OCM. Cardiac standstill was defined as including the absence of all cardiac motion or the presence of isolated valvular movement alone. The panel recommended that POCUS can guide cardiac arrest resuscitation, and that these definitions are applicable to pediatric patients and the prehospital setting.

**CONCLUSION**: The expert panelists established consensus definitions of OCM and CS during cardiac arrest. These definitions can guide further research into POCUS use during cardiac arrest and aid ongoing efforts to standardize its use.

articles.title: Prehospital Advanced Airway Management in Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Cohort Study Using Time-Dependent Propensity Score Sequential Matching.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (TCA) has extremely poor outcomes, and the benefit of prehospital advanced airway management (AAM) remains uncertain, partly because previous observational studies may have been affected by resuscitation time bias. We examined the association between prehospital AAM and clinical outcomes in adults with TCA using a time-dependent analytic approach.

**METHODS**: We conducted a nationwide retrospective observational cohort study using the All-Japan Utstein Registry linked with emergency medical services transport records from 2021 to 2023. Adults (≥18 years) with TCA were included. The exposure was successful prehospital AAM, including supraglottic airway placement or endotracheal intubation. The primary outcome was 30-day survival, and the secondary outcome was favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2) at 30 days. We applied time-dependent propensity score sequential matching and estimated corrected risk differences (RDs) using generalized estimating equations with inverse-frequency weighting.

**RESULTS**: Among 7,217 patients, 2,653 (36.8%) received prehospital AAM, of whom 2,637 were successfully matched within the analytic cohort. Thirty-day survival was 1.8% in the AAM group and 1.4% among matched controls (corrected RD, 0.6%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -0.1 to 1.2). Favorable neurological outcome occurred in 0.2% and 0.4%, respectively (corrected RD, -0.2%; 95% CI, -0.6 to 0.1). No significant timing-dependent association or prespecified subgroup heterogeneity was observed.

**CONCLUSIONS**: In this nationwide cohort study using time-dependent propensity score sequential matching, prehospital AAM was not significantly associated with improved outcomes in adults with TCA.

articles.title: Resuscitation using fresh-frozen plasma is associated with improved contextual fear memory in a non-TBI mouse model of trauma and hemorrhagic shock.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Cognitive dysfunction is a consequence of traumatic injury with lasting impacts. Even without direct brain injury, trauma and hemorrhagic shock (T/HS) can cause malperfusion, inflammation, and neuronal injury. Disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx (eGC), a key regulator of vascular homeostasis, contributes to trauma-induced endotheliopathy and may influence secondary neurologic injury. Prior work demonstrated that fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) resuscitation preserves eGC expression and reduces maladaptive vascular repair in a murine T/HS model. This study evaluates post-injury cognition and FFP protection against cognitive impairment compared with lactated Ringer's (LR).

**METHODS**: Male C57BL/6 mice were randomized to sham procedure or T/HS followed by a volume-driven LR or pressure-directed FFP resuscitation approach. T/HS mice underwent laparotomy, femoral artery cannulation, hemorrhagic shock, pseudofractures via bone homogenate injection, and hindlimb muscle crush injuries. Sham mice received laparotomy and femoral artery cutdown. Four days postsurgery, open field testing assessed locomotion, followed by fear conditioning on days 7 to 8 to assess cognition. Brains were collected to analyze hippocampal glycosaminoglycans hyaluronan, heparan sulfate (HS), and chondroitin sulfate (CS).

**RESULTS**: Open field testing showed intact locomotion at post-injury day 4 in all groups. On day 8, mice resuscitated with FFP had significantly greater contextual freezing compared with mice resuscitated with LR, consistent with improved hippocampal-dependent contextual memory. Cued fear conditioning did not differ between groups. LR and FFP resuscitation strategies resulted in distinct hippocampal hyaluronan and HS staining patterns, without synthesis gene expression differences. T/HS+LR brains showed increased 4-O-sulfated CS (CS-4S), a neurologically detrimental sulfation pattern, whereas FFP decreased CS-4S and increased CS-6S.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Goal-directed plasma resuscitation is associated with improved spatial memory and distinct eGC structural remodeling compared with volume-driven crystalloid resuscitation following T/HS. These findings highlight the potential for resuscitation strategy after hemorrhagic shock to influence neurological recovery, even in the absence of direct brain injury.

articles.title: Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Review.
articles.abstract:
**IMPORTANCE**: Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US.

**OBSERVATIONS**: Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours-and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy-based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence.

**CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE**: Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

articles.title: Traumatic renal injuries: the prevalence, management and outcome of renal vascular injury.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: To assess the prevalence, management and outcome of renal vascular injuries (RVIs; active bleeding and contained vascular injuries) seen on admission CT. Also, we wanted to find out the prevalence and survival of patients with concomitant injury to liver, spleen, and kidney seen on admission CT.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, longitudinal cohort study with nine-year data (2013-2021) of all ≥ 15-year-old patients with renal injury identified in a trauma registry. Admission CT and angiographic examinations were reviewed to assess RVIs, including active bleeding, arterial dissection, segmental infarct, pseudoaneurysm or AV-fistulae. Medical records were reviewed for treatment, hospital length of stay and 30-day survival rate.

**RESULTS**: Out of 2805 patients with abdominal trauma, 243 (8.7%) had a renal injury, of whom 182 (74.9%) underwent CT on admission. RVI was found in 56 patients (30.8%). Among these 56 patients, 42 (75%) had active bleeding, eight (14.3%) segmental infarct, six (10.7%) pseudoaneurysm, and three (5.4%) arterial dissection. Of these, ten patients (17.9%) underwent angioembolization, and three (5.4%) underwent laparotomy. Patients with RVI were slightly older than those without RVI (43.6 vs. 37.8 years, p = 0.0409) and had more often a penetrating trauma (OR 2.836; 95% CI 1.127-7.136, p = 0.0416). Hospital length of stay (14.7 vs. 14.9 days, p = 0.9520) and 30-day survival (95.2% vs. 92.6%, p = 0.3165) did not differ significantly between patients without and with RVI. Among patients with available CT, fourteen (14/182; 7.7%) had concomitant injuries to the liver, spleen and kidney, with no statistically significant difference in 30-day survival compared with patients without such concomitant injuries (92.9% vs. 94.6%; p = 0.5237).

**CONCLUSION**: RVI was not uncommon in our study cohort, occurring in 30.8% of patients with renal injury who underwent CT on admission. Of these, 17.9% were treated with angioembolization. Patients with RVI were slightly older and were more likely to have a penetrating injury than patients without RVI. No statistically significant difference in hospital length of stay or 30-day survival was found between patients without and with RVI.

articles.title: The Impact of Hospital Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Volume and Its Distribution Across ICUs on Adult Patients' Outcomes: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Research from a prior era of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) found that higher hospital ECMO volume was associated with higher survival rates, but it did not examine whether distributing ECMO volume across multiple ICUs affected this relationship.

**DESIGN**: Retrospective analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry.

**SETTING**: ECMO centers contributing to the registry.

**PATIENTS**: Adult patients required ECMO support from 2012 to 2023.

**INTERVENTIONS**: None.

**MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS**: We analyzed adult patients from the ELSO registry (2012-2023), adjusting for hospital factors and case mix using multivariable hierarchical logistic regression. The main outcome was in-hospital mortality. Hospital experience was measured by the annual number of adult ECMO cases and total ECMO hours. Volume-outcome associations were modeled for all centers and by total adult ICUs per center. We included 115,849 adults on ECMO across 495 hospitals. Model estimates showed small decreases in mortality odds with higher annual case counts (odds ratio [OR], 0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99 per 10-case increase) and ECMO hours (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr increase). Hospitals with one ICU had a median of 10 cases (interquartile interval [IQI], 3-25 cases), while those with four or more ICUs had a median of 50 (IQI, 28-91). Adjusted mortality was higher in centers delivering ECMO across four+ ICUs compared with one ICU (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.06-1.31), the annual case model (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06-1.26), and the annual ECMO hours model. Higher volume was associated with a reduction in the odds of mortality for hospitals with four+ ICUs compared with those with one ICU (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.96-1.00 per 10 cases and OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Higher hospital ECMO volume is associated with reduced mortality. Hospitals with more adult ICUs that perform ECMO may experience higher mortality, which may be explained by increased patient complexity and is offset by the higher center volume. More research is needed to better understand the optimum design of ECMO centers.

articles.title: Airway management during missions of a neurologist-staffed mobile stroke unit: a retrospective registry study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Following their endorsement by international guidelines, mobile stroke units (MSUs) are increasingly being integrated into emergency medical services worldwide. In real-world use, physician-staffed MSUs can be dispatched beyond their intended indication, exposing on-board neurologists to non-stroke emergencies. This raises important clinical and regulatory questions about the competencies MSU physicians need. Advanced airway management is one of the most critical prehospital interventions. Yet, its frequency, indications, procedural characteristics and success rates have not been investigated in neurologist-staffed MSU services.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively analysed a prospective registry of mission documentation from a neurologist-staffed MSU service in Berlin, Germany from 31 August 2024 to 15 March 2026. Dispatches of the MSU were classified as stroke or non-stroke dispatches using the recorded activation code. The primary outcome was the dispatch-based frequency of endotracheal intubation (ETI), defined as a documented intubation attempt. All ETIs were performed by the on-board neurologist. Secondary outcomes included supraglottic airway (SGA) use, first-pass success rate, procedural characteristics and self-reported post-mission National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) workload. Proportions are reported with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CI).

**RESULTS**: We analysed 3,887 dispatches. ETI occurred in a total of 49 dispatches (1.26%; 95% CI 0.95-1.66) with 2 in 1,755 stroke- (0.11%; 95% CI 0.03-0.41) and 47 in 2,132 non-stroke dispatches (2.20%; 95% CI 1.66-2.92). SGA use occurred in 22 dispatches (0.57%; 95% CI 0.37-0.86). All 49 intubation attempts were successful (100.0%; 95% CI 92.7-100.0). First-pass success was achieved in 43/49 (87.8%; 95% CI 75.8-94.3) with no ETI requiring more than two attempts. Videolaryngoscopy was used in all ETIs and capnographic confirmation of tube position in 48/49 (98%). Non-traumatic cardiac arrest was the most frequent indication (30/49). In the exploratory workload analysis, the median NASA-TLX score was 59.8 [IQR 50.0-68.7] in 49 dispatches with ETI and 27.0 [15.5-41.7] in 2,700 dispatches without ETI.

**CONCLUSIONS**: ETI was infrequent overall and particularly rare during stroke dispatches, yet first-pass success was high. Prospective studies are needed to define airway management requirements and training standards for MSU physicians.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med

articles.title: Implementation of a low-cost trauma intake form with real-time clinical decision support: Mixed-methods findings from a stepped-wedge clinical trial in Ghana.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Most injured patients in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) receive care from non-specialist providers at smaller hospitals lacking trauma experience and standardized protocols. A trauma intake form (TIF) with real-time clinical decision support prompts was developed to address this gap. This study examined key implementation outcomes, including adoption, usability, acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and sustainability.

**METHODS**: This study was conducted at six district and two regional hospitals in Ghana as part of a hybrid effectiveness-implementation stepped-wedge clinical trial. Direct observation of 4077 injured patients over 17.5 months was combined with a structured questionnaire administered to all 241 participating clinicians, alongside thematic analysis of open-ended responses.

**RESULTS**: Overall observed TIF uptake was 85.6%, with five of eight hospitals classified as adopters. Implementation outcomes were consistently positive across qualitative and quantitative measures, with high levels of acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability reported across both adopting and non-adopting facilities. Barriers included time constraints, a lack of pre-existing documentation culture, and a perception among some clinicians that patients were too sick to prioritize use of the form.

**CONCLUSION**: The TIF achieved high adoption among non-specialist providers in a resource-limited setting, demonstrating that low-cost, contextually developed tools can bridge the gap between clinical effectiveness and implementation success. Sustained scale-up will require structural solutions to address time and documentation barriers, targeted training to correct the misperception that the tool is unsuitable for the most severely injured patients, and embedded feedback mechanisms to maintain clinician engagement.

articles.title: Predictors and clinical outcomes of extubation failure in patients with cervical spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Respiratory compromise is common in cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) and poses a challenge in deciding whether to extubate or perform a tracheostomy. This study evaluated the characteristics of failed extubations and hypothesized that those with unsuccessful extubation attempts would have a higher trauma burden and worse weaning parameters.

**METHODS**: This was a retrospective review of intubated cervical SCI at a Level 1 trauma center from 2018 to 2024. Demographics, injury, surgical and airway management data were collected. Location of intubation and extubation, weaning parameters, and time to airway event or failure were tabulated. Statistical analysis was completed using Stata with p < 0.05 as significant.

**RESULTS**: Seventy patients with SCI were analyzed with a mean age of 54 years (range 18-89) and 62 (89%) males. Twenty successful extubations (SE) were compared to 36 failed extubations (FE), excluding the direct to tracheostomy (10) or terminally extubated (4) patients. Frequency of TBI (5% FE vs 14% SE, p = 0.3), blunt cerebrovascular injury (25% vs. 32%, p = 0.63) and ISS (30 vs 23, p = 0.13) were not statistically different. Documented weaning parameters - rapid shallow breathing index and negative inspiratory force were similar, although more FE patients were extubated in the OR/PACU. FE patients had significantly fewer hospital and ICU-free days; however, mortality differences did not reach statistical significance.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Failed extubation in SCI is associated with longer length of stay. Trauma burden and weaning parameters were not correlated with FE; however, extubation outside of the ICU may increase the risk of failure.

articles.title: Fracture-related infection after operative fixation of acetabular fractures: Incidence and factors independently associated with infection.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: The purpose of this study was to determine the incidence of fracture-related infection following acetabular fracture fixation and to identify factors independently associated with its occurrence.

**METHODS**: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted at a Level I trauma center. Patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent operative fixation of an acetabular fracture between January 2021 and July 2025 were included. Fracture-related infection was defined according to the AO/EBJIS consensus definition. Patients were followed for a minimum of 12 months. Multivariable analysis was performed using Firth penalized logistic regression.

**RESULTS**: Of 359 patients, 27 (7.5%) developed fracture-related infection. All 27 met at least 1 confirmatory criterion. The median time to diagnosis was 9 days (IQR, 7-14), with 20 infections (74.1%) diagnosed within 14 days of fixation. Sixteen infections (59.3%) were culture-positive, with gram-negative organisms more common than Staphylococcus aureus. Eleven infections (40.7%) were culture-negative, including 6 patients who had received empirical linezolid before tissue sampling. All infected patients underwent infection-related reoperation; 23 (85.2%) were managed with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention, and 4 (14.8%) underwent implant removal. On Firth penalized multivariable analysis, higher body mass index (adjusted OR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.15-1.55), longer operative duration (1.63; 1.11-2.36), diabetes mellitus (2.55; 1.09-6.05), and a longer admission-to-surgery interval (1.08; 1.00-1.16) were independently associated with infection. Polytrauma was not independently associated with infection (2.10; 0.89-5.09). At final follow-up, fracture union was achieved in 20 patients (74.1%).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Fracture-related infection after acetabular fracture fixation appears to reflect a combination of patient-related and operative factors. Recognizing these factors may help identify patients at higher risk and allow closer postoperative surveillance.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Prognostic Level III.

articles.title: Preoperative CT-derived psoas attenuation and correction loss after traumatic thoracolumbar fracture fixation: A construct-dependent association.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Postoperative correction loss remains a concern after posterior fixation of traumatic thoracolumbar fractures. Although bone quality and construct characteristics influence mechanical stability, the role of preoperative muscle quality remains poorly defined. We examined whether CT-derived psoas attenuation was associated with correction loss and whether fracture-level screw placement modified this association.

**METHODS**: This retrospective single-center cohort included 78 adults who underwent posterior pedicle screw fixation for traumatic AO Spine A3 thoracolumbar fractures. Preoperative psoas and paravertebral attenuation and cross-sectional area were measured at L3. Correction loss was defined as the difference between final-follow-up and immediate postoperative Cobb angles measured on supine sagittal CT reconstructions. Multivariable linear regression tested the interaction between centered psoas attenuation and fracture-level screw placement, adjusting for age, sex, vertebral attenuation, instrumented levels, and follow-up duration. An extended model added vertebral height loss and canal compromise. HC3 robust variance estimation and sensitivity analyses were performed.

**RESULTS**: Mean correction loss was 4.1 ± 5.4°, and 23 patients (29.5%) experienced loss greater than 5°. The psoas attenuation-by-fracture-level screw interaction was significant (B=0.311°/HU; 95% CI, 0.091-0.530; p = .006; HC3 p = .037). Without fracture-level screws, each 10-HU increase in psoas attenuation corresponded to approximately 2.6° less correction loss (B=-0.255°/HU; 95% CI, -0.440 to -0.071; p = .007), although HC3 inference crossed the null (p = .068). No clear association was observed with fracture-level screws. The interaction persisted after adjustment for vertebral height loss and canal compromise (B=0.342°/HU; 95% CI, 0.127-0.556; p = .002; HC3 p = .016), when short- versus long-segment fixation replaced instrumented-level count, and in patients with at least 12 months of follow-up. Paravertebral attenuation showed a similar pattern, whereas muscle cross-sectional area did not.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Preoperative psoas attenuation showed a construct-dependent association with correction loss after fixation of traumatic AO Spine A3 fractures. Lower attenuation may identify mechanical vulnerability when the fractured vertebra is not incorporated into the construct. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before CT-based muscle assessment can guide construct selection.

articles.title: Comparative mortality of pelvic ring fractures vs. hip fractures in adults ≥55 years: A propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Hip and pelvic fragility fractures are associated with substantial mortality in older adults. While standardized care pathways are established for hip fractures, management of pelvic fragility fractures remains less defined. This study compared mortality between matched hip and pelvic ring fracture patients managed operatively or nonoperatively.

**HYPOTHESIS**: Pelvic and hip fractures would demonstrate comparable mortality within operative and nonoperative treatment groups.

**PATIENTS AND METHODS**: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX network to identify adults aged ≥ 55 years with hip or pelvic ring fractures. Patients were stratified by operative or nonoperative management, and cohorts were propensity score matched 1:1 based on demographic and clinical characteristics. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were mortality at 30 days, 90 days, and 2 years. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated 1-year mortality.

**RESULTS**: After matching, 255,202 patients per cohort were included in the nonoperative subgroup and 11,448 per cohort in the operative subgroup. Among nonoperative patients, 1-year mortality was higher after hip than pelvic fracture (11.13% vs 10.68%; HR 1.123, 95% CI 1.105-1.141). Among operative patients, 1-year mortality was also higher after hip fracture (8.84% vs 5.94%; HR 1.424, 95% CI 1.314-1.545). However, 30-day mortality was higher after operative pelvic fracture (3.11% vs 2.49%; p = 0.004). Male sex, older age, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease were associated with increased mortality.

**DISCUSSION**: Hip fractures were associated with greater 1-year mortality across management strategies; however, operative pelvic fractures demonstrated greater early mortality. These findings highlight pelvic fragility fractures as high-risk injuries warranting further evaluation of standardized geriatric care pathways.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: III.

articles.title: Facial burns as functional trauma: Integrating expression, identity and long-term recovery: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Advances in acute burn care have improved survival, shifting focus toward long-term functional recovery. Facial burns present a distinct clinical challenge due to the concentration of ocular, oral, respiratory, and expressive functions within a highly visible anatomical region.
