This narrative review synthesises functional and psychosocial literature to examine facial burns as trauma that disrupts dynamic facial movement, communication, and participation, and to evaluate limitations in current outcome frameworks. The face supports ocular protection, articulation, alimentation, airway patency, and non-verbal signalling. Contracture patterns, including microstomia, ectropion, nasal distortion, and midfacial contracture, may impair both mechanical function and expressive range. Recovery is typically longitudinal and iterative, addressing evolving distortion rather than restoring pre-injury dynamics. Even subtle restrictions of facial movement may alter speech clarity, eye contact, and self-recognition, with consequences extending beyond visible scarring. Existing outcome measures, including body image scales, burn-specific health instruments, and isolated physical metrics, do not adequately capture the interaction between structural repair, expressive mobility, and communicative participation. Recognition of facial burns as functional trauma supports the need for facial-specific composite outcome models and coordinated multidisciplinary care to optimise long-term recovery.

articles.title: A tale of two nails: A retrospective cohort comparison of TFNA and PFNA in proximal femoral fracture fixation.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: The aging population has transformed proximal femoral fractures into a public health crisis, resulting in an increased burden of postoperative complications and revision surgeries. While the Proximal Femoral Nail Antirotation (PFNA) has been a standard in certain countries, the Trochanteric Fixation Nail Advanced (TFNA) was introduced with engineering refinements intended to enhance fixation. This study aims to compare the two implants, specifically focusing on fixation failure rates and distinct biomechanical failure mechanisms.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at an Academic Level I trauma center involving 1006 patients treated between January 2020 and March 2025. Patients with a minimum six-month follow-up were included (681 PFNA, 325 TFNA). Radiographic assessments, including reduction quality, Tip-Apex Distance (TAD), and blade positioning, were independently performed by two senior fellowship-trained surgeons. The primary outcome was fixation failure requiring reoperation.

**RESULTS**: The fixation failure rate was 1.6% (n = 11) in the PFNA group and 3.4% (n = 11) in the TFNA group; however, this difference was not statistically significant. While radiographic parameters such as TAD and reduction quality did not differ significantly between the failure groups, a distinct shift in biomechanical failure modes was identified. PFNA failures were overwhelmingly characterized by the classic "cut-out" mechanism (91%), whereas TFNA failures frequently involved medial migration or "cut-through" (55%).

**CONCLUSION**: Although the TFNA was associated with a higher absolute rate of fixation failure, no statistically significant difference in fixation failure rates was observed between the two implants. However, the failure profile shifted toward medial "cut-through" migration with the TFNA. These findings suggest that the TFNA may possess a unique failure profile, potentially reflecting a learning curve or specific biomechanical properties. Suboptimal reduction and blade positioning were frequent among the failures and may have contributed to them; however, a considerable proportion of failures occurred after a reduction graded as good. These findings emphasize that technical precision remains the primary determinant of stability, regardless of the cephalomedullary device used.

articles.title: The Effect of Guanfacine on Delirium in Surgical and Trauma ICU Patients: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To evaluate the feasibility of conducting a randomized controlled trial investigating guanfacine for ICU delirium, including assessment of recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, and data completeness, while estimating treatment effects to inform future trial design.

**DESIGN**: Single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial conducted from November 2020 to February 2023.

**SETTING**: Surgical and Trauma ICUs at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Hospital.

**PATIENTS**: One hundred critically ill adults with Confusion Assessment Method-ICU-confirmed delirium randomized 1:1 to guanfacine or placebo.

**INTERVENTIONS**: Patients received 2 mg guanfacine or matching placebo nightly for up to 14 days, or until ICU discharge or delirium resolution.

**MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS**: Primary feasibility outcomes included protocol adherence (target ≥ 90%), retention (target ≥ 80%), recruitment rate (target ≥ 2 patients/mo), and data completeness (target ≥ 95%). Most feasibility targets were achieved: protocol adherence was 100%, retention was 100%, and data completeness was 100%. Recruitment was significantly impacted by COVID-19 pandemic disruptions, achieving 0.9 patients/wk during active recruitment periods.For clinical outcomes, in unadjusted analyses, median delirium and coma-free days were higher with guanfacine than placebo (2 [interquartile range [IQR], 0-6] vs. 1 [IQR, 0-4]; p = 0.02); however, this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for prespecified baseline covariates. ICU and hospital length of stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ significantly between groups. No hemodynamic differences or safety concerns were observed.

**CONCLUSIONS**: This pilot study successfully supports feasibility for a definitive trial, with excellent protocol adherence, adequate retention, and preliminary signals that warrant further evaluation. Although adjusted analyses were not statistically significant, the observed unadjusted difference in delirium and coma-free days and favorable safety profile support progression to a multicenter trial informed by these pilot estimates.

articles.title: From sirens to systems: Characterizing EMS and trauma care across America.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: State emergency medical services (EMS) and trauma systems determine prehospital triage, transport, trauma center designation, data reporting, and quality improvement, yet their contemporary organization has not been systematically characterized. We sought to describe state-level EMS and trauma system structures, policies, resources, and perceived gaps across the United States.

**METHODS**: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of EMS and trauma system leaders in all 50 states and the District of Columbia from July 2025 through March 2026. A 56-item instrument utilizing categorical, Likert-type, rank-order, and free-text items assessed oversight, prehospital triage and transport, clinical protocols, trauma center verification, registries, quality improvement, and funding. Respondents were recruited by email and phone. Multiple respondents could contribute complementary domain-level information to a single state profile. Responses were summarized descriptively.

**RESULTS**: All 51 jurisdictions participated. Most states reported a state EMS medical director (84%), statewide trauma triage protocols (84%), and mandatory participation in their state trauma registry (88%). However, operational coordination varied: only 29% had a centralized trauma communications center, only 6% of states reported a single point of contact for helicopter EMS dispatch, and 35% required a certificate of need for new helicopter services. Trauma center verification relied on American College of Surgeons (ACS) verification in 59% of states, while others used state-administered processes. More than half of states rated EMS financial resources in the two lowest adequacy categories, and 55% reported that their trauma system required at least moderate improvement. Rural populations were most frequently identified as underserved (96%) and as experiencing worse outcomes (92%).

**CONCLUSIONS**: State EMS and trauma systems share broad adoption of national clinical standards but differ substantially in governance, coordination, verification, data integration, and funding.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE AND STUDY TYPE**: Level V, Prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Non-urgent emergency department utilization in adults: a systematic review of associated factors across diverse health systems.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Non-urgent emergency department (ED) visits represent a growing global challenge with significant economic and operational consequences. Despite previous reviews, important gaps remain. No review has included all commonly used terms for non-urgent ED visits, recent evidence has not been synthesised, and factors related to patients, health systems, and care contexts have rarely been examined together. This systematic review aimed to identify and categorize factors associated with non-urgent ED visits in adults.

**METHODS**: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for articles published between January 2015 and May 2026. We included cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control studies that compared urgent and non-urgent ED visits and reported at least one associated factor. Quality assessment was performed using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists. Because of substantial heterogeneity in definitions, the findings were synthesised narratively.

**RESULTS**: Thirty-two studies from 21 countries were included. The proportion of non-urgent visits ranged from 1% to 82.4%, depending on the definition and measurement approach used. Five approaches were used to define non-urgent visits. The most common were triage-based (41%) and clinical judgment-based (28%). Associated factors were classified into three main categories: (1) demographic and socioeconomic (younger age, female sex, low income, lower education, non-native nationality); (2) access and health system (self-referral, arrival on foot, weekend visits, shorter distance to ED, lack of a family physician, public insurance); and (3) clinical and perceptual (non-specific diagnosis, musculoskeletal problems, mental health conditions, prior ED visit history, and patient perception of illness severity). The strongest associations were reported for frequent previous ED visits (aOR up to 82.13) and patients who perceived their illness as non-serious (aOR up to 21.03).

**CONCLUSION**: Non-urgent ED visits are influenced by multiple individual, health system, and perceptual factors. The substantial heterogeneity in definitional approaches underscores the need for conceptual standardization. No single intervention is likely to reduce non-urgent ED visits. Effective strategies should strengthen primary care, improve insurance policies, increase public health education, and empower patients.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med

articles.title: A bedside score using arrival data to identify major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring fracture: Development and validation.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Early recognition of major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring injury could guide mobilization of transfusion and hemorrhage-control resources. We developed an arrival-based bedside score and compared its performance with shock index.

**METHODS**: We studied 239,736 adults with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures in the 2019-2024 National Trauma Data Bank. Major hemorrhage was defined as a hemorrhage-control procedure, hemorrhagic death, or transfusion of ≥ 1000 mL or ≥ 4 units of red blood cells within 4 h. Penalized logistic regression selected arrival variables for an integer score. We assessed performance in a held-out test set (n = 79,912) and at approximately matched alert volume. A model refitted on 2019-2022 admissions was evaluated in 2023-2024. Subgroup analyses were post hoc.

**RESULTS**: Major hemorrhage occurred in 26,479 patients (11.0%); 31.0% were aged ≥ 75 years, and 45.9% had fallen. In the test set, the score achieved an AUROC of 0.882 (95% CI, 0.879-0.886), exceeding shock index by 0.060 (95% CI, 0.055-0.064; P < 0.001). At approximately 15.6% of patients flagged, the score identified 678 additional major hemorrhage cases with 684 fewer false-positive alerts. The temporally validated model achieved an AUROC of 0.885 (95% CI, 0.881-0.888). Discrimination exceeded shock index for pelvic ring disruption (0.830 vs 0.778) and high-energy mechanisms (0.811 vs 0.764), but was lower after falls (0.779 vs 0.800).

**CONCLUSIONS**: In patients with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures, an arrival-based score identified major hemorrhage more accurately than shock index at a similar alert burden. Reduced performance after falls and uncertain applicability to suspected fractures warrant caution. External validation and prospective impact assessment are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Traumatic hip dislocation: Clinical and epidemiological features, management and prognostic factors in a series of 44 cases from a tertiary centre.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Traumatic hip dislocation is an uncommon but potentially severe injury requiring emergency management. We aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological features and associated injuries of patients with traumatic hip dislocation treated at a tertiary centre, and to analyse the factors related to complications and to the need for salvage surgery.

**PATIENTS AND METHODS**: Retrospective observational study of 44 patients aged 15 years or older treated between 2010 and 2024. Demographic variables, injury mechanism, direction of the dislocation, associated fractures (Judet-Letournel and Pipkin classifications), management and complications were recorded. Bivariate analysis used Fisher's exact test for categorical variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables; a p value < 0.05 was considered significant.

**RESULTS**: Mean age was 37.4 years (SD 19.3) and 70.5% of patients were men. The commonest mechanism was a road traffic accident (52.3%) and the posterior direction was the most frequent (72.7%). A complex dislocation (with an associated fracture) was present in 72.7% of patients, and 36.4% occurred in the context of polytrauma. Closed reduction was performed in 88.6% of cases, with a median time to reduction of 2 h. The most frequent complication was sciatic nerve injury (20.5%). Femoral head osteonecrosis occurred in 2 patients (4.5%). Male sex was associated with more late complications (p = 0.043), and a prolonged hospital stay was associated with both early (p = 0.002) and late (p = 0.017) complications. Complex dislocations showed a consistent trend towards greater morbidity.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Traumatic hip dislocation predominantly affects young men after high-energy trauma. Prompt reduction was associated with a low rate of osteonecrosis. The presence of associated fractures and a prolonged hospital stay identify patients with a worse course.

articles.title: Does the number of debridement procedures impact risk of infection in open fractures?
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between the number of debridements and risk of infection, while stratifying by degree of wound contamination. It was hypothesized that patients with severe contamination, a higher number of debridements would be associated with lower risk of infection.

**METHODS**: This is a retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected data in the PREP-IT trial (Program of Randomized trials to Evaluate Preoperative antiseptic skin solutions in orthopaedic Trauma). The primary outcome measure was adjudicated surgical site infection. Independent variables were number of debridement procedures and time from injury to definitive wound closure. Analysis was stratified by degree of contamination and multivariable analyses were performed to control for confounders.

**RESULTS**: 3502 total open fractures corresponding to 3222 patients with a median (interquartile range, IQR) age of 42 (29-58) years (2199 [62.8%] men; median (IQR) body mass index 27.7 [24.3-32.6]) were included in this analysis. 2199 patients were included in the non/minimal contamination group, 970 in the surface contamination group, and 333 in the embedded contamination group. After controlling for patient-level characteristics there was a 27% increase in the risk of infection for each debridement performed in the overall patient cohort (OR 1.27 [1.12-1.43] p < 0.001), and a 45% increase in the embedded contamination group (OR, 1.45 [1.12-1.88] p = 0.004). There was no statistically significant difference between minimal contamination groups and the surface contamination group.

**CONCLUSION**: The results of this study indicate that increased number of debridement procedures was not associated with lower infectious rates. Patients with the highest degree of contamination demonstrated significantly increased risk of developing an infection with each additional debridement. These findings support the importance of limiting unnecessary additional debridement procedures to reduce infection risk and optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Cone-Beam CT-Guided SpineJack® vertebral augmentation: A reproducible technique for accurate pedicular access and implant deployment.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: SpineJack® vertebral augmentation requires precise bilateral transpedicular access and accurate implant deployment. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and technical performance of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-guided SpineJack augmentation.

**METHODS**: This retrospective single-institution, two-site study included consecutive CBCT-guided procedures performed between May 2021 and April 2026. Technical success required planned bilateral implantation, expansion, and cement augmentation without pedicle breach or implant malposition on final CBCT. Secondary outcomes included immediate vertebral height restoration, complications, procedure duration, radiation exposure, and treatment setting.

**RESULTS**: The analysis included 178 procedures; median age was 45 years (interquartile range [IQR], 27-59), and 158 procedures (88.8%) involved traumatic fractures. Technical success was 100% (178/178), including 64 procedures (36.0%) with pedicle-implant clearance < 0.8 mm. Median absolute vertebral body height gain was 4.1 mm (IQR, 2.7-6.1), and median restoration of baseline height loss reached 77% (IQR, 47-98). All 24 cement leaks (13.5%) were asymptomatic. No neurological, vascular, infectious, or implant-related complications occurred. Median procedure duration was 60 min (IQR, 50-90), and median dose-area product was 33.2 Gy·cm² (IQR, 19.4-53.1). One hundred procedures (56.2%) were performed on an outpatient basis.

**CONCLUSIONS**: CBCT-guided SpineJack augmentation achieved accurate bilateral implant deployment and substantial immediate vertebral height restoration without major procedure-related complications. These findings support CBCT as a reliable guidance strategy for vertebral augmentation, with demonstrated feasibility in outpatient practice.

articles.title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation (SPD) is a rare, high-energy injury associated with substantial mortality and morbidity. Surgical stabilization is technically challenging and has historically been associated with relatively high rates of construct failure. The present study describes and evaluates a novel minimally invasive spinopelvic diamond-shaped construct (The MIS-Diamond fixation), designed to improve rigid triangular stabilization while minimizing soft-tissue morbidity and facilitate the fracture reduction.

**METHODS**: A retrospective observational study was conducted including patients who underwent MIS-Diamond fixation for AO Type C3 sacral fractures at a single Level-I Trauma Center between January 2014 and December 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, and radiological outcomes were systematically assessed. Fractures were classified according to the AO Spine Sacral Injury Classification System.

**RESULTS**: Thirty-two patients (mean age 39 years) were included. Surgery was performed at a median of 5 days post-injury, with a mean operative time of 115.8 min and mean estimated blood loss of 82.7 mL. No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a postoperative S1 motor impairment attributed to indirect radicular injury during reduction. Implant-related complications were recorded in 4 patients (12.5%), including one late-onset surgical site infection and three cases of asymptomatic iliac screw loosening. No soft tissue or wound healing complications were observed. Implant removal was successfully completed in 28 patients (87.5%) at 12 months postoperatively.

**DISCUSSION**: MIS-Diamond fixation demonstrated a favourable safety profile while enabling early postoperative mobilization. The incorporation of a 5.5 mm transverse iliac rod converts the classical triangular construct into a rigid box-like configuration, enhancing rotational stability and preventing coronal diastasis during vertical distraction. Limiting instrumentation to L4-L5 reduces the number of immobilized motion segments compared to previously described longer constructs, potentially mitigating long-term degenerative sequelae.

**CONCLUSIONS**: The MIS-Diamond fixation represents a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical option for SPD, providing reliable multiplanar stabilization with a low complication profile. Routine implant removal at 12 months is feasible and recommended to preserve motion segment function. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

articles.title: Pooled Prevalence of Infectious Diseases Among First Responders in the Prehospital Setting: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis by Occupation.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers.

**METHODS**: Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using 

**RESULTS**: Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%-5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonization. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%-25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%-12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, 

**CONCLUSIONS**: Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

articles.title: Prehospital Whole Blood Resuscitation in Pediatric Patients: A San Antonio Cohort Descriptive.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: The objective of this study is to describe the demographic, clinical, and prehospital care characteristics of pediatric patients receiving whole blood (WB) resuscitation by San Antonio Fire Department (SAFD).

**METHODS**: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study to evaluate pediatric patients who received prehospital low-titer group O positive WB transfusion through the SAFD prehospital blood program between October 2018 and June 2025. The objective was to characterize patient demographics, injury patterns, resuscitative interventions, shock physiology, and outcomes among pediatric recipients in a mature civilian emergency medical services WB program.

**RESULTS**: Of 1703 WB transfusions, 73 (4.3%) were pediatric. Most patients were male (76%), age range 1-17 years old with a mode of 17 years, adolescents represented 78%. Trauma accounted for 96% of cases, firearm injury (74%); all penetrating (84%), blunt (12%), with the remainder classified as medical/unknown. Vascular access was intravenous (73%), intraosseous (26%). Tranexamic acid was co-administered in 39%; 12% received ceftriaxone. When analyzed using age-adjusted Shock Index Pediatric Age-Adjusted (SIPA) thresholds (>1.2 for 1-6 years, >1.0 for 7-12 years, and >0.9 for 13-17 years), based on the initial available prehospital heart rate and systolic blood pressure, 45% of patients had an elevated SIPA, 22% had a normal SIPA, 20% were pulseless and therefore could not undergo SIPA calculation, and 14% lacked sufficient vital-sign data for classification. Survival was 50%; died 39%, and unknown outcomes 11%. Mean delta shock index values were most negative in toddlers (1-4 years) -0.97 ± 1.29, followed by children (5-11 years) -0.76 ± 1.07 and adolescents (12-17 years) -0.16 ± 0.46, indicating a greater physiologic response to resuscitation among younger pediatric patients.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Pediatric WB recipients were predominantly adolescent males who sustained penetrating trauma and presented with moderate-to-severe shock. Younger age groups had larger descriptive decreases in shock index during the prehospital encounter; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small subgroup sizes and observational design.

articles.title: Hospital cost structures and resource utilisation across representative treatment pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care: a nationwide DRG-based analysis in Germany.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Implant-associated orthopaedic infections require prolonged inpatient treatment, repeated surgery and multidisciplinary care, yet nationwide evidence on how hospital resources are distributed across clinically distinct treatment pathways is limited. This study characterised hospital-side case costs, resource utilisation and aggregate expenditure across representative German diagnosis-related groups (DRGs) relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care.

**METHODS**: Publicly available 2024 data from the German Institute for the Hospital Remuneration System (InEK) were analysed. Twelve representative DRGs were selected a priori from official definitions and diagnostic/procedural profiles and grouped into six treatment pathways. The InEK cost matrix reflects standardised hospital-side resource costs from participating calculation hospitals and does not represent actual DRG reimbursement. National case frequencies, length of stay and mean case costs were analysed using frequency-weighted pathway estimates, while pathway-level cost composition was calculated from aggregate component expenditure.

**RESULTS**: The included DRGs represented 36,212 hospitalisations and €305.2 million in aggregate annual hospital-side expenditure represented by the selected DRGs. Mean hospital-side costs ranged from €5,859 to €22,495 per case. Ward care accounted for approximately 34-69% of pathway expenditure; operating theatre services contributed up to 39% in revision arthroplasty. Geriatric rehabilitation generated the largest aggregate expenditure (€119.0 million; 39.0%) because of high case volume, whereas complex vacuum-assisted wound care had the highest per-case cost but only 2.9% of aggregate expenditure. At the aggregated DRG level, mean length of stay was associated with mean case cost (Pearson r = 0.87, 95% CI 0.60-0.96; P < 0.001); leave-one-out correlations ranged from r = 0.79 to r = 0.96.

**CONCLUSION**: Resource requirements differ markedly across representative DRG pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Because the selected DRGs are not infection-exclusive, the reported expenditure should not be interpreted as the national economic burden of implant-associated orthopaedic infection. The findings may inform hospital resource planning and future cost-revenue analyses.

articles.title: Violent Reinjury Trajectories Across Injury Mechanisms: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
**STUDY OBJECTIVE**: Survivors of violent injury often experience reinjury. We sought to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with violent reinjury across different injury types.

**METHODS**: We conducted an observational cohort study of individuals with violent injury (ie, blunt assaults, stabbings, and firearm injuries) across 2 adult and 2 pediatric Level I trauma centers from 2016 to 2023. Covariates included age, sex, race, hospital type, insurance status, and social vulnerability. Our primary outcome was time to reinjury. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to measure associations between each covariate and time to reinjury across injury types.

**RESULTS**: There were 29,038 individuals with nonfatal violent injuries. Male sex (n=19,273; 66.4%), Black and other race (n=21,403; 73.7%), presentation to adult hospitals (n=24,200; 83.3%), public insurance (n=13,879; 47.8%), and living in an area with high social vulnerability (n=21,044; 72.5%) were associated with a greater risk of any violent reinjury, adjusting for covariates. For index firearm injuries, patients younger than18 years had greater risk of firearm reinjury than patients aged 18 to 26 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]:0.65 [0.47 to 0.91]) and for those older than 26 years (aHR:0.47 [0.34 to 0.66]). Although women with firearm injury had a lower risk of firearm reinjury compared with men (aHR:0.46 [0.36 to 0.58]), they had greater risk of blunt reinjury (aHR:1.77 [1.34 to 1.24]). Patients living in areas with high social vulnerability had a higher risk of escalating reinjury mechanism (eg, blunt to firearm; aHR:1.46 [1.11 to 1.90]) versus patients in areas with low/average social vulnerability.

**CONCLUSION**: This research underscores how sequelae of violent reinjury are shaped by certain demographic and clinical characteristics, highlighting opportunities to strengthen reinjury prevention in key subgroups.

articles.title: Prospective Observational Study Assessing Patient Characteristics, Management and Early Outcomes of Major Trauma Patients With Prehospital Shock. A preliminary report of the Sydney COAST study.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Despite advances in trauma resuscitation, significant gaps remain in understanding how early physiological and biochemical derangements influence clinical outcomes. The Sydney 'Clinical Outcomes following Acute Shock in Trauma' (COAST) registry was developed by clinicians containing both prehospital and in-hospital data, allowing for the identification of risk factors that influence early mortality for major trauma patients with shock. This study reports the formation of the registry and the patient cohort enrolled over its first 12 months.

**METHODS**: A multi-centre, prospective registry of shocked adult trauma patients treated by prehospital medical teams and transported directly to a Sydney-based major trauma centre. Shock was defined as either (1) systolic blood pressure less than 100 mmHg, (2) shock index greater than one, (3) blood transfusion or (4) administration of inotropes. Descriptive statistics were used to report outcomes including injuries, pathology, transfusions, immediate intervention, mortality and length of stay.

**RESULTS**: Two hundred fifty seven patients were enrolled. The predominant shock criteria for inclusion was hypotension (90% of cases), whilst 53% received prehospital blood transfusion. Interventional haemorrhage control was required in 31% of cases, whilst 74% received in-hospital transfusion. Injury severity was high (median injury severity score of 27). Four-hour mortality was 4.7% (9% at 24-h and 21% at 30-days).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Consistent with recent observational studies, the Sydney COAST registry captured a cohort of critically ill trauma patients, not all of whom may have had haemorrhage. This will serve as an important dataset, allowing clinicians to better understand factors driving traumatic shock whilst exploring avenues for improving care in these cases.

articles.title: Supply of Fibrinogen Concentrate Across Queensland Health.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: To describe fibrinogen concentrate (FC) supply across Queensland Health.

**METHODS**: Statewide FC supply from January 2016 to September 2026 was analysed by service type, geography, major trauma designation, viscoelastic haemostatic assay (VHA) availability and temporal trends.

**RESULTS**: Of 24,717 g FC supplied, 97.0% was distributed to 54 hospitals, 2.0% to retrieval services and 1.0% to ambulance services. Of hospital supply, 25.4% reached regional and 6.1% remote/very remote hospitals; 66.2% was supplied to major trauma services and 92.9% to VHA-capable hospitals. Population-adjusted FC supply increased from 8.19 to 59.2 g per 100,000 population between 2016 and 2025.

**CONCLUSION**: FC supply has increased substantially across Queensland, extending to regional, remote and prehospital services. This highlights the value of statewide patient-level utilisation data for haemovigilance.

articles.title: Synovial fluid biomarker changes after acute anterior cruciate ligament injury: comparison with primary osteoarthritis as a biological comparator.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUNDS**: Post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) typically develops 10-20 years after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, but reliable early biomarkers are lacking. We examined synovial fluid biomarker changes in patients with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) and in patients with primary OA. The primary OA group served as a biological comparator representing established degenerative OA, not as a healthy or matched control.

**METHODS**: Our study included patients from January 1, 2021 to September 30, 2023: 51 with primary OA biological comparator and 53 with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group). Levels of Interleukin (IL)-1β, sulfated glycosaminoglycans (sGAG), aggrecan neoepitope fragment (ARGS-aggrecan), and cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) were measured in synovial fluid and compared between the two groups at baseline and one year later. Patients underwent unilateral knee MRI and bilateral weight-bearing radiography at follow-up.

**RESULTS**: The findings demonstrated that synovial fluid from acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) and primary OA biological comparator contained inflammatory mediators, collagen markers, and aging-related indicators such as CRP. Following one year of surgical follow-up, PCT, GAG, CTxI, osteocalcin, β-aspartate, and COMP all showed significant decreases. Biomarker comparisons between groups revealed that the primary OA biological comparator had significantly lower levels of CRP, GAG, ARGS, BMP2, FGF-10, and ADAM-TS5 than the ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group, while CTX-II showed no discernible difference. The Spearman rank correlation was used to examine synovial fluid biomarker concentrations relative to injury duration. Significant time-dependence was observed for: IL-1b (p = 0.025, Rs=-0.112), GAG (p = 0.011, Rs=-0.265), ARGS aggrecan (p = 0.032, Rs=-0.021), C1,2 C (p = 0.002, Rs=0.665), CTxI (p = 0.025, Rs=0.251), C2C (p = 0.011, Rs=0.055), CPII (p = 0.015, Rs=0.336), Osteocalcin (p = 0.029, Rs=0.114), β-aspartate (p = 0.001, Rs=-0.77), D-Asx (p = 0.0215, Rs=-0.425), MMP-3 (p = 0.0201, Rs=0.356), and WOMAC (p = 0.001, Rs=0.264). Univariate regression analysis demonstrated significant associations of IL-1β and osteocalcin with ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group membership. Multivariate logistic regression revealed significant associations with increased levels of β-aspartate, WOMAC, GAG, IL-1β, and osteocalcin. LASSO regression analysis was employed as an exploratory feature selection method to identify the biomarker panel that best distinguished between the ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group and primary OA biological comparators within this cohort. Among the 20 variables included in the analysis, five demonstrated non-zero coefficients in the LASSO model: WOMAC, GAG, β-aspartate, IL-1β, and osteocalcin. These findings suggest that inflammatory markers, matrix turnover products, and functional status are prominent features differentiating the acute post-injury state from chronic degenerative OA in this dataset. However, given the exploratory nature of this analysis and the lack of external validation, these results should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in independent cohorts.

**CONCLUSION**: Our findings demonstrate that patients with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) exhibit distinct synovial fluid molecular signatures compared with a primary OA biological comparator. These signatures encompass acute inflammatory responses and early matrix remodeling. However, this study cannot explain why only approximately 18.8% of ACL-injured patients later develop PTOA. Future longitudinal studies including ACL-injured non-progressors and age-, sex-, and activity-matched controls are required.

articles.title: Direct ICU admission versus floor-to-ICU upgrade in geriatric patients with multiple rib fractures and flail chest: A national analysis.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: It remains unclear whether direct ICU admission benefits geriatric patients compared with delayed floor-to-ICU upgrade. The study evaluated the association of direct ICU admission versus floor-to-ICU upgrade with clinical outcomes in geriatric trauma patients with flail chest and thoracic injury, stratified by oxygenation compromise, frailty, and rib fracture burden.

**METHODS**: This retrospective cohort study used the 2017-2024 ACS-TQIP-PUF to identify patients aged 65 years or older with blunt trauma, flail chest, at least three rib fractures, an Injury Severity Score of 9 or greater, and thoracic injury. Patients were classified as floor admission without ICU upgrade, direct ICU admission, or floor-to-ICU upgrade. The primary adjusted analysis compared direct ICU admission with floor-to-ICU upgrade, using floor-to-ICU upgrade as the reference group.

**RESULTS**: A total of 6743 patients were included. Mortality did not differ significantly between direct ICU admission and floor-to-ICU upgrade in the primary adjusted analysis (aOR 0.732, 95% CI 0.467-1.148, p = 0.174). Direct ICU admission was associated with lower odds of unplanned intubation (aOR 0.355, 95% CI 0.251-0.502, p < 0.001), ARDS (aOR 0.412, 95% CI 0.172-0.987, p = 0.047), sepsis (aOR 0.352, 95% CI 0.171-0.725, p = 0.005), and DVT (aOR 0.444, 95% CI 0.209-0.942, p = 0.034). Mortality was lower with direct ICU admission among patients with 3-5 documented rib fractures (aOR 0.535, 95% CI 0.296-0.969, p = 0.039), and the association with fewer unplanned intubations persisted across all subgroups. In the secondary analysis, both direct ICU admission and floor-to-ICU upgrade were associated with higher mortality, lower odds of discharge home, and fewer ventilator-free days than floor admission without ICU upgrade.

**CONCLUSION**: Direct ICU admission was associated with lower odds of unplanned intubation, ARDS, sepsis, and DVT compared with floor-to-ICU upgrade. These findings support identifying at-risk geriatric rib fracture patients for direct ICU admission before deterioration occurs.

articles.title: Predicting survival in pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: Development and internal validation of risk scores.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in the pediatric population is associated with poor survival and neurological outcomes. We aimed to develop and internally validate risk scores to predict survival to discharge in pediatric OHCA patients.

**METHODS**: We included pediatric OHCA patients in the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival from 2013 to 2023. We used logistic regression (LR) and classification and regression trees (CART) to develop risk scores using 70% of the data and validated them using the remaining 30% of the data. We used discrimination and predictive accuracy to evaluate model performance.

**RESULTS**: We included 26,895 pediatric patients, of whom 27.8% survived to hospital admission and 11.9% survived to hospital discharge. We developed three separate risk scores for i) infants ii) preschool and school-age children, and iii) adolescents. The most important predictor variables were gender, arrest location, witness status, etiology of arrest, bystander CPR, use of prehospital AED, and first rhythm. Models developed using both LR and CART approaches had good classification accuracy (AUROCC for LR: 0.81, 0.77 and 0.82, AUROCC for CART: 0.78, 0.76, 0.82 for the three age groups) However, we found CART models to be the most useful because they are simpler to follow, classified more patients in low and high survival categories using a smaller number of predictors. The average survival probability in infants for each risk group was 3%, 13%, and 33%, for preschool and school-age children it was 4%, 11%, and 29%, whereas for adolescents it was 4%, 13%, and 48% for the low, moderate, and high survival categories.

**CONCLUSION**: Pediatric patients experiencing OHCA can be classified into low, moderate, and high survival categories using a simple risk score and easily identified prehospital variables. These risk scores can facilitate research, monitor the quality of medical services and can potentially support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Integration of multimodal large language models into point-of-care ultrasound documentation: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: There are no studies evaluating the potential to deploy artificial intelligence in the interpretation of cardiac point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) documentation. Telexy Health developed an image interpretation and documentation system using multimodal model extensions with video capabilities (MLLM) and deployed it on the POCUS manager QpathE. This study evaluated the MLLM's agreement to experts in identifying cardiac POCUS views and interpreting normal and abnormal examinations.

**METHODS**: This was a retrospective pilot study using cardiac POCUS studies stored in QPathE. The MLLM was applied to POCUS examinations until 350 examinations were reached, 100 normal, and 250 with pathology. MLLM view identification and interpretation were recorded using Qualtrics, with expert image review serving as the gold standard.

**RESULTS**: The MLLM was applied to 370 examinations, with 20 failures. View identification agreed with expert review in 151 examinations (43.1%). Cohen's kappa showed fair agreement for apical four-chamber views between expert and MLLM, with moderate agreement for parasternal long axis, parasternal short axis, subxiphoid, and inferior vena cava views. The MLLM agreed with expert interpretation 86 of 100 normal examinations; the agreement varied by pathology with pericardial effusion, ejection fraction, aortic outflow tract, chamber size, and inferior vena cava having an agreement of 8%, 4%, 70%, 0%, and 12% respectively.

**CONCLUSION**: While agreement in image interpretation was poor, this vendor agnostic workflow demonstrated the ability to integrate an MLLM model into image interpretation. While it should not be incorporated into clinical practice in this state, future model improvement may enable automated POCUS interpretation and documentation.

articles.title: Emergency Response and Patient Transport in Remote Indigenous Communities: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Prehospital and inter-facility transport, such as air medical retrieval and pre-birth evacuation, often move Indigenous patients in rural and remote settings out of their communities, where care is already shaped by fragmented funding and structural inequities; no review has mapped these pathways globally. This scoping review mapped evidence on prehospital emergency response and patient transport for this population.

**METHODS**: A librarian-assisted PubMed, Embase, and Scopus search was conducted for English-language publications on March 9, 2026. Eligible studies included an explicit rural Indigenous population with a defined prehospital pathway. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full texts, and a third reviewer resolved disagreements. Data were charted using a standardized form and synthesized descriptively.

**RESULTS**: Across eight countries, 76 studies met the inclusion criteria, primarily from Australia (

**CONCLUSIONS**: The published evidence disproportionately described transporting patients out of their communities. Community first response and tele-support were described more often than their standing in the literature suggests; however, they were rarely evaluated, and Indigenous-led governance of the research itself was reported in 7% of publications. Low reporting frequency does not establish that these models are uncommon in application and practice. Future priorities include community-partnered evaluation of community-based capacity and telehealth-supported care, alongside the development of patient and family cultural safety.

articles.title: Navigating Uncertainty: 2026 AAST Presidential Address.
Global, Regional, and National Burden of Head Injuries and Main Causes, 1990-2021: A Systematic Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study With Projections to 2050.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES**: We report the global, regional, and national burden of head injuries and their principal causes from 1990 to 2021, with projections to 2050.

**METHODS**: In the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, "head injuries" denotes the cause category "injuries to the head". We extracted age-standardized prevalence, incidence, and years lived with disability (YLDs), with absolute case counts and 95% uncertainty intervals, stratified by age, sex, year, country, and sociodemographic index; the etiological category "transport injuries" includes both motorized and nonmotorized modes. Temporal trends were assessed using the estimated annual percentage change, and projections to 2050 were generated with autoregressive integrated moving average models, with order selected by the Akaike information criterion and residual diagnostics.

**RESULTS**: In 2021, head injuries accounted globally for an estimated 37.9 million prevalent cases, 20.8 million new cases, and 5.5 million YLDs. Compared with 1990, these absolute counts had risen by 54.4%, 22.6%, and 52.7%, respectively, reflecting population growth and aging. Over the same period, age-standardized rates (ASRs) declined by 16.5% for prevalence (536.7-448.0 per 100 000), 20.2% for incidence (324.4-259.0), and 16.2% for YLDs (77.3-64.8). Transport injuries were the leading etiological contributor to YLDs (20.7%), followed by falls (9.0%). The highest age-standardized burden was observed in high-middle sociodemographic index regions and in Europe, with older adults and males disproportionately affected. Autoregressive integrated moving average projections suggest a continued decline in ASRs through 2050.

**CONCLUSION**: ASRs of head injury have declined globally between 1990 and 2021, yet absolute case numbers have continued to rise because gains in per-capita risk reduction have been outpaced by population growth and aging.

articles.title: Rapid Endovascular Hemorrhage Control in Trauma: Joint Position Statement from the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma and the Society of Interventional Radiology.
articles.abstract: Timely hemorrhage control is a critical determinant of survival after traumatic injury, and advances in transarterial embolization have made rapid access to endovascular intervention an increasingly important component of contemporary trauma care. This joint position statement from the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma and the Society of Interventional Radiology clarifies expectations for interventional radiology under ACS Verification, Review, and Consultation Program Standard 4.15 and provides practical guidance for integrating endovascular hemorrhage control into trauma centers. Standard 4.15 reflects a requirement for system readiness rather than a universal mandate that every vascular intervention begin within 60 minutes. Rapid intervention is expected when clinically indicated, particularly for patients with an endovascular target who are hemodynamically labile, and the relevant performance interval is the time from a shared decision by trauma surgery and interventional radiology to proceed with intervention to arterial puncture. Trauma centers should establish multidisciplinary activation pathways that enable rapid mobilization of personnel and resources while preserving clinical judgment regarding patient selection and competing priorities. Recommended strategies include standardized activation protocols, process mapping, parallel rather than sequential workflows, early patient transport when appropriate, documentation of key time points, structured debriefing, and continuous performance monitoring. Interventional radiologists should be integrated as essential members of multidisciplinary trauma teams rather than engaged late as procedural consultants. Applying the 60-minute expectation according to clinical urgency and monitoring decision-to-puncture time focuses Standard 4.15 on its intended objectives: institutional readiness, timely definitive hemorrhage control in appropriately selected high-risk patients, and continuous performance improvement.

articles.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited.

**METHODS**: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge.

**RESULTS**: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

articles.title: Laparoscopic approach for emergency colon resection: a retrospective propensity score-matched study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Despite its routine use in elective procedures, the role of laparoscopy in emergency colorectal surgery remains debated due to limited evidence. This study compared laparoscopic and open surgery regarding complications, mortality, and hospital stay following emergency colon operations.

**METHODS**: This retrospective study included adult patients treated at Päijät-Häme Central Hospital between 2010 and 2020 who underwent emergency colon resection. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for comorbidities, prior ICU admission, surgical indication, and contamination between laparoscopic and open surgery groups.

**RESULTS**: All together 484 patients had an emergency colorectal resection of which 85 (17.6%) were carried out laparoscopically, 31 (6.4%) were converted and 377 (76.0%) were open. In the whole cohort, Comprehensive complication index was lower among laparoscopy patients than open surgery patients if intraoperative conversion to open surgery was avoided (25.8 vs. 34.9, p = 0.012). The subgroup analysis also showed lower CCI after laparoscopic resection for patients presented with obstruction (21.3 vs. 29.7, p = 0.046) or colorectal cancer (21.1 vs. 29.4, p = 0.020) A multivariable regression analysis also showed that starting the procedure laparoscopically predicted lower complication rates. Patients who had a laparoscopic resection also had shorter hospital stay (9.0 vs. 12.9 days, p < 0.001). Patients with open surgery had significantly more wound complications (10.3% vs. 1.2%, p = 0.010). Open surgery was also an independent risk factor for higher CCI (p = 0.008) and the need for intensive care (p = 0.027). Mortality was similar regardless of the approach in short term (30 days, p = 0.810; 90 days, p = 0.354) and in long-term survival (p = 0.466).

**CONCLUSIONS**: The laparoscopic technique in colorectal emergencies may offer similar benefits as in elective surgery, with a lower burden of total complications, less wound complications and shorter hospital stay. Laparoscopy was not associated with any unexpected harmful events.

articles.title: Association of tranexamic acid with early death or massive transfusion after severe pelvic ring fractures: A nationwide registry-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Evidence for tranexamic acid during emergency treatment of severe pelvic ring fractures is limited. We examined its association with early death or massive transfusion.

**METHODS**: We studied adults in the Japan Trauma Data Bank from 2019 to 2023 with blunt pelvic ring fractures of Abbreviated Injury Scale severity 3 or higher. Exposure was any in-hospital tranexamic acid. The primary outcome was death within 24 h after arrival or transfusion of at least 20 Japanese red blood cell units within 24 h after injury. We used multiple imputation, propensity-score overlap weighting, and hospital-clustered standard errors.

**RESULTS**: Among 5288 patients, 1985 (37.5%) received tranexamic acid. The weighted primary-outcome risks were 13.0% with tranexamic acid and 18.1% without it (risk ratio 0.72, 95% confidence interval 0.60-0.87). The association was driven by 24-hour mortality (risk ratio 0.62, 95% confidence interval 0.48-0.80); massive transfusion alone (risk ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.73-1.21) and mean red blood cell use did not differ. Any red blood cell transfusion was more frequent with tranexamic acid (risk ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.30). The primary-outcome risk ratio was 0.76 (0.62-0.93) after excluding deaths within 2 h and 0.81 (0.65-1.00) when both components were assessed within 24 h after injury.

**CONCLUSION**: The mortality association was not accompanied by lower transfusion requirements and weakened when outcome time origins were aligned. Because treatment timing was unavailable, these findings do not establish an independent survival benefit and provide no corroborating transfusion evidence of a pelvic-specific hemostatic benefit.

articles.title: Survival From Traumatic Cardiac Arrest After Sequential Decompression of Dual-Tension Thoracic Physiology Without Chest Compressions.
articles.abstract: Traumatic pulseless electrical activity arrest from simultaneous dual-tension thoracic physiology-bilateral tension pneumothorax and tension pneumomediastinum-with concurrent oropharyngeal hematoma causing airway obstruction has not been described as a unified presentation in the published literature. We report a 28-year-old male who sustained penetrating machete injuries producing this presentation and arrested in pulseless electrical activity on arrival. A sequential surgical resuscitation was performed without external chest compressions: hemostasis and evacuation of an oropharyngeal hematoma restored ventilation, with return of peripheral photoplethysmographic signal consistent with pseudo-pulseless electrical activity physiology; bilateral finger thoracostomies achieved pleural decompression; digital exploration through the manubrial wound vented tension pneumomediastinum, producing an audible air rush, immediate resolution of jugular venous distension, and confirmed return of spontaneous circulation. The patient ambulated independently within hours of arrest and was discharged neurologically intact on day 7. This case illustrates that mechanically mediated pulseless electrical activity arrest from dual thoracic obstructive physiology may be reversible by sequential surgical decompression, and that persistent jugular venous distension following pleural decompression may signal residual mediastinal tension warranting urgent decompression.

articles.title: Administered opioids and benzodiazepines and the interpretation of positive trauma urine drug screens.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Urine drug screening (UDS) is routine in trauma care, and results populate trauma registries, quality review, and research. Trauma patients receive opioids and benzodiazepines before urine is collected, so a positive class-matched screen may reflect administered drug rather than pre-injury use. We estimated the magnitude of this effect by drug class and its impact on reported prevalence.

**METHODS**: Retrospective cohort of all trauma patients at a Level II center, 2023-2024 (n = 2538), of whom 1420 (55.9%) underwent UDS. Medication administration was matched to the corresponding immunoassay channel, with fentanyl analyzed against its dedicated assay and opiate-assay-matched opioid against the opiate assay. Logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score, activation, intubation, and substance use disorder. Treatment-associated positives were estimated by g-computation with bootstrap confidence intervals; cannabinoids, amphetamines, and cocaine were negative controls.

**RESULTS**: Class-matched positivity greatly exceeded unexposed positivity: 70.0% versus 12.5% for the fentanyl assay (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 15.3, 95% CI 11.5-20.4), 59.0% versus 19.0% for the opiate assay given an opiate-assay-matched opioid (aOR 5.9), and 51.6% versus 8.9% for benzodiazepines (aOR 6.1). Restricting exposure to pre-hospital administration, which necessarily precedes collection, preserved the effect (fentanyl aOR 19.9). Negative controls showed minimal association (amphetamine aOR 1.1). By g-computation, an estimated 62.8% (56.9-68.6) of fentanyl-assay positives, 33.7% of opiate positives, and 29.3% of benzodiazepine positives were associated with administered drug. Any-positive prevalence was 64.4% overall and 37.3% among patients given neither class.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Administered fentanyl was associated with a model-estimated majority of positive fentanyl-assay screens; administered opiates and benzodiazepines were associated with smaller shares of their corresponding positive screens. Class-matched results should be interpreted alongside the medication record. These findings do not establish the source or analytical validity of an individual positive result.

articles.title: Does greater orthoplastic integration reduce deep infection after open tibial fracture? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Combined orthoplastic management of open tibial fractures is widely recommended, but existing evidence has not quantified whether the degree of care-pathway integration, beyond a binary orthoplastic-versus-orthopaedic distinction, is associated with a graded difference in outcome. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified deep infection and secondary outcome rates across four care-pathway models of increasing team continuity.

**METHODS**: MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and grey literature were searched in collaboration with a specialist medical librarian. Studies were classified into four care-pathway groups: Group 1, single-setting simultaneous fixation and soft tissue coverage; Group 2, staged care with continuous orthoplastic team involvement; Group 3, discontinuous or delayed plastic surgical involvement; Group 4, purely orthopaedic management. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled deep infection, limb salvage, reoperation, and non-union rates per group. Comparative meta-analyses used genuine within-study comparator arms. Confounding was assessed via meta-regression and subgroup analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE.

**RESULTS**: Fifty-eight studies (81 classified arms) were included. Pooled deep infection rates rose progressively with decreasing care-pathway integration: 8% (95% CI 5-12%) in Group 1, 16% (9-24%) in Group 2, 28% (11-49%) in Group 3, and 37% (25-50%) in Group 4. A similar gradient was observed for non-union (4-26% across groups). Limb salvage was near-universal (94-99%) and did not discriminate between pathways. Leave-one-out and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness for Groups 1, 2, and 4; Group 3's estimate was substantially influenced by a single Critical-risk-of-bias study, with deep infection rates attenuating from 28% to 23% on exclusion. No significant publication bias was detected. Certainty of evidence, per GRADE, was Very Low for majority of the pooled estimates, reflecting serious risk of bias and inconsistency, and Low where heterogeneity was minimal.

**CONCLUSION**: Progressive care-pathway integration is associated with a consistent, graded reduction in deep infection and non-union risk following open tibial fracture, independent of injury mechanism. These findings support continued investment in combined orthoplastic care, including partial integration models where single-setting surgery is not achievable.

articles.title: Osteoporosis treatment gaps and risk of recurrent hip fracture following initial fragility fracture: Insights from over one million cases.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Patients who sustain a hip fracture are at high risk of a second hip fracture, yet most do not receive osteoporosis pharmacotherapy. We evaluated the association between bone-health medication initiation after a first hip fracture and the risk of a second hip fracture.

**METHODS**: This retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos, a de-identified multi-institutional electronic health record database. Adults who underwent surgery for a first femoral neck, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric hip fracture were classified as having no bone-health medication, as baseline users (medication documented at admission), or as initiators within six months of the index fracture. Second hip fracture was assessed over fixed 1-, 2- and 5-year horizons. We estimated absolute risks, cumulative incidence accounting for death as a competing risk, and multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models.

**RESULTS**: Overall, 1,051,020 patients were eligible for the 5-year analysis: 705,059 (67.1%) had no medication, 83,452 (7.9%) were baseline users and 262,509 (25.0%) initiated medication within six months. Five-year cumulative incidence of second hip fracture was 17.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] 17.1-17.3) with no medication, 14.1% (95% CI 13.8-14.4) among baseline users and 8.9% (95% CI 8.8-9.1) among initiators. In adjusted models, the hazard of second hip fracture was lower among baseline users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71, 95% CI 0.69-0.73) and initiators (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.37-0.39) than among patients with no medication.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Initiation of bone-health medication within six months of a first hip fracture was associated with a lower risk of a second hip fracture. Baseline users had intermediate risk, which may reflect confounding by indication, agent selection or adherence. These findings support early, coordinated post-fracture osteoporosis treatment; the observational design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery.

**METHODS**: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed.

**RESULTS**: Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025.

**CONCLUSIONS**: ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) approach defines safe zones for W-plate fixation of the anterior pelvic ring.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To define the procedure-specific surgical anatomy of the pre-symphyseal region relevant to W-plate fixation by characterizing the soft-tissue layers, identifying critical neurovascular structures, and defining quantitative safe zones for dissection and plate placement.

**METHODS**: Fresh-frozen adult cadavers underwent standardized low Pfannenstiel dissections reproducing the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) exposure required for W-plate fixation. Pre-symphyseal soft-tissue layers were sequentially dissected from the skin to the anterior pubic symphysis. The locations of critical neurovascular structures relative to the pubic midline and pubic tubercles were recorded, together with anatomical layers, dimensions of the prepubic ligamentous-aponeurotic complex, soft-tissue thickness, sex-related anatomical differences, and surgical safe zones.

**RESULTS**: Three reproducible anatomical layers were identified in ten specimens. The superficial layer contained the pre-symphyseal fat pad and superficial epigastric vessels. The intermediate layer contained the spermatic cord or round ligament, ilioinguinal and genitofemoral nerves, and suprapubic artery, with these critical structures located at a mean distance of approximately 3.2 cm from the midline. The deep layer was consistently formed by the Pyramidalis-anterior pubic Ligament-Adductor longus Complex (PLAC), which covered the anterior pubic symphysis and measured a mean of 4.6 × 3.1 cm. No critical neurovascular structure crossed the central trajectory corresponding to W-plate placement. Female specimens demonstrated greater preperitoneal soft-tissue thickness, whereas lateral surgical safe zones were narrower in male specimens.

**CONCLUSION**: The pre-symphyseal region demonstrated a reproducible three-layer surgical anatomy with a predictable distribution of critical neurovascular structures. Quantitative anatomic mapping defined procedure-specific safe zones for extrapelvic W-plate fixation and provided practical guidancefor surgical exposure, implant positioning, and avoidance of iatrogenic injury.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level IV, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Common acetabular fracture patterns in patients with femoroacetabular impingement.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: The incidence of acetabular fractures is rising, affecting both younger and elderly patient populations. Developmental abnormalities such as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and hip dysplasia alter hip biomechanics, potentially predisposing younger patients to fracture. FAI, resulting from a cam and/or pincer deformity, is common, affecting 25% of asymptomatic males and 5% of asymptomatic females, and has been linked to hip pain and early osteoarthritis. However, the relationship between FAI morphology and acetabular fracture pattern remains unclear.

**METHODS**: Patients, 18-55 years old, treated between 2005 and 2023 for acetabular fracture, hip dislocation, or femoral head fracture were reviewed for FAI morphology using the Judet and Letournel classification systems. Statistical comparisons were conducted using Fisher's exact tests and unpaired t-tests, with significance set at p < 0.05.

**RESULTS**: A total of 294 patients (72%) exhibited plain radiographic FAI morphology, while 115 (28%) served as controls. The most common fracture pattern in both groups was posterior wall (PW) fractures (23.1% FAI, 31.3% control). Male FAI patients were significantly more likely to experience transverse fractures (p = 0.032, OR=4.6) and posterior column plus PW fractures (p = 0.035, OR=2.5) than controls. Among FAI patients, posterior column fractures were significantly more likely to occur in females (p = 0.011, OR=19). A total of 31 (27.0%) control patients and 63 (21.4%) FAI patients experienced complications.

**CONCLUSIONS**: In our data set, FAI patients accounted for 72% of patients undergoing acetabular fracture ORIF. FAI patients most commonly sustained posterior wall fractures, but male FAI patients had a significantly higher rate of transverse and posterior column plus PW. FAI patients experienced a complication rate of 21.4% compared to 27.0% in non-FAI patients.

articles.title: Robotic navigation-assisted versus conventional freehand placement of the infra-acetabular screw in acetabular fracture surgery: A retrospective comparative study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: The infra-acetabular screw (IAS) is an important component of fixation constructs for complex acetabular fractures, but accurate freehand placement is technically demanding, and evidence on robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement remains limited. This study compared robotic navigation-assisted (RA) and conventional fluoroscopic freehand (CF) IAS placement in acetabular fracture surgery.

**METHODS**: In this retrospective study, 53 patients with acetabular fractures who underwent IAS fixation between June 2022 and July 2024 were included, 28 underwent RA placement using the HoloSight robotic navigation system and 25 underwent CF placement. The primary outcome was screw-placement accuracy, graded on postoperative CT according to the Lonstein criteria. Secondary outcomes included the number of guide-wire adjustments, fluoroscopy frequency, IAS insertion time, total operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture reduction quality, hip function, and complications.

**RESULTS**: The grade 0 (no cortical penetration) rate was higher in the RA group than in the CF group (96.4% [27/28] vs. 60.0% [15/25], p = 0.005). RA placement was associated with fewer guide-wire adjustments (0.07 ± 0.26 vs. 3.60 ± 1.15), fewer fluoroscopies (9.32 ± 1.66 vs. 21.28 ± 3.18), shorter IAS insertion time (10.36 ± 2.50 vs. 26.68 ± 4.11 min), shorter total operative time (134.54 ± 15.46 vs. 155.80 ± 18.48 min), and less intraoperative blood loss (468.21 ± 84.68 vs. 588.40 ± 80.76 mL) (all p < 0.001). The mean follow-up duration was 15.7 ± 2.0 months (range, 13-22 months). Reduction quality, hip function, and complication rates did not differ significantly between the two groups.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement was associated with significantly higher screw-placement accuracy and greater procedural efficiency than the conventional freehand technique, without compromising fracture reduction quality, hip function, or safety.

articles.title: Risk factors for complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures carries a substantial risk of postoperative complications, particularly surgical site infection, yet the relative contribution of fracture pattern and associated soft tissue injury to this risk remains incompletely defined.

**OBJECTIVE**: To describe the rate and spectrum of complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures and to identify factors independently associated with these complications, with particular attention to acute surgical site infection.

**METHODS**: Retrospective, single-center cohort study of 126 patients who underwent surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures between December 2014 and November 2024, reported in accordance with the STROBE statement. Candidate demographic, injury-related, and treatment-related exposures were compared against a composite primary outcome (any postoperative complication) and against acute infection using Fisher's exact test, Pearson chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and multivariable logistic regression.

**RESULTS**: Overall, 39 of 126 patients (31.0%) experienced at least one postoperative complication; chronic pain (22.2%) and acute surgical site infection (16.7%) were the most frequent individual components. In bivariate analysis, the presence of a Morel-Lavallée lesion at baseline was significantly associated with both the composite outcome (OR 12.65, 95% CI 1.42-112.27, p = 0.011) and acute infection (OR 12.12, 95% CI 2.06-71.37, p = 0.007); Young-Burgess fracture pattern was also associated with infection (p = 0.018). After multivariable adjustment for infection, a Morel-Lavallée lesion (adjusted OR 17.69, 95% CI 2.46-126.95, p = 0.004) and combined-mechanism fracture pattern (adjusted OR 8.25 versus anteroposterior compression, 95% CI 1.91-35.58, p = 0.005) remained independently associated with infection. Neither the presence, technique, nor surgical approach of posterior ring fixation was associated with any complication type, and time from injury to definitive fixation (median 13 days) showed no significant association with either outcome.

**CONCLUSION**: A Morel-Lavallée lesion identified at initial evaluation was associated with postoperative complications in bivariate analysis and, together with a combined-mechanism fracture pattern, remained an independent predictor of surgical site infection after multivariable adjustment. No statistically significant association was identified between posterior fixation technique and complication risk.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is used for life-threatening hemorrhage, but evidence has largely focused on acute outcomes. Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized.

**METHODS**: This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up. Forty-nine REBOA-treated patients were matched 1:1 to 49 non-REBOA patients by major Young-Burgess category, Injury Severity Score, and age. The primary outcome was functional status among hospital survivors, categorized as good/fair/poor. Deep surgical site infection (SSI) after definitive pelvic fixation was the key secondary outcome, and nonunion was exploratory. Main models used a propensity-score linear predictor based on age, Injury Severity Score, initial systolic blood pressure, and lactate.

**RESULTS**: Seventy-five patients survived hospitalization (30 REBOA; 45 non-REBOA); median follow-up was 19 months. Good/fair/poor outcomes were 16.7%/46.7%/36.7% in REBOA survivors and 51.1%/37.8%/11.1% in non-REBOA survivors. REBOA exposure was associated with worse functional status after adjustment (common odds ratio [cOR], 3.14; 95% CI, 1.11-8.92; P = 0.032). Among 68 definitive-fixation survivors, deep SSI occurred in 44.0% versus 9.3% (adjusted OR, 7.01; 95% CI, 1.88-31.07; P = 0.003); all observed events occurred within 60 days. Nonunion occurred in 26.7% versus 6.7% (adjusted OR, 9.09; 95% CI, 2.00-53.71; P = 0.004). Sensitivity analyses for deep SSI were directionally consistent.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Among hospital survivors, REBOA exposure was associated with poorer long-term functional recovery and a higher burden of deep SSI. Nonunion was more frequent but remained exploratory. These findings characterize a high-risk orthopaedic survivor phenotype but do not establish a direct causal effect of REBOA.

articles.title: The prevalence of mental health service use after long-term minor-to-moderate motor vehicle crash injury: a retrospective cohort study.
