Ultrasound-trained attendings used CTAP less frequently than non-ultrasound-trained attendings (57.8% vs 71.8%; aOR for non-ultrasound-trained physicians 1.86, 95% CI 1.18-2.93).

**CONCLUSION**: PIT exposure was associated with greater CTAP and lower ultrasound utilization in patients with renal colic, including among a prespecified lower-risk cohort. Ultrasound-trained physicians used ultrasound more frequently and CTAP less frequently in renal colic patients.

articles.title: Long-term survival following extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a two-center five-year analysis.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials have shown short-term benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the long-term durability of survival and neurological recovery after hospital discharge remains poorly defined. We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory VT/VF OHCA from two academic centers (University of Minnesota, USA, and Charles University, Prague) from January 2013 through December 2022. The primary outcome was 5-year survival. Secondary outcomes included neurological status by Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) and associations of age and discharge disposition with long-term outcomes. Among 728 patients treated with ECPR, 211 (29.0%) survived to discharge; 138 from Minnesota and 73 from Prague. Median follow-up was 3.9 years; 68 patients (32%) completed 5 years. No patients were lost to follow-up. Among hospital survivors, 76.9% and 67.2% were alive at 1 and 5 years, respectively, with most deaths occurring within 90 days of discharge. CPC 1-2 was present in 78.7% at discharge and remained high among survivors beyond 1 year (93.4-94.2%). Five-year survival declined by age from 91.6% for those between 18-39 years and 52.9% for >70 years. Discharge disposition also strongly stratified long-term prognosis. Among patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory OHCA, long-term survival was substantial, with approximately two-thirds alive at 5 years with favorable CPC in most. Younger age and discharge home or to acute rehabilitation identified subgroups with particularly favorable prognosis. These findings support the long-term durability of benefit among selected patients treated within established ECPR systems of care.

articles.title: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries: A 13-year retrospective review of injury characteristics, treatment, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries are rare but potentially devastating. Due to low incidence, optimal perioperative management remains poorly defined, and evidence is scarce. This study evaluates the injury characteristics, surgical treatment, age-specific functional outcomes, and challenges in this population.

**METHODS**: A retrospective review was conducted on 79 pediatric patients (mean age 6.84 ± 4.27 years; 67.1% male) who underwent surgical repair for flexor tendon lacerations between 2010 and 2023. Outcomes were assessed using Total Active Motion (TAM), Strickland score, grip/pinch strength, Semmes-Weinstein monofilament, two-point discrimination, and QuickDASH questionnaire, with a mean follow-up of 59.9 ± 32.8 months.

**RESULTS**: Zone 2 was the most common injury site (45.6%), with glass being the predominant mechanism (67.1%). Nerve injury was present in 35.4% of cases. Overall, good/excellent results were achieved in 81.9% (TAM) and 89.0% (Strickland) of patients. The 0-5 years age group had significantly lower Strickland scores than the 6-12 years group (74.28% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.05). Zone 5 injuries demonstrated significantly better outcomes than Zone 2 and 3 (p < 0.001). The overall complication rate was low (5.1%), with a rerupture rate of 2.5%.

**CONCLUSION**: Pediatric flexor tendon repairs yield favorable functional outcomes with low complication rates. Age-related differences in functional outcomes should be interpreted cautiously because of developmental differences in patient cooperation and age-dependent rehabilitation strategies. Concomitant nerve injury was associated with poorer functional outcomes. The modified Kessler technique remains a reliable repair method.

articles.title: Limb preservation and optimization: A whole-patient approach to comprehensive care after catastrophic extremity injuries.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: The objective of this study was to describe the Limb Preservation and Optimization Center's (LPOC) components and mechanisms in treating catastrophic extremity injuries and report the initial patient demographics, indications, and outcomes using data from an established registry.

**METHODS**: A retrospective observational study was performed including all patients entered in the LPOC registry since January 1, 2014. Patient demographics, injury types and treatments, and outcomes, including functional outcomes. Descriptive statistics were calculated to determine proportions, means, standard deviations, and ranges.

**RESULTS**: 992 patients were included with a mean final follow-up of 20.5 months (SD:22.1, range 0-114); 178 (17.9%) underwent an amputation. Of those who reported RTW, 164 patients (71.6%) reporting RTW at full capacity. Lower extremity injuries were most common (74.9%). Demographic, health insurance, living setting, and presentation variables were similar among LPOC patients. Fractures and soft tissue injuries predominated across all injury categories with fracture fixation and wound coverage treatments most common. Upper extremity joint injuries and all types of combined injuries were associated with the highest reoperation rates. Treatment failure rates ranged from 11% to 100% with fracture and bone-related injuries being associated with the most favorable outcomes across categories.

**DISCUSSION**: Fractures and soft tissue injuries were the primary types of problems affecting all patients utilizing the LPOC. Fracture fixation and wound coverage treatments were the most performed procedures. Return to the operating room to address the limb preservation and optimization goal was extremely common across categories such that patients may expect at least 4 reoperations. Patients return to some type of work 75-88%. Treatment failure rates varied from 11% to 100%, with fracture and bone-related injuries being associated with the most favorable outcomes across categories. Overall, the results are encouraging and will help shape care in these patients.

articles.title: Geography matters: Variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Geodemographic factors create divergent clinical patterns between urban and rural settings. Level-II trauma centers are a vital trauma-care infrastructure for both urban and rural communities. This study compares neck trauma patterns, resource utilization, and outcomes at these distinct geodemographic nodes.

**METHODS**: Retrospective analysis (2014-2024) of neck trauma at an urban center (UC, n = 65) and a rural center (RC, n = 60). Demographics, mechanism, treatments, interventions, and outcomes were analyzed.

**RESULTS**: RC patients sustained more blunt, transport-related multisystem trauma with higher ISS. UC patients predominantly presented with localized penetrating injuries. Rural patients had higher ICU admission rates, longer ICU stays, more transfers to level-I centers yet underwent fewer operative interventions, invasive airway procedures, and CT angiogrophy.

**CONCLUSIONS**: There are significant variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers. An "intervention paradox" exists were rural centers stabilize high-severity blunt trauma for transfer, while urban centers provide definitive care for penetrating wounds. These findings necessitate geodemographically tailored protocols. Understanding geodemographic variations is a critical aspect of optimizing trauma systems.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: II Retrospective cohort.

articles.title: Gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription after long bone fracture fixation is associated with increased 1-year nonunion.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Gabapentinoids are increasingly incorporated into multimodal analgesia after orthopaedic surgery, yet their impact on outcomes following fracture fixation remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between early postoperative gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription and clinical outcomes after operative fixation of closed long bone fractures.

**METHODS**: Using TriNetX, we identified opioid-naïve and gabapentinoid-naïve adults undergoing intramedullary or plate-and-screw fixation of isolated closed diaphyseal tibia, humerus, or femur fractures. Patients prescribed gabapentin or pregabalin and opioids within three days after surgery were compared with patients receiving opioids alone. Propensity score matching (1:1) incorporated demographics, medical comorbidities, fracture location, fixation method, mental health disorders, and substance use disorders. Primary outcomes were prolonged (30-90 days) and chronic (90-180 days) postoperative opioid use. Secondary outcomes included 30-day emergency department (ED) visits and readmissions, and 1-year nonunion and reoperation.

**RESULTS**: After matching, each cohort consisted of approximately 2000 patients (range, 1946-2012). Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with higher rates of prolonged (21.0% vs 16.1%; RR 1.31; p < 0.001) and chronic (9.8% vs 7.4%; RR 1.33; p = 0.007) postoperative opioid use. Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with fewer 30-day ED visits (25.1% vs 42.5%; RR 0.59; p < 0.001), while 30-day readmission rates were similar between cohorts (p = 0.174). One-year rates of nonunion (4.3% vs 1.9%; RR 2.21; p < 0.001) and reoperation (7.1% vs 4.2%; RR 1.68; p < 0.001) were significantly higher among patients receiving gabapentinoid-opioid therapy. In a sensitivity analysis that defined the opioid-only cohort based on the absence of gabapentinoid prescriptions during the first 3 postoperative days, rather than the 1-year postoperative medication window used in the primary analysis, the associations with prolonged and chronic opioid use and reoperation were no longer statistically significant, whereas the association with nonunion remained significant (RR 1.62; p = 0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with fewer ED visits and higher rates of prolonged and chronic opioid use, nonunion, and reoperation; in sensitivity analysis, ED visits and nonunion remained significant, whereas opioid use and reoperation did not. These findings suggest that potential short-term analgesic benefits may be offset by adverse long-term outcomes, warranting caution and further study of gabapentinoid-opioid prescribing for acute perioperative fracture pain.

articles.title: Timing matters: Delayed surgery increases mortality for blunt hollow viscus injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Immediate surgical exploration is recommended for suspected hollow viscus injury (HVI) following blunt trauma. However, diagnostic uncertainty can lead to delayed operative management. We aimed to evaluate if delayed bowel resection/repair (DBR), defined as ≥8 hours after emergency department arrival, was independently associated with increased mortality in blunt trauma patients. We also sought to identify risk factors associated with DBR.

**METHODS**: The Trauma Quality Improvement Program database (2017-2024) was queried for admitted adults with blunt abdominal trauma (abdomen abbreviated injury scale grade ≥2) who underwent bowel resection/repair. Patients who were transferred from another facility or died within 8 hours were excluded. Patients undergoing early bowel resection <8 hours (EBR) were compared with patients undergoing DBR (≥8 h). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between DBR and mortality, controlling for age, severe head and thoracic injury, intubation within 1 hour of arrival, injury to the small bowel, colon, or rectum, and blood transfusion within 4 hours.

**RESULTS**: Of 33,728 patients undergoing bowel resection/repair, 16,010 (47.5%) underwent DBR. The DBR cohort had lower rates of small bowel (49.6% vs. 53.9%, p<0.001) and colon (46.7% vs. 49.7%, p<0.001) injuries, but similar rates of rectal injury (4.4% vs. 4.1%, p=0.166). Injuries to the liver (26.8% vs. 20.8%), spleen (28.2% vs. 23.4%), and kidney (12.9% vs. 9.0%) were more frequent in the DBR cohort (all p<0.001). DBR patients had an increased associated risk of mortality (13.0% vs. 8.5%, OR 1.21, 95% CI: 1.12-1.30, p<0.001). Small bowel injury was the only independent factor with decreased associated risk of DBR (OR 0.93, CI: 0.89-0.97, p=0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: Delayed operative management for blunt HVI occurs more often in patients with solid organ injuries and is independently associated with increased mortality. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and timely surgical management of HVI.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Therapeutic/Care Management, Level IV.

articles.title: Defining the therapeutic window for ADAMTS13 modulation in early trauma-induced coagulopathy.
Hypoxia Paradox in Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Mechanistic Framework for Treatment Resistance.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES**: The clinical efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) in chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is increasingly established; yet, recent landmark randomized controlled trials consistently report only a 30% to 50% reduction in recurrence, implying that middle meningeal artery occlusion alone does not fully resolve the pathological microenvironment of the outer hematoma membrane. The mechanistic basis of this incomplete treatment response remains undefined.

**METHODS**: To develop a mechanistic framework for this clinical paradox, we performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review. Of 876 records identified across PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov, 47 underwent full-text review and 18 studies (16 clinical studies and 2 registry records) published through October 2025 were included, integrating clinical outcomes with pathological and molecular insights. A secondary analysis of a publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data set of normal human dural tissue was performed to map the cellular infrastructure underlying key molecular drivers.

**RESULTS**: CSDH progression is driven by an interconnected triad of inflammatory infiltration, pathological angiogenesis, and vascular hyperpermeability within the outer hematoma membrane. While MMAE suppresses these pathogenic programs by reducing middle meningeal artery-derived arterial supply, we propose that occlusion-induced ischemic stress may paradoxically stabilize hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, triggering compensatory angiogenesis in cases of incomplete devascularization, a mechanism we formally term the "hypoxia paradox". Secondary single-cell RNA sequencing analysis identified fibroblast-like and endothelial dural populations as the primary cellular platforms for this response, providing a translational cellular basis for the proposed framework.

**CONCLUSION**: The hypoxia paradox represents a testable mechanistic hypothesis, offering a coherent explanation for heterogeneous MMAE outcomes and generates specific, testable predictions regarding post-MMAE molecular signatures in the outer hematoma membrane. Prospective paired tissue sampling integrated with multimodal molecular analyses is essential to validate this model and advance CSDH management toward individualized, mechanism-guided therapy.

articles.title: Post-Traumatic Amnesia Testing for Suspected Concussion in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Among patients discharged from the ED after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), 16%-25% experience post-concussive symptoms for up to 3 months after injury. However, the assessment of mTBI in the ED is variable. A common tool for the assessment of mTBI in Australia is the Abbreviated Westmead Post-Traumatic Amnesia Scale (A-WPTAS). The aim of this study was to report the proportion of patients who were detected to have post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) following a head injury and whether this varied by reported loss of consciousness (LOC), age, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and mechanisms of injury.

**METHODS**: This was a single-centre, retrospective cohort study. Data were extracted from patients' electronic medical records. All patients presenting to the ED between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2021 with a head injury, documented results of A-WPTAS, and aged ≥ 18 years were included for analysis.

**RESULTS**: There were 6259 patients included, and 5746 (91.8%, 95% CI: 91.1%-92.5%) passed the A-WPTAS. -PTA was more frequent among patients who presented with GCS 13 or 14, male patients, those with low falls and presenting after hours. Among patients with documented LOC, the pass rate was 90.6% (95% CI: 88.8%-92.4%), and among those without LOC, it was 92% (95% CI: 91.3%-92.8%); p = 0.13.

**CONCLUSION**: PTA was detected in a small proportion of patients tested in the ED. PTA was associated with low initial GCS, but not with reported LOC. Among patients discharged from the ED, follow-up for persistent post-concussion symptoms is indicated.

articles.title: Can posterolateral tibial plateau fractures be treated with an anterolateral approach? A biomechanical study on novel plating concepts in artificial tibia models.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: The aim of this study was to evaluate biomechanically whether fixation of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures (PLTPFs) through the more accessible modified anterolateral approach and by using a newly designed lateral plate with or without posterior plate extension or supplemental anteroposterior screw fixation, can provide comparable stability to direct posterolateral buttress plating.

**METHODS**: PLTPFs were simulated on 40 artificial tibiae and subsequently fixed with 5 different plating techniques (n = 8), namely using Variable Angle Locking Compression Plate (VA-LCP) Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (VA Lateral), Variable Angle Optimized Locking Technology (VOLT) Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (VOLT Lateral), VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with Posterolateral Extension (Hug), VOLT Posterolateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (PL), and VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with two anteroposterior parallel 3.5 mm locking screws placed superiorly to the plate's lateral-to-medial rafting locking screws (Jail) using a dedicated guide block. Biomechanical testing was performed under progressively increasing cyclic loading to failure. Interfragmentary movements were monitored via motion tracking.

**RESULTS**: Fragment displacement and its posterior tilt over the first 40,000 cycles did not differ significantly between Hug, PL, and Jail (all p > 0.999). Hug, PL, and Jail outperformed VA Lateral significantly in terms of fragment displacement over 40,000 cycles (p ≤ 0.004). In addition, Hug was associated with significantly less fragment displacement versus VOLT Lateral (p = 0.018). Posterior fragment tilting over 40,000 cycles was significantly lower in Hug, PL, and Jail versus VA Lateral and VOLT Lateral (p ≤ 0.014). Hug, PL, and Jail demonstrated significantly higher cycles to clinical failure and corresponding loads at clinical failure than VA Lateral and VOLT Lateral (p < 0.001), with no significant differences among Hug, PL, and Jail (p > 0.999). For catastrophic failure, Hug demonstrated significantly higher values than all other groups (p ≤ 0.045).

**CONCLUSION**: From a biomechanical perspective, VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with Posterolateral Extension and VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate with supplemental jail screw fixation provide fixation stability comparable to VOLT Posterolateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with respect to fragment displacement, posterior tilt, and clinical failure. Whether PLTPFs could be addressed via the more accessible anterolateral approach without compromising the biomechanical stability of fracture fixation remains yet to be clinically validated. Standalone Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (VA-LCP or VOLT) performed inferiorly to their augmented alternatives.

articles.title: Where is trauma care delivered in New York state? A statewide analysis of distribution and outcomes by trauma center level.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Understanding where and how trauma care is delivered is critical to preventing and managing its disease burden. This study identified patterns in trauma care delivery by characterizing the relationship between trauma presentations and outcomes as a function of trauma center level, including trauma presentations at non-trauma centers.

**METHODS**: A retrospective review of trauma inpatients aged ≥ 15 years across New York State from 2016 through 2020 was performed, utilizing a comprehensive New York State all-payer data reporting system, the Statewide Planning and Research Cooperative System (SPARCS). The primary endpoint for this study was mortality. Secondary endpoints included overall complications, discharge dispositions, and hospital length of stay.

**RESULTS**: A total of 361,141 patients were included with 42.1% presenting to Level 1 and 37.3% to Non-Trauma Centers. Older adults were more frequently treated at Level 3 and Non-Trauma Centers, while younger patients and high-energy mechanisms (motor vehicle crashes and penetrating injuries) were more commonly managed at Level 1 and Level 2 Centers. The association between trauma-center group and mortality varied by severity of illness (SOI) (interaction p < 0.0001). Compared with Level 3 and Non-Trauma Centers, Level 1 and 2 Centers had higher adjusted mortality odds among hospitalizations with major SOI (aOR 1.43, 95% CI 1.12-1.83) and extreme SOI (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.18-1.62), with no significant difference in moderate SOI (aOR 0.83, 95% CI 0.62-1.11).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Differences in outcomes across trauma center levels are strongly influenced by case mix and severity. These findings highlight opportunities to improve triage, resource allocation, and system-level performance.

articles.title: Variations in hip fracture management at trauma vs. non-trauma centers.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Hip fractures represent a growing public health burden. Optimal management relies on timely surgical intervention coordinated by multidisciplinary care and appropriate resource availability, all of which may vary between hospital settings. Differences between trauma hospitals and non-trauma hospitals may influence outcomes, yet these variations have not been well characterized.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of hip fracture cases over a 2-year period (October 2022 to August 2024), comparing patient and procedural characteristics between a Level II trauma hospital (TH) (n = 104) and a non-trauma hospital (NTH) (n = 31). Polytrauma patients were excluded. Data were extracted from the electronic medical record (EMR). Primary outcomes were hospital length of stay (LOS) and time from admission to surgery. Group comparisons utilized chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U or Welch t-tests for continuous variables, as appropriate. A multivariable random forest model was used to evaluate predictors of operative duration.

**RESULTS**: ASA physical status distribution differed significantly between facilities (p = 0.03), with more ASA > 2 patients at the NTH (76.6% vs. 65.7%). Osteosynthesis was performed in 73.3% of NTH cases and 82.2% of TH cases; arthroplasty comprised 26.7% and 17.8%, respectively. LOS differed significantly by facility (p < 0.01), with a shorter mean stay at the NTH (4.3 vs. 5.9 days; mean difference, -1.73 days). Time to surgery also differed significantly (p < 0.001): mean 846 min (95% CI, 615-1078) at the NTH vs. 2686 minutes (95% CI, 2391-2981) at the TH. In multivariable modeling, procedure type was the dominant predictor of operative duration (permutation importance 0.686), followed by payer type (0.216); facility identity contributed minimally (0.034) after accounting for case mix.

**CONCLUSION**: Hip fracture care differed meaningfully between the TH and NTH within the same health care system. The NTH demonstrated significantly shorter time to surgery and LOS despite treating a proportionally higher-acuity patient population by ASA classification. These findings highlight opportunities for optimizing timeliness and resource allocation in hip fracture management across hospital settings and questions whether THs are the optimal location to treat these injuries.

articles.title: Segmental phase angle as predictor of activities of daily living and muscle health in patients with osteoporotic fracture A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: This study aimed to determine whether the segmental phase angle is associated with clinical outcomes such as activities of daily living (ADL), muscle strength, and skeletal muscle mass in patients with osteoporotic fractures.

**METHODS**: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with osteoporotic fractures admitted to convalescent rehabilitation wards. The primary outcome was a Functional Independence Measure motor (FIM-motor) score at discharge, and secondary outcomes were handgrip strength and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) at discharge. Multivariate analysis was used to adjust for confounders and to examine the association between segmental phase angle and outcome.

**RESULTS**: A total of 115 subjects (97 women, age 81.0 ± 10.0 years) were included in the study. The median baseline phase angle was 3.6°. Multiple regression analysis adjusted for confounders showed that arm phase angle was independently positively associated with handgrip strength (β=0.250, P < 0.001) and SMI (β=0.215, P < 0.001) at discharge. Leg phase angle was independently positively associated with FIM-motor score (β=0.077, P = 0.045), handgrip strength (β=0.174, P < 0.001), and SMI (β=0.154, P < 0.001) at discharge.

**CONCLUSIONS**: The leg phase angle was associated with ADL, muscle strength, and skeletal muscle mass in patients with osteoporotic fractures at discharge. Segmental phase angle may be a useful indicator for considering intervention methods in patients with osteoporotic fractures.

articles.title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Emergency care capacity remains critically limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in rural areas where specialists and infrastructure are scarce. In Cambodia, stroke and ischemic heart disease are leading causes of mortality, and trauma burdens are increasing alongside rapid infrastructure development. Evidence on emergency equipment availability and frontline provider skills at the facility level in rural provinces remains limited.

**METHODS**: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment was conducted across all seven public referral hospitals in Battambang Province, Cambodia, in January 2023. Emergency equipment availability was evaluated through structured interviews and direct visual confirmation against the World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care. Clinical skill examinations were administered to physicians (two scenario-based cases: acute stroke with airway compromise; traumatic injury with tension pneumothorax and intra-abdominal bleeding) and nurses (a Basic Life Support [BLS] scenario assessed in pairs). Hospitals were stratified by Complementary Package of Activities (CPA) level: CPA1 (basic care only), CPA2 (including surgery and intensive care), and CPA3 (highest provincial level).

**RESULTS**: At Complementary Package of Activities (CPA)1 (basic care only) hospitals, intubation equipment and 12-lead electrocardiogram were each available in only 25% of facilities. None had a crash cart, blood transfusion capacity, basic metabolic panel, or coagulation testing. In the stroke scenario, airway patency was confirmed by 28.6% of physicians at CPA1 hospitals, compared with 70.0% at CPA2 hospitals (including surgery and intensive care), 57.1% at the CPA3 hospital (highest provincial level), and 75.0% at the Provincial Health Department. In the trauma scenario, no physician at CPA1 hospitals correctly performed spinal immobilization with the spine kept straight or thoracentesis at the correct anatomical location. Among 38 nurse pairs, 97.4% initiated chest compressions promptly, but only 21.1% demonstrated correct compression technique, and 13.2% provided effective bag-valve-mask ventilation. Deficiencies in equipment and clinical skills were most pronounced at CPA1 hospitals.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Emergency care capacity in Battambang Province was substantially limited, with the greatest deficiencies at CPA1 hospitals. Recurrent low-cost training and targeted strengthening of basic emergency care should be prioritized at lower-level facilities.

articles.title: A scoping review evaluating artificial intelligence applications across various injury prevention domains.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly utilized for injury prevention across diverse clinical and community settings including machine learning (ML). This scoping review aimed to synthesize the current literature on the applications and predictive performance of AI across multiple injury prevention domains.

**METHODS**: This scoping review searched five major databases, including PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, and the Cochrane Library, to identify studies evaluating AI applications for injury prevention published through May 2026. Eligible studies included original U.S.-based, English-language research across self-harm and suicide, abuse and violence, fall prevention, and sports injury prediction. Studies were excluded if they lacked measurable prevention outcomes or sufficient methodological detail, or focused on injury treatment rather than prevention, to ensure relevant and interpretable evidence for synthesis.

**RESULTS**: Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. ML models generally outperformed or matched traditional screening methods for self-harm and suicide prediction (AUC 0.81-0.82), while multimodal approaches achieved the highest predictive accuracy (AUC 0.90). In abuse and violence prevention, AI predicted intimate partner violence with an AUC of 0.88 and identified cases before formal disclosure. AI also improved fall risk assessment by accurately categorizing patient risk levels, predicting future falls, and mitigating fall injuries through wearable airbag technology. ML models predicted future sports-related injuries (AUC 0.76-0.84), while identifying modifiable risk factors including workload, strength deficits, prior injury burden, and concussion history.

**CONCLUSION**: ML-based prediction showed promise for risk stratification in self-harm, suicide, intimate partner violence, and recurrent victimization. Additionally, AI predicted fall risk and identified athletes at risk for future sports-related injuries while detecting modifiable risk factors, including workload, prior injury burden, and strength deficits. Although these findings suggest that AI and ML may have potential applications in supporting earlier risk identification, informing targeted prevention strategies, and facilitating more personalized approaches to injury prevention, the limited available evidence warrants careful interpretation.

articles.title: Enhanced wound healing potential of a carboxymethyl cellulose/gelatin-based hydrogel containing decellularized amniotic membrane and Matricaria chamomilla extract: A multifunctional composite dressing.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Chronic wound healing remains a complex biological process influenced by excessive inflammation, oxidative stress, microbial invasion, and insufficient tissue regeneration. Therefore, the design of multifunctional biomaterials that integrate structural support with biological regulation has emerged as a promising strategy in advanced wound care. This study sought to develop a composite hydrogel incorporating decellularized amniotic membrane (dAM)-derived extracellular matrix components alongside Matricaria chamomilla extract, with the goal of achieving enhanced regenerative and therapeutic outcomes.

**METHODS**: A CMC/GEL-Chamomilla-dAM hydrogel was prepared using decellularized dAM and subsequently evaluated in terms of its physicochemical and biological characteristics. The effectiveness of the decellularization process and preservation of ECM components were first examined, followed by characterization of hydrogel morphology, rheological properties, swelling and degradation behavior, and pH stability. Its biological performance was further assessed through hemocompatibility, cytocompatibility, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial assays, as well as a full-thickness wound model.

**RESULTS**: Incorporation of dAM and chamomile extract resulted in a stable hydrogel with favorable physicochemical and biological characteristics. The decellularization procedure removed 97.9% of the DNA. The resulting composite hydrogel exhibited an average pore size of 78.3 ± 9.8 µm, and all hydrogel formulations showed hemolysis rates below the 5% threshold accepted for blood-contacting biomaterials, with values ranging from 3.8% to 4.5%. The composite hydrogel also supported enhanced fibroblast viability (109.6 ± 11.3%) and demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial activities against wound-associated pathogens. In vivo, treatment with CMC/GEL-Chamomilla-dAM accelerated wound closure (85.7 ± 6.3% at day 14) and supported tissue regeneration, outperforming both the dAM-containing hydrogel (78.9 ± 9.9%) and the commercial DuoDERM dressing (58.9 ± 4.5%), as evidenced by improved re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and early signs of tissue remodeling.

**CONCLUSION**: The CMC/GEL-Chamomilla-dAM hydrogel combines a dAM-containing extracellular matrix scaffold with chamomile-derived bioactive compounds, creating a favorable microenvironment for tissue repair. The addition of chamomile extract to the dAM-containing scaffold was associated with improved wound closure and tissue regeneration. While the present study design does not permit a definitive assessment of synergy between dAM and chamomile, these findings support the potential of this formulation as a multifunctional biomaterial platform for advanced wound healing applications.

articles.title: Union rate and time to union following platelet-rich plasma therapy in fracture nonunion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Fracture nonunion remains a challenging clinical problem associated with prolonged disability and repeated surgical interventions. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been proposed as a biological adjunct to enhance bone healing; however, clinical evidence remains inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of PRP in the management of fracture nonunion.

**METHODS**: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO Registration: CRD420261366849). PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies evaluating PRP in fracture nonunion and reporting union rate or time to union were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to compare PRP with control interventions. Risk ratios (RR) were calculated for union rates and standardized mean differences (SMD) for time to union. Additional single-arm analyses were performed to estimate pooled outcomes in PRP-treated cohorts.

**RESULTS**: Twenty-one studies comprising 877 patients were included. Two comparative studies (n = 119) demonstrated a higher likelihood of union with PRP (RR 1.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.36, p < 0.05) without significant heterogeneity. Six studies (n = 250) showed no significant difference in time to union between PRP and control groups (SMD -0.72, 95% CI -1.48-0.05), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 85%). In PRP-only analyses, the pooled union rate was 0.86 (95% CI 0.76-0.94; I² = 61%) across seven studies (n = 150), and the pooled mean time to union was 6.08 months (95% CI 4.26-7.90; I² = 100%) across eight studies (n = 187).

**CONCLUSION**: PRP was associated with higher union rates in the limited comparative evidence, although no statistically significant difference in time to union was demonstrated. Heterogeneity in PRP protocols, methodological limitations, and the small comparative evidence base limit the certainty of these findings. PRP may have a potential role as a biological adjunct in fracture nonunion management, but further well-designed randomized controlled trials are required before definitive clinical recommendations can be made.

articles.title: Comprehensive treatment approaches for traumatic tattoos: An integrative review.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Traumatic tattoos result from an injury that drives external pigment into the dermis. They often affect exposed sites such as the face and extremities. Pigment may persist for years within the dermis, complicating management and limiting cosmetic outcomes. Consequently, no optimal treatment technique has been identified, and long-term data remain limited.

**AIM**: To synthesise evidence on treatments for traumatic tattoos and to evaluate effectiveness and outcomes over the past 25 years.

**DESIGN**: Integrative review with narrative synthesis following Whittemore and Knafl's five stages.

**DATA SOURCES**: An electronic search of PubMed and Scopus was conducted from 2000 to November 2025 to identify original peer-reviewed research focusing on treatments for traumatic tattoos and to evaluate their effectiveness and outcomes.

**RESULTS**: Twenty-eight articles met the inclusion criteria, representing 27 studies, comprising largely case reports and small series, with one retrospective cohort study. Treatment approaches are grouped into laser-based therapies, acute or delayed mechanical debridement (including hydrosurgery), and other surgical or mechanical methods. Q-switched Nd:YAG, ruby, alexandrite, fractional CO

**CONCLUSION**: Best practice appears to combine prompt removal of foreign material in the acute phase with appropriate laser therapy for established traumatic tattoos. The overall evidence is low-level and heterogeneous, and prospective comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Patterns of depression screening, referral, and behavioral health follow-up after orthopaedic trauma.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: To evaluate baseline patterns of depression, behavioral health referral, and behavioral health treatment among orthopaedic trauma patients at a Level I trauma center.

**METHODS**: Design: Retrospective Cohort, Secondary Analysis Setting: Single Level 1 Trauma Center Patient selection criteria: Adult orthopaedic trauma patients who completed an ambulatory postoperative visit between September 2024 and November 2025. Outcome measures and comparisons: Demographic variables, PHQ-9 screening results, injury characteristics, behavioral health referral patterns, and referral completion were extracted from institutional electronic health records. Primary outcomes were the proportion of patients screening positive for depression (PHQ-9 >10), with moderately severe to severe depression (PHQ-9 ≥15) triggering behavioral health referral, and subsequent referral completion rates. Secondary outcomes included referral patterns by injury mechanism and six-month orthopaedic complications or unplanned healthcare utilization.

**RESULTS**: Among 528 patients, 44.7% (236/528) screened positive for depressive symptoms, and 21.2% (112/528) demonstrated moderately severe to severe depression triggering a behavioral health referral. 33.9% (38/112) of referred patients completed a behavioral health visit compared with 67.6% (115/170) of referred non-trauma orthopaedic patients. The severe depression cohort was on average younger and more likely to be female, black, and have Medicare/Medicaid insurance status. Injury Severity Score did not differ significantly across depression categories. Patients with ballistic injury had significantly higher rates of positive depression screening (51.9% vs. 41.8%; P = 0.040) and behavioral health referrals (34.0% vs. 18.0%; P < 0.001) than non-ballistic patients, though referral completion did not differ significantly by mechanism (25.0% ballistic vs. 38.2% non-ballistic; P = 0.198). Infectious and wound complications and unplanned healthcare utilization, driven by emergency department visits for wound complications, were significantly higher among patients who screened positive and failed to complete their referral compared with those who screened negative for depression (P < 0.001).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Significant gaps exist in the depression care cascade for orthopaedic trauma patients. Referral completion rates were approximately two-fold lower than non-trauma orthopaedic subspecialties, and referral non-completion was associated with significantly higher rates of infectious complications and unplanned healthcare utilization. Targeted, navigation-based interventions addressing structural barriers at the point of care are needed to close the gap between depression identification and treatment engagement in orthopaedic trauma.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level III.

articles.title: Awake intubation in a Japanese tertiary emergency department: a single-center retrospective descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Evidence on awake intubation in emergency departments (EDs) is limited. We aimed to describe patient characteristics, intubation indications, procedural practices, and outcomes for awake intubation in the ED.

**METHODS**: This single-center retrospective descriptive study included consecutive adult patients who underwent tracheal intubation at a tertiary ED in Japan from April 2020 through December 2025. Patients intubated during cardiac arrest were excluded. Operational definition for awake tracheal intubation required topical upper airway anesthesia, no neuromuscular blockers before or during the initial attempt, and documented preservation of consciousness and spontaneous ventilation throughout that attempt. Outcomes included first-pass success, adverse events related to airway management, and definitive airway management, including rescue.

**RESULTS**: Eighty-four patients underwent awake tracheal intubation, representing 5.5% of intubations in patients without cardiac arrest (84/1531). Upper airway infectious diseases were present in 54 patients (64.3%); airway-related indications accounted for 63 cases (75.0%). Emergency physicians performed 79 initial attempts (94.0%); a flexible bronchoscope was used initially in 49 patients (58.3%). First-pass success occurred in 63 patients (75.0%; 95% confidence interval, 64.4%-83.8%). Seven patients (8.3%) experienced adverse events related to airway management. Eighty patients (95.2%) achieved definitive airway management without a surgical airway. Four patients (4.8%) required a surgical airway, all after first-pass failure.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Awake intubation, performed primarily by emergency physicians, was used to manage upper airway infectious diseases with actual or impending obstruction in a tertiary ED. A flexible bronchoscope was used initially in over half of cases and most patients were intubated without a surgical airway.

articles.title: From Tamburello to track reform: neurosurgical lessons and motorsport safety after Ayrton Senna's Formula 1 accident in 1994.
articles.abstract: Ayrton Senna, a three-time Formula 1 (F1) motorsport world champion from Brazil, met his tragic demise at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix F1 race in Imola, Italy, after a devastating accident led to multiple skull base injuries and severe traumatic brain injury. The purpose of this study was to analyze the life and legacy of Senna, including his accident and injuries, forensic details surrounding his death, and the subsequent safety review and implementation of improved safety standards throughout F1 racing. Senna's accident, which was found to have resulted from steering column failure, helped shape the future of motorsport safety. Investigations into safety protocols and vehicle mechanisms revealed several shortcomings, resulting in multifaceted reform including introduction of the head and neck support device, changes in helmet design, track and barrier safety improvements, more stringent approval requirements for affiliated medical staff, new driver extrication measures, and a new seat belt standard. Senna's death further accelerated multidisciplinary safety reforms in motorsport medical care and prompted reassessments of acute on-track medical evaluations, specifically neurological evaluations. The combined contributions of Senna's close friends (including Dr. Eric Sidney "Sid" Watkins), the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile, and the Instituto Ayrton Senna have aided in developing robust safety standards that have prevented such tragedies for decades.

articles.title: Impact of pre-existing bleeding disorders on outcomes in patients with traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major global public health problem. This study aimed to evaluate the association between pre-existing bleeding disorders and clinical outcomes among patients with TBI. We hypothesized that pre-existing bleeding disorders would be associated with worse outcomes following TBI.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2021-2023 National Inpatient Sample (NIS) to evaluate the association between pre-existing bleeding disorders and clinical outcomes among patients aged 15 years or older hospitalized with TBI.

**RESULTS**: Mortality was significantly higher in the bleeding disorder group (13.9% vs. 4.8%; p < 0.001), the median length of stay was longer (5 days vs. 3 days; p < 0.001), median hospitalization costs were substantially higher (US $20,582 vs. US $13,515; p < 0.001), and discharge home was less frequent (44.8% vs. 61.6%; p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, comorbidity burden, injury severity, and other clinically relevant covariates, pre-existing bleeding disorders remained independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.99-2.69).

**CONCLUSION**: Pre-existing bleeding disorders were independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality after TBI. Patients with these disorders also experienced worse clinical outcomes. Early recognition and appropriate hemostatic assessment may support individualized management in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Prevalence of Persistent Severe Hypertension and Rates of Treatment Among Pregnant Patients in the Prehospital Setting.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) contribute to maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality and require time-sensitive intervention. In April 2025, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), in collaboration with the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) and the National Association of EMTs (NAEMT), published new guidelines on the prehospital management of elevated blood pressure in pregnancy. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent severe hypertension among pregnant patients encountered by prehospital clinicians, characterize baseline frequency of pre-guideline treatment, and establish a benchmark to inform implementation of these guidelines.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using the 2024 ESO Data Collaborative public release research dataset (January 1 to December 31, 2024). We identified all 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients documented as pregnant beyond 20 wk of gestation. We excluded injury-related encounters and patients outside the World Health Organization-defined childbearing age range (15 to 49 years). Consistent with the new guidelines, we defined persistent severe hypertension as at least two documented blood pressure measurements with systolic blood pressure ≥ 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 110 mmHg. We defined guideline-adherent treatment as administration of both magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) and an antihypertensive medication (labetalol, hydralazine, or nifedipine).

**RESULTS**: We identified 39,546 eligible 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients beyond 20 wk of gestation. The prevalence of persistent severe hypertension was 3.1% (

**CONCLUSIONS**: Approximately 1 in 32 pregnant patients beyond 20 wk of gestation encountered by prehospital clinicians had persistent severe hypertension. In the year prior to dissemination of the 2025 ACOG, NAEMSP, and NAEMT-supported guidelines, fewer than 1% received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. These findings establish a national benchmark and identify opportunities to improve prehospital care through protocol development, medication availability, clinician education, and implementation of updated guidelines.

articles.title: Association Between Craniotomy and Outcomes in Patients With Acute Subdural Hematoma: Analysis of a Nationwide Trauma Registry in Japan.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE**: The benefits of surgery remain unclear in less severe cases of acute subdural hematoma (ASDH). We aimed to investigate the association between surgical intervention and outcomes in patients with ASDH.

**METHODS**: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Japan Trauma Data Bank between January 2019 and December 2023. Patients age 18 years and older with large supratentorial ASDH (>50 cm3, >1 cm thick) and a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 6 to 15 at hospital arrival were included. One-to-one propensity score matching was performed to compare patients who underwent craniotomy with those who did not. Study outcomes included survival to hospital discharge and favorable neurological outcomes.

**RESULTS**: Overall, 1808 patients (median age, 79 years; 64.9% male) from 83 hospitals were included, and 46.6% underwent craniotomy. Craniotomy rates ranged from 0.0% to 83.3% (median, 46.2%) across hospitals. Propensity score matching identified 610 matched patients with and without craniotomy. Patients who underwent craniotomy had a significantly higher survival rate (77.2% vs 62.6%; within-hospital difference, 14.7%; 95% CI, 9.6%-19.8%); however, no significant difference was observed in the proportion of favorable neurological outcomes at discharge (16.1% vs 17.9%; within-hospital difference, -1.9%; 95% CI, -7.5% to 3.7%). Subgroups analyses demonstrated significant interactions between craniotomy and both age and GCS scores, with greater benefit observed in patients age 65 years and older (difference, 3.9% [<65 years] vs 17.1% [≥65 years]) and in those with a GCS score of 6 to 12 (difference, 27.8% [GCS 6-12] vs -6.1% [GCS 13-15]).

**CONCLUSION**: In patients with large ASDHs, craniotomy was significantly associated with improved survival, particularly among patients age 65 years and older and those with lower GCS scores (6-12). A uniform approach based solely on hematoma thickness may be suboptimal. Instead, surgical decision-making needs to adopt a more individualized approach that incorporates age and neurological severity.

articles.title: Hospital-level Variation in Medical Debt After Acute Traumatic Injury.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: To determine whether the treating hospital contributes to patients' medical debt following injury.

**SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA**: Trauma patients often have little or no choice in where they receive care. However, variation in hospital billing and collection practices, and their association with patient medical debt, remains poorly characterized.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult trauma patients hospitalized from January 2019 to December 2020 at 29 Level I and II trauma centers within a statewide quality collaborative. Trauma registry data were linked to quarterly consumer credit reports from 12 months preinjury through 18 months postinjury. The primary outcome was change in medical debt in collections from baseline to months 9-18 postinjury. Hierarchical mixed-effects models with empirical Bayes shrinkage and reliability adjustment estimated risk-adjusted hospital-level changes, adjusting for demographics, injury severity, and treatment intensity. Hospitals were classified as outliers if 95% confidence intervals for observed-minus-expected differences excluded zero.

**RESULTS**: Among 20,613 patients (mean age 63 y; 49% female; 82% non-Hispanic White), mean change in medical debt was $314 (SD $3464). Four hospitals (14%) were high outliers, generating $365-$566 more debt per patient than expected, while 4 (14%) were low outliers, generating $292-$676 less. Low-outlier hospitals cared for younger, lower-income, and higher-risk patients yet produced less debt than predicted. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Substantial hospital-level variation in postinjury medical debt persists after adjustment for clinical and demographic factors. Billing, financial assistance, and collection practices may represent modifiable targets to reduce financial hardship after trauma.

articles.title: The first 72 hours of acute pancreatitis: patterns of variability in early clinical decision-making.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To assess real-world adherence to evidence-based international guidelines in the early management of acute pancreatitis (AP), and to identify how variability in clinical decision-making is distributed during the first 72 h of care.

**METHODS**: This multicentre, cross-sectional survey was conducted among consultant physicians and trainees in General Surgery, Gastroenterology, and Emergency Medicine actively practising in Catalonia, Spain. An expert-reviewed 21-item questionnaire assessed self-reported practices across eight key domains of early AP management relative to international consensus recommendations (IAP/APA and WSES). Factors associated with guideline adherence were analysed using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.

**RESULTS**: A total of 165 clinicians clinicians completed the survey. Self-reported adherence to key recommendations was low, particularly for target-directed fluid resuscitation and early oral feeding, while more than half of respondents reported antibiotic use in the absence of confirmed infection. Crucially, clinical practice variability was not uniformly distributed. The greatest differences were observed in time-sensitive, treatment-related decisions, particularly fluid resuscitation and nutritional strategies, where adherence varied significantly according to clinician experience and hospital size. In contrast, antibiotic use showed no significant variation across subgroups, indicating a consistent and widespread deviation from guideline recommendations. On multivariable analysis, overall adherence was independently associated with clinician experience (p = 0.035) and hospital size (p = 0.009), but not with medical speciality or clinician age.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Early AP management showed substantial variation in self-reported practice across clinical domains. Variability was greatest for time-sensitive therapeutic decisions, whereas antibiotic overuse appeared to represent a widespread pattern of non-concordant practice across subgroups. Structured local pathways and decision-support tools may help reduce these implementation gaps.

articles.title: WSES-PSOGI-SICO evidence-infomed guidelines on surgical emergencies in patients with peritoneal surface malignancies: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and structured expert consensus.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Peritoneal surface malignancies (PSM) are primary or secondary neoplastic deposits involving the peritoneum and are commonly associated with colorectal, gastric, appendiceal, gynecological, pancreaticobiliary, and other intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal cancers. Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is one of the most frequent and clinically consequential emergency presentations in this population, yet diagnostic and therapeutic pathways remain heterogeneous. We aimed to develop evidence-informed recommendations for emergency management of MBO in patients with PSM by integrating a systematic review, meta-analysis and a structured international expert consensus process.

**METHODS**: This systematic review, meta-analysis, and Delphi consensus followed PRISMA, Cochrane, and relevant MOOSE reporting principles. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 2025 (English language). Five predefined PICO/PIRT questions addressed: (1) the diagnostic role of CT, plain abdominal X-ray, or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; (2) nonoperative medical management versus surgical or endoscopic therapy; (3) surgical versus endoscopic treatment after failure of nonoperative management; (4) bowel resection versus stoma or bypass in surgical candidates; and (5) endoscopic stenting versus endoscopic ultrasound-guided bypass with lumen-apposing metal stents in endoscopic candidates. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and MINORS for non-comparative studies; certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses (REML) produced odds ratios (OR), mean differences (MD), pooled means, or pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was summarized using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Evidence profiles informed statements voted on by the WSES-PSOGI-SICO expert panel during the 2025 WSES Congress.

**RESULTS**: No comparative diagnostic study evaluated abdominal X-ray or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; two small retrospective CT-based series supported contrast-enhanced CT for mapping obstruction and excluding urgent complications, but no diagnostic meta-analysis was possible. For medical versus procedural treatment, medical management was associated with lower morbidity (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.07-0.39) and shorter length of stay (MD - 9.48 days, 95% CI - 12.65 to -6.32), while success, mortality, and overall survival remained inconclusive. For surgery versus endoscopy, surgery showed higher clinical success (OR 2.57, 95% CI 1.47-4.50), whereas endoscopy shortened hospital stay (MD 3.35 days, 95% CI 1.46-5.23); mortality did not differ (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.70-1.49). Among surgical options, resection showed a signal toward higher perioperative mortality than bypass or ostomy (OR 3.55, 95% CI 1.45-8.68). Endoscopic stenting showed a pooled clinical success rate of 0.71 (95% CI 0.62-0.79), whereas evidence on LAMS was limited to one retrospective study. All guideline statements reached 100% agreement among voting participants.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Despite the low certainty of available evidence, integration of systematic review findings with expert consensus provides a structured international framework to support decision-making in emergency presentations of PSM-related MBO. These consensus-based recommendations are intended to assist clinicians in harmonizing care across peripheral and referral hospitals, while emphasizing individualized multidisciplinary judgement and the need for future higher-quality evidence.

articles.title: Rural Pathologies: A Late Presentation Special.
articles.abstract: Patients in rural and remote Australia often present later and with more advanced disease compared to major and regional cities. Drawing on experience as a junior doctor in the Cape and in rural emergency departments, this article explores how geographic isolation, limited resources, health literacy challenges and inequities in access shape these presentations. Cases include a critically unwell patient managed overnight in a makeshift intensive care bay when weather delayed retrieval, a family of young children with Norwegian Scabies, and a partial finger amputation complicated by weekend staffing shortages. The article reviews Australian evidence on sepsis, scabies and its link to rheumatic heart disease and trauma outcomes, all of which tend to be more challenging to manage. Timely care in rural and remote communities depends on early recognition, clear communication and close collaboration between rural generalists, FACEMs, retrieval services and specialist teams.

articles.title: Predictors of 30-day mortality and complications following surgical treatment of pathologic hip fractures.
articles.abstract: Pathologic hip fractures present complex challenges and are associated with higher postoperative complication rates and mortality compared with non-pathologic fractures. This study aimed to compare 30-day outcomes between pathologic and non-pathologic hip fracture patients and identify factors associated with 30-day mortality and postoperative complications among patients with pathologic hip fractures using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. A retrospective analysis was conducted from 2006 to 2023. Patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing hip fracture surgery were included. Patients with non-pathologic hip fractures were compared with those with pathologic hip fractures. Univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with pathologic hip fracture 30-day mortality and complications. Among 204,675 hip fracture patients, 6159 (2.9%) had pathologic hip fractures. Patients with pathologic hip fractures had higher rates of 30-day mortality (7.8% vs. 5.1%, p < 0.001), any postoperative complication (35.3% vs. 30.2%, p < 0.001), cardiac/transfusion complications (27.5% vs. 22.2%, p < 0.001), renal complications (0.5% vs. 0.3%, p = 0.017), and venous thromboembolic complications (3.4% vs. 1.7%, p < 0.001). Infectious complications and neurological complications were not significantly different between groups. In multivariable analyses, prominent protective factors associated with decreased 30-day mortality included absence of disseminated cancer (aOR 0.4, p < 0.001), independent functional status (aOR 0.2, p < 0.001), and absence of sepsis history (aOR 0.4, p = 0.02). Thrombocytopenia (aOR 1.9, p < 0.001) and anemia (aOR 1.9, p < 0.001) were prominent risk factors for 30-day mortality. Thrombocytopenia and anemia were also significant risk factors for any complications and cardiac/transfusion complications. These findings underscore the importance of comprehensive preoperative assessment and multidisciplinary care to optimize outcomes for patients with pathologic hip fractures. Patients with multiple risk factors for adverse postoperative morbidity and mortality should receive appropriately tailored care.

articles.title: Video-assisted resident education is associated with improved ankle joint reduction: A prospective controlled study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Proper fracture reduction and splinting technique is critical for soft tissue protection and fracture stability in the acute management of ankle fractures. However, residency education for acute ankle fracture reduction and splinting techniques remains poorly standardized and streamlined. This study evaluated the effect of implementing a video-assisted ankle fracture management education program administered to first-year orthopaedic residents on ankle joint reduction and splint quality.

**METHODS**: This was a prospective controlled study conducted at a single level I trauma center. All consecutive ankle fractures (OTA/AO: 4F, 44) requiring the placement of a bivalved short leg cast or AO splint from January 1, 2019, to June 30th, 2022 were included. Exclusion criteria included skeletal immaturity, missing imaging, delayed fracture presentation more than two weeks from injury, concurrent ipsilateral injury/polytrauma interfering with ankle reduction, open fracture, or ankle fractures treated without an AO splint or cast. The primary outcome was joint reduction quality defined as radiographic post-reduction tibiofibular overlap, tibiofibular clear space, and medial clear space. Secondary outcomes included splint padding thickness and ankle dorsiflexion angle to assess splint quality.

**RESULTS**: A total of 280 consecutive ankle fracture cases were included for evaluation of splint quality: 111 in the intervention group (mean age 46; [range 14-92]; 44% female) versus 169 in the control group (mean age 44; [range 14-90]; 41% female). Comparable injury severity was observed between groups. In the supination-external rotation IV (SER4) and type IV-equivalent (SER4e) subgroup, there was significant improvement in joint reduction quality in the intervention group as compared to control (55% versus 36%, respectively; Risk Ratio: 1.52, [95% CI: 1.03-2.25], p = 0.04). In the entire cohort, splint padding thickness was not significantly improved in the intervention group (p > 0.05), however, there was a significant increase in the percentage of ankles splinted in an appropriately dorsiflexed position (p = 0.03).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Implementation of video-assisted ankle fracture management education program was associated with improvements in overall ankle joint reduction quality. While the clinical significance of the improvements observed in ankle reduction remains yet to be established, orthopaedic surgery residency programs should consider incorporating video technique guides into their educational curricula.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level II, Therapeutic Study.

articles.title: Disparities in investigation of physical abuse among trauma patients.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Physical abuse is a significant public health issue in the United States, leading to poor health outcomes such as chronic illness, depression, and substance abuse. Research regarding how the medical system addresses physical abuse in the overall adult population is scarce. The objective of this study was to assess disparities in investigation of physical abuse among adult trauma patients.

**METHODS**: This is a retrospective analysis of the 2017-2019 American College of Surgeons-Trauma Quality Program database. This study included all adult patients (≥18 years) who had a report of physical abuse by the medical team to authorities. Chi square and multivariate analysis were applied where appropriate to assess which characteristics showed disparities in investigation rate.

**RESULTS**: On univariate analysis, there were disparities with regard to age, mechanism, race, ethnicity, payment method, and mental health or substance use disorder. On multivariate analysis, male sex, non-penetrating trauma, age ≥70, American Indian race, and presence of a mental health disorder were associated with decreased odds of investigation. Non-elderly adult patients made up a disproportionate amount of abuse victims.

**CONCLUSIONS**: This study shows significant disparities in the escalation of a physical abuse report to an official investigation in the trauma setting. The authors recommend increased advocacy and resource allocation for these vulnerable populations in the clinical setting as well as further research regarding to what extent patient choice versus discretion of authorities influences these disparities. The authors also recommend a larger research focus on non-elderly adult victims of abuse.

articles.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI.

**MAIN TEXT**: Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent.

**CONCLUSIONS**: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes.

**HIGHLIGHTS**: VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.

articles.title: 24-hour risk updating for major ICU complications after severe trauma: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Conventional trauma prognostic models rely primarily on admission data and cannot account for subsequent physiological response to treatment. We evaluated whether routinely collected physiological information available at 24 h provides incremental prognostic information for major intensive care unit (ICU) complications in severely injured patients.

**METHODS**: We conducted a prospective cohort of adults with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score [ISS] ≥ 15) admitted to the ICU between January 2024 and April 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of major respiratory, hemodynamic, renal, or septic complications during the ICU course. TRISS was compared with an admission ridge model incorporating ISS, Glasgow Coma Scale, hemoglobin, lactate, and international normalized ratio, and a 24-h updated ridge model additionally incorporating 24-h lactate and change in creatinine. Performance was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

**RESULTS**: Among 109 patients, median ISS was 29 (IQR 20-38), and 73 (67.0%) developed major ICU complications. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 for TRISS, 0.873 for the admission model, and 0.887 for the 24-h updated model; Brier scores were 0.178, 0.140, and 0.131. Compared with the admission model, the 24-h updated model improved performance (ΔAUC 0.016, 95% bootstrap interval 0.004-0.030; ΔBrier - 0.010, - 0.017 to - 0.005). Twenty-four-hour lactate and creatinine change were the strongest contributors to the update.

**CONCLUSION**: In severely injured ICU patients, incorporating physiological evolution during the first 24 h refined admission-based prognostic assessment. Lactate and creatinine trajectories provided incremental information for major ICU complications during the ICU course. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Maternity versus non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
**RATIONALE**: Substantial uncertainty exists regarding how healthcare system factors, especially care setting types, affect the uptake and implementation of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy screening in practice. Evidence suggests that the care environment may influence diagnostic processes.

**OBJECTIVES**: To assess the effectiveness of maternity and non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus or diabetes in pregnancy.

**SEARCH METHODS**: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) up to April 2026, and for controlled non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs) up to December 2025. We also searched CENTRAL to identify ongoing trials.

**ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**: We included RCTs and planned to include cluster-RCTs and NRSIs, but we did not find any. Eligible participants were pregnant women being screened for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) or diabetes in pregnancy. We defined maternity healthcare settings as those specialising in care for pregnant, birthing, and postpartum individuals, with appropriate screening protocols, and non-maternity healthcare settings as general medical environments lacking a focus on pregnancy and women's care. We considered any screening format (e.g. risk-factor-based screening) and any diagnostic test (e.g. one- and two-step oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT)).

**OUTCOMES**: Critical health service outcomes were compliance with screening and follow-up guidelines, diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy, maternal emergency department visits during pregnancy, maternal antenatal hospitalisation, length of maternal hospitalisation, length of neonatal hospitalisation, and care accessibility. Critical maternal outcomes included hypertensive disorders, maternal death, intensive care admissions, hyperglycaemia requiring pharmacological treatment, infections, and postpartum glucose intolerance, including progression to diabetes, within 15 years after birth. Critical child-related outcomes encompassed perinatal death, neonatal intensive care admissions, preterm birth, neonatal hypoglycaemia, large-for-gestational-age, shoulder dystocia, and birth trauma. Further critical and important outcomes not included in the summary of findings tables can be found in the full text.

**RISK OF BIAS**: We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs. We had planned to use ROBINS-I version 2 to assess bias in the NRSIs if we had identified any.

**SYNTHESIS METHODS**: We used standard Cochrane methodology. We planned to synthesise results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible (inverse-variance or Mantel-Haenszel approaches; fixed-effect model). We used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence for each outcome.

**INCLUDED STUDIES**: We included one RCT with 781 participants: 390 were randomised to screening in a maternity healthcare setting and 391 were randomised to screening in a non-maternity healthcare setting. Except for screening compliance, trialists evaluated all outcomes using a per-protocol analysis instead of by original randomised groups. This approach created substantial disparities in sample sizes between settings and largely nullified the methodological protections typically provided by a randomised design. The trial evaluated screening for GDM only. We did not identify any ongoing studies or studies awaiting classification.

**SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS**: Health service outcomes Screening in a maternity healthcare setting may increase compliance with screening and follow-up guidelines (risk ratio (RR) 1.69, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.53 to 1.87; 781 participants) and may improve care accessibility, assessed as time to access antenatal diabetes care, measured in days (mean difference (MD) -4.70, 95% CI -6.03 to -3.37; 690 participants), both with low-certainty evidence. We are very uncertain about the effect of screening in a maternity healthcare setting versus a non-maternity healthcare setting on diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy (RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.60 to 2.01; 690 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and length of neonatal hospitalisation (MD 0.04, 95% CI -0.57 to 0.65; 690 participants; very low-certainty evidence). No direct evidence was available on screening for diabetes in pregnancy as distinct from GDM. No data were reported on maternal emergency department visits, maternal antenatal hospitalisation, length of maternal hospitalisations, and costs. Maternal outcomes We are very uncertain about the effect of screening in a maternity healthcare setting versus a non-maternity healthcare setting on pre-eclampsia (RR 1.24, 95% CI 0.56 to 2.75; 690 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The following outcomes were not reported: eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, maternal death, admission to intensive care, hyperglycaemia requiring pharmacological treatment, infections, and postpartum glucose intolerance. Child-related outcomes We are very uncertain about the effect of screening in a maternity healthcare setting versus a non-maternity healthcare setting on: stillbirth or foetal death (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.08 to 9.93), admission to neonatal intensive care (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.59 to 1.71), preterm birth (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.41 to 2.71), neonatal hypoglycaemia (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.23 to 3.59), large-for-gestational-age (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.04), shoulder dystocia (RR 0.15, 95% CI 0.01 to 3.70), and birth trauma (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.08 to 9.93), all with 690 participants each and very low-certainty evidence. An effect estimate for neonatal death was not estimable (maternity setting: 0/475; non-maternity setting: 0/215).

**AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS**: There is insufficient evidence to determine whether screening for gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy in maternity healthcare settings compared with non-maternity healthcare settings improves health service, maternal, or child-related outcomes. Low-certainty evidence from a single study indicates that screening in maternity healthcare settings may result in a reduction in time to access antenatal diabetes care and may increase compliance.
