The effects on other outcomes remain unknown. Conducting studies using intention-to-treat analyses could bridge existing research gaps, enhancing effect estimates and certainty.

**FUNDING**: This Cochrane review was funded by the World Health Organization (WHO) and the UNDP-UNFPA-UNICEF-WHO-World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development and Research Training in Human Reproduction (HRP).

**REGISTRATION**: Protocol available via PROSPERO: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251108692.

articles.title: Predictors of Return to Work Following Major Trauma in New Zealand.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: This study aimed to identify physical and psychological predictors of return to work (RTW) in a cohort of major trauma patients in New Zealand.

**METHODS**: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Christchurch Hospital involving patients identified from the New Zealand Major Trauma Registry. Full-time workers (n = 130) who sustained major trauma between 2016 and 2020 completed self-reported questionnaires assessing post-injury work capacity, PTSD (PCL-5), anxiety and depression (HADS) and perceived social support (MSPSS). Univariable and multivariable analyses were performed to determine predictors of decreased RTW following injury.

**RESULTS**: Older age, longer hospital length of stay (LOS) and ICU admission were all significantly associated with decreased RTW in the univariable analysis. Probable anxiety and depression were also significantly associated with decreased RTW, while meeting PTSD thresholds did not yield a significant association. In the final multivariable analysis, older age (OR 1.08, p < 0.01), longer LOS (OR 1.04, p = 0.048) and those with probable depression (OR 5.29, p = 0.01) were significantly associated with decreased RTW.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Probable depression is a strong, independent psychological predictor of reduced RTW following major trauma. These findings highlight the need for integrated post-trauma care models that incorporate routine psychological screening and early intervention to address both the physical and psychological needs of patients suffering from major trauma.

articles.title: Variation in Pediatric Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Survival After In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Development and Validation of a Survival Model for Risk-Standardized Survival Rates: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To develop and internally validate a multivariable prediction model for survival to hospital discharge after pediatric extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and to use this model to derive risk-standardized survival rates (RSSRs) and quantify between-hospital variation in outcomes.

**DESIGN**: Retrospective multicenter cohort study.

**SETTING**: Hospitals contributing to the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry between 2020 and 2023.

**PATIENTS**: Children (< 18 yr) treated with ECPR for IHCA.

**INTERVENTIONS**: None.

**MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS**: Eligible patients were identified from the ELSO Registry and split into derivation (N = 1060) and validation (N = 317) cohorts using a hospital-stratified split to preserve within-hospital clustering. Survival prediction models were derived using penalized logistic regression with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. A full-event model incorporating 14 routinely available clinical variables demonstrated fair discrimination (area under the curve, 0.728 in the derivation cohort and 0.678 in the validation cohort) and good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, 0.995; Brier score, 0.222 in the validation cohort). This model was embedded in a multilevel logistic regression model to generate hospital-level RSSRs for centers reporting five or more ECPR cases. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio, which was 1.30 (95% CI, 1.11-1.93), indicating significant differences in survival likelihood between centers after adjusting for patient-level risk.

**CONCLUSIONS**: In a large, international cohort of pediatric ECPR patients, we developed and internally validated a clinically interpretable model for survival to hospital discharge. The model performance as a discriminator likely limits its use as a standalone tool for clinical decision-making. However, strong internal calibration allowed for determination of hospital-level RSSRs, which revealed significant inter-hospital variability. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of developing a risk-adjustment model capable of estimating hospital-level RSSRs. Additional external validation and evaluation of residual case-mix differences are needed before such models can be used for benchmarking across pediatric ECPR centers.

articles.title: Ischemic severity rather than ischemic time is associated with major limb complications in traumatic popliteal artery injury: A retrospective case series.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Although prolonged ischemic time is considered a key determinant of limb loss in traumatic popliteal artery injury (PAI), it does not fully explain the variability in clinical outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether ischemic severity at presentation is associated with major limb complications in PAI.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively reviewed patients with blunt PAI treated at a single trauma center between 2013 and 2025. Ischemic severity was assessed using the Rutherford classification and the presence of collateral circulation on computed tomography angiography (CTA). Patients were categorized into mild ischemia (Rutherford grade I-II) and severe ischemia (Rutherford grade III). Outcomes included extensive soft tissue defects requiring reconstruction and amputation.

**RESULTS**: Twenty-one limbs were included. Thirteen limbs were classified as mild ischemia and eight as severe ischemia. Collateral circulation was preserved in 17 limbs and absent in 4 limbs. The time to arterial reconstruction was comparable between groups. No major soft tissue complications occurred in the mild ischemia group. In contrast, 5 of 8 limbs with Rutherford grade III developed extensive soft tissue defects (p = 0.006). Absence of collateral circulation was also strongly associated with adverse outcomes, with all limbs without collateral flow developing major soft tissue complications (p = 0.002), despite a shorter time to revascularization.

**CONCLUSION**: Ischemic severity at presentation, particularly Rutherford grade III and absence of collateral circulation on CTA, is associated with major limb complications in traumatic PAI, whereas ischemic time alone may be insufficient to predict outcomes.

articles.title: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings.

**METHODS**: Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks.

**RESULTS**: A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 min of traumatic cardiac arrest.

**CONCLUSION**: In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

articles.title: Opportunistic assessment of bone quality using CT-derived hounsfield units in postmenopausal women with femoral trochanteric fractures.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: CT-derived Hounsfield unit (HU) measurements may provide an opportunistic assessment of bone density when dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is difficult to obtain during acute treatment of femoral trochanteric fractures. We compared three femoral-head regions of interest (ROIs) and explored their ability to identify markedly low total hip bone mineral density (BMD).

**METHODS**: This single-center retrospective study included 87 women aged ≥ 65 years with AO/OTA type 31A1 (excluding A1.1) or 31A2 femoral trochanteric fractures treated with intramedullary nailing. Admission CT HU values were measured in three femoral-head ROIs on coronal and axial images and compared with contralateral hip DXA T-scores measured approximately 1 week after surgery. Pearson correlations and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. The prespecified total hip T-score thresholds were ≤ -2.5 and ≤ -3.3; the latter was used as an operational definition of markedly low BMD in this study.

**RESULTS**: Coronal whole-femoral-head HU values (ROI 1) showed a moderate correlation with total hip T-scores (r = 0.569). For the ≤ -2.5 threshold, 74 women met the criterion and only 13 did not; the ROI 1 coronal AUC was 0.841. For the ≤ -3.3 threshold, 51 women met the criterion and 36 did not. A coronal ROI 1 threshold of < 158.7 HU had an AUC of 0.765 (95% CI, 0.660-0.870), sensitivity of 84.3% (43/51), and specificity of 66.7% (24/36) for identifying a total hip T-score ≤ -3.3.

**CONCLUSION**: Whole-femoral-head HU values were moderately associated with DXA-derived T-scores in this cohort. Admission CT may help flag patients with markedly low BMD, but the threshold showed limited specificity and requires external validation. Its effect on surgical decisions or clinical outcomes was not assessed.

articles.title: Thoracic irrigation in managing traumatic hemothorax: A concise review of techniques and practice variations.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Retained hemothorax following tube thoracostomy occurs in up to one-third of thoracic trauma patients, often necessitating additional interventions. Thoracic irrigation has emerged as a potential adjunct to improve pleural drainage. The objective of this concise review is to evaluate the role of thoracic irrigation in the management of traumatic hemothorax by highlighting current standards of care and variations in techniques.

**METHODS**: This review searched five search engines, screening studies published before September 26, 2025. Studies focusing on thoracic irrigation in the setting of trauma and hemothorax were included.

**RESULTS**: A total of six studies were included. Thoracic irrigation in the management of traumatic hemothorax showed significantly lower odds of secondary intervention (OR: 0.16, p < 0.001) and shorter hospital length of stay (7 days vs. 9, p = 0.04) in patients who received thoracic irrigation compared with standard chest tube drainage. Most patients underwent irrigation using medium to large-bore tubes, although one study showed no association between tube size and outcomes. Patients receiving ≥ 1000 milliliters (mL) of irrigation had more hospital-free days compared to those receiving < 1000 mL (p = 0.007), while another study found no significant differences.

**CONCLUSION**: Thoracic irrigation shows promise as an adjunct to tube thoracostomy in managing post-traumatic hemothorax, with evidence of reduced retained collections, fewer secondary interventions, and shorter hospital stays. Studies are needed to achieve standardized thoracic irrigation techniques and develop more comprehensive and consistent evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Do radiographic surrogates of pre-bend appropriateness influence outcomes after titanium elastic nailing in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures?
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: To investigate whether radiographic technical parameters reflecting pre-bend appropriateness are associated with radiographic and clinical outcomes after titanium elastic nailing (TEN) in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures.

**METHODS**: This retrospective cohort included 85 children aged 5-11 years treated with TEN between 2015 and 2025. Constructs were classified as criteria-met (n = 38) or criteria-unmet (n = 47) using nail symmetry, a bend apex-fracture apex distance ratio ≤ 10%, and a metaphyseal spread ratio ≥ 50%. Separate exploratory multivariable models evaluated the composite classification and its components, adjusting for clinical and technical covariates.

**RESULTS**: Median coronal angulation was lower in the criteria-met group (2.0° vs 5.0°; p = 0.005). The adjusted mean difference (criteria-unmet minus criteria-met) was 3.42° (95% CI 0.98-5.87; p = 0.007). Other group comparisons were inconclusive. Exploratory component analysis associated greater spread with greater limb length discrepancy (3.61 mm per increase of 10 %age points; 95% CI 1.81-5.40; q = 0.002), although technical parameters were highly correlated. The complication risk ratio for criteria-unmet versus criteria-met constructs was 1.41 (95% CI 0.45-4.48).

**CONCLUSION**: Meeting the study-specific radiographic criteria was associated with lower coronal angulation, but its clinical importance remains uncertain. Overlapping criteria, correlated technical parameters, and limited precision preclude conclusions of equivalence or definitive independent effects.

articles.title: Scapular fracture and risk of great vessel injury in geriatric blunt trauma: A TQIP analysis.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Scapular fractures are markers of high-energy blunt thoracic trauma and may indicate severe intrathoracic injury. Despite the substantial mortality linked with great vessel injuries (GVI), data specifically examining scapular fracture and GVI in the geriatric population remain limited. We hypothesized that scapular fracture, particularly when accompanied by concomitant thoracic fractures, is independently associated with GVI in geriatrics with blunt trauma.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program (ACS-TQIP) database (2017-2023). Patients aged ≥ 65 years with a blunt mechanism of injury and AIS severity 2-5 in the neck, thorax, or upper extremity were included. GVI was defined using specific AIS codes for major thoracic and cervical vessels. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated association between scapular fracture patterns and GVI, including isolated scapular fractures, those with concomitant sternal, rib or flail chest fractures. Models adjusted for age, sex, race, mechanism, ISS, shock index, and modified frailty index. Vessel-specific analyses were also performed. Primary outcome was GVI. Secondary outcomes were mortality and LOS.

**RESULTS**: A total of 677,134 patients were included. Median age was 76 [70-82] years; 54.1% were female. Scapular fractures were identified in 5.0% of patients and GVI in 0.7%. In multivariable regression, isolated scapular fracture was associated with lower odds of GVI (aOR 0.783, 95% CI 0.704-0.871, p < 0.001), while scapular fracture with sternal fracture was associated with significantly higher odds (aOR 1.423, 95% CI 1.122-1.806, p = 0.004). Among vessel-specific analyses, subclavian artery injury demonstrated the highest association with scapular fracture (aOR 1.527, 95% CI 1.113-2.094, p = 0.009). GVI was associated with markedly higher in-hospital mortality (25.1% vs. 4.2%; OR 7.726, 95% CI 7.234-8.251, p < 0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: In geriatric blunt trauma, isolated scapular fracture is not an independent predictor of GVI. After a fall, a scapular fracture without a sternal fracture does not by itself suggest a missed vascular injury. In contrast, combined scapular and sternal fractures represent a high-risk pattern that warrants a heightened index of suspicion and a low threshold for CT angiography, with particular attention to the subclavian vessels.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

articles.title: Early fecal diversion versus no initial diversion in blunt open pelvic fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of pelvic infection and mortality.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: The benefit of routine early fecal diversion in blunt open pelvic fractures remains uncertain. We examined its association with pelvic infection and short-term mortality.

**METHODS**: MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 12 August 2026, with citation searching. Comparative observational studies were synthesized using crude risk ratios (RRs), REML random-effects models, modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals, and Mantel-Haenszel sensitivity analyses without continuity correction. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed ROBINS-I risk of bias and GRADE certainty.

**RESULTS**: Eighteen observational comparative reports were retained. Potential cohort overlap prevented a valid unique overall participant total. Eight cohorts contributed to broad pelvic infection (171 participants; seven estimable): RR 0.78 (95% CI 0.35-1.70; I²=19.6%). The stricter outcome-definition analysis included five cohorts (88 participants; four estimable): RR 0.72 (95% CI 0.07-6.97). Excluding two author-reported infected hematomas through an existing replacement sensitivity gave RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.34-2.05). Eight mortality cohorts (236 participants) yielded RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.33-2.07; I²=19.0%). Post-2006 evidence remained inconclusive for infection (three cohorts; RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.009-58.85) and mortality (five cohorts; RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.27-5.26). Diversion was preferentially used in patients with more severe injuries. All reports had Serious or Critical risk of bias; certainty was very low.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Available evidence does not establish a reduction in pelvic infection or short-term mortality with routine early diversion. Confounding, inconsistent outcome ascertainment, and imprecision prevent causal conclusions or exclusion of benefit in selected high-risk injuries.

articles.title: Orthopedic trauma in patients with opioid use disorder: Current concepts in perioperative management.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is an important challenge in orthopedic trauma, where acute injury intersects with preexisting opioid exposure, tolerance, complex pain, and barriers to continuity of addiction treatment. OUD has been associated with higher rates of complications, readmission, and treatment disruption, yet OUD-specific perioperative management remains inconsistently incorporated into orthopedic trauma practice. This review synthesizes the epidemiology, outcomes, and perioperative management evidence for this population.

**METHODS**: A clinically oriented current concepts review synthesized peer-reviewed literature, prioritizing studies published from 2013 onward. PubMed and Embase were searched, supplemented by Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, and manual review of reference lists from relevant articles. Studies examining perioperative outcomes, multimodal analgesia, and management of medications for OUD (MOUD) relevant to orthopedic trauma were included; studies limited to pediatric, elderly, or prenatal populations were excluded.

**RESULTS**: Preinjury opioid exposure is common among orthopedic trauma patients, whereas formally diagnosed OUD is less prevalent, affecting approximately 1% of operative trauma patients and up to 2.3% of patients with open lower-extremity fractures. OUD and opioid-related disorders are associated with higher rates of infection, nonunion, revision, prolonged hospitalization, and readmission. Consensus guidance and observational evidence support continuation of evidence-based MOUD, individualized opioid supplementation, multimodal nonopioid analgesia, regional anesthesia when appropriate, and early coordination with addiction and acute pain services. Guideline-based approaches to postoperative opioid prescribing, tapering, and patient education are also summarized.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Orthopedic trauma patients with OUD require individualized, multidisciplinary perioperative care. The strongest available evidence supports preservation of OUD treatment, multimodal analgesia, early addiction and pain consultation, and coordinated discharge planning rather than either opioid avoidance or opioid-only treatment. The review concludes with the authors' recommendations for the operating surgeon, including in-hospital and outpatient tapering plans, management of requests for additional opioids, and patient education.

articles.title: Latent class phenotypes and emergency department disposition for patients with traumatic subdural hematoma and midline shift.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Guidelines recommend surgical evacuation for traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) with >5 mm midline shift (MLS), but emergency department (ED) triage varies between the operating room (OR) and the intensive care unit (ICU). We investigated whether ED disposition to the OR versus ICU was associated with differences in outcomes and whether distinct patient phenotypes modified these associations.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively identified adult patients from the ACS TQIP dataset with traumatic SDH, MLS >5 mm, and ED disposition to either the ICU or OR. We defined patient phenotypes using latent class analysis (LCA) and investigated associations between ED disposition and outcomes (inpatient mortality, favorable discharge) using risk-adjusted hierarchical logistic regression. We tested for interaction between patient phenotype and ED disposition and repeated these analyses among patients undergoing an ICU stay ≥1 day and cranial surgery.

**RESULTS**: Among 9582 patients, 29% (N = 2794) were triaged to the OR. Two LCA-informed phenotypes emerged: class 1 (older-mild injury) and class 2 (younger-severe injury). There was an interaction between ED disposition and patient phenotype, such that younger-severe patients had lower mortality with OR triage (P < 0.001). In the subgroup of 4573 patients (48%) with ≥1 day of ICU stay who underwent cranial surgery, there was a significant interaction between OR triage and the older-mild phenotype indicating increased mortality (P = 0.003).

**CONCLUSIONS**: For traumatic SDH with MLS >5 mm, triage the OR was associated with improved outcomes only among younger, severely-injured patients, while older, mildly-injured patients may benefit from early ICU stabilization. These findings support phenotype-guided ED triage strategies to optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Fatal Opioid-Like Toxidrome Associated With a 7-Hydroxymitragynine Kratom Product.
articles.abstract: Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) use has increased in the United States, with the market shifting from traditional leaf preparations to concentrated products containing concentrated or chemically processed alkaloids such as 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-HMG) and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. These formulations may deliver supraphysiologic opioid-receptor agonist doses with poorly characterized toxicity. A 42-year-old man was found dead at home after reportedly ingesting 3 tablets of a commercial "7-HMG" product and several beers. Postmortem examination revealed purge fluid at the mouth and nose, severe bilateral pulmonary edema, distended bladder, and no evidence of trauma or injection drug use. Quantitative analysis of the remaining tablet showed 29 mg 7-HMG and 0.58 mg mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, with minimal mitragynine. Postmortem blood contained 37.3 ng/mL 7-HMG and 76 ng/mL mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, whereas gabapentin and other medications were present at subtherapeutic concentrations. Compared with an estimated 1 to 4.5 mg 7-HMG in a typical high dose of dried kratom leaf powder, this ingestion delivered approximately 87 mg 7-HMG (19-fold to 87-fold greater 7-HMG exposure than a high-dose botanical leaf preparation). Given the high μ-opioid receptor activity of 7-HMG and its in vivo conversion to the even more potent opioid agonist mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, the postmortem findings are most consistent with a fatal opioid-like toxidrome associated with exposure to concentrated kratom alkaloids. This case illustrates the emerging risk posed by new kratom-branded products containing purified or chemically enriched alkaloids at doses far exceeding traditional preparations.

articles.title: Associations Between Diagnostic Blood-Based Biomarkers and Neuroimaging Findings in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
**STUDY OBJECTIVE**: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a prevalent and resource-intensive injury in the emergency department (ED). The blood-based biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) have demonstrated diagnostic potential for acute structural brain injury. Our objective was to clinically validate a US Food and Drug Administration-approved plasma test to aid in the identification of intracranial injury in patients with mTBI presenting to the ED and assess its integration with existing protocols.

**METHODS**: This single-center validation study enrolled 104 adult patients with suspected mTBI undergoing head computed tomography (CT) for evaluation between October 2023 and June 2024 at a Level I trauma center. Peripheral blood draw was completed within 12 hours postinjury and processed at the hospital clinical laboratory. Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values for the test were calculated and compared with a standard clinical decision rule (Canadian Head CT Rule). ED length of stay and diagnostic turnaround times were examined.

**RESULTS**: Within the cohort (n=104), 83 patients had elevated biomarker levels (GFAP >30 pg/mL or UCH-L1 >360 pg/mL), and 11 patients had intracranial injury identified on CT. The combination plasma test demonstrated high sensitivity (0.91 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.59 to 1.00]) but low specificity (0.22 [95% CI 0.14 to 0.31]) for predicting intracranial injury on CT with low positive predictive value (0.12 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.21]) and high negative predictive value (0.95 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.00]). These findings are consistent with prior studies (pooled sensitivity 0.97 [95% CI 0.95 to 0.98]; specificity 0.28 [95% CI 0.23 to 0.34]). False-positive cases (78%) were older than true-negative cases (median 72 years [interquartile range (IQR) 54 to 83] versus 58.5 years [IQR 38.25 to 66]). Median turnaround time for the GFAP/UCH-L1 test was 2 hours faster than head CT (1.09 hours [IQR 0.87 to 1.65] versus 3.28 hours [IQR 2.37 to 4.70]).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Blood biomarkers for mTBI have potential as an initial rule-out tool for intracranial injury prior to obtaining CT imaging; however, large multicenter studies are needed to clarify its impact on ED resource utilization, length of stay, and acute and long-term costs and benefits to patients and health care systems.

articles.title: Micromobility Injury Patterns and Resource Use in US Trauma Centers.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Micromobility-related injuries increasingly contribute to trauma care, but differences in injury patterns and resource use across bicycle, e-bike, and e-scooter injuries remain incompletely characterized. We compared injury severity, injury patterns, and resource use among injured riders presenting to participating trauma centers.

**STUDY DESIGN**: We queried the American College of Surgeons National Trauma Data Bank (2023-2024) for injured bicycle, e-bike, and e-scooter riders ≥18 years. The primary outcome was severe injury (Injury Severity Score ≥16). Secondary outcomes included serious regional injuries (Abbreviated Injury Scale ≥3), craniofacial fractures, operative and critical care resource use, and in-hospital mortality.

**RESULTS**: Among 47,102 injured riders, 32,100 (68%) rode bicycles, 8,744 (19%) e-bikes, and 6,258 (13%) e-scooters. Compared with bicycle riders, e-scooter riders had lower risk of severe injury (aRR 0.93, 95% CI 0.87-0.99) but higher risk of serious head/neck injury (aRR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04-1.17). Risks of serious chest (aRR 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.82) and extremities/pelvic girdle injuries (aRR 0.92, 95% CI 0.86-0.99), emergency surgery (aRR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.87), early transfusion (aRR 0.71, 95% CI 0.54-0.94), and in-hospital mortality (aRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.94) were lower. Helmet use was associated with lower craniofacial fracture risk, most strongly among e-scooter riders (aRR 0.49, 95% CI 0.41-0.58).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Among injured riders presenting to participating trauma centers, e-scooter injuries were associated with lower overall severity and resource use than bicycle injuries but greater serious head/neck injury risk. Helmet use was associated with lower craniofacial fracture risk, supporting continued helmet promotion.

articles.title: Prehospital Analgesia in Trauma: A Systematic Review of Current Evidence.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Pain management is integral to prehospital trauma care. However, due to multiple challenges, pain is frequently undertreated despite important physiologic and psychologic implications. Among these challenges is uncertainty regarding the safety and effectiveness of pharmacologic agents administered enroute. We aimed to evaluate the level of evidence for the safety and effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adult trauma patients.

**METHODS**: An electronic database search of PUBMED, Google Scholar, Cochrane Library, Embase and Scopus for studies that reported on safety and/or effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adults (aged > 15 years) from January 1st, 2014, to January 1st, 2026. Non-original studies, paediatric studies, studies of non-pharmacologic agents or non-systemic administration (e.g., topical) were excluded.

**RESULTS**: Seventeen studies, involving 17,115 patients, met the inclusion criteria. The studies consisted of 6 randomized controlled trials, 5 retrospective cohort studies, one retrospective comparative study, one retrospective observational study, two prospective observational studies, one prospective cohort study and one non-randomized clinical trial. Agents included opioids, ketamine, methoxyflurane and paracetamol. Apart from one study of opioid therapy, no drug-attributed serious adverse events were reported. Minor adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness, dysphoria, agitation and drowsiness were common. All agents demonstrated effectiveness to varying levels.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Current evidence demonstrates an overall favourable safety and effectiveness profile of prehospital analgesia for adult trauma patients. However, considering the wide prehospital prevalence of injury-related pain, evidence is limited by scope, methodology and variations of treatment protocols.

articles.title: Association between transfer pathways and functional outcomes in severe trauma patients: a cohort study using the PATOS registry.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Optimal transport strategies for severe trauma remain debated, particularly in Asia. We evaluated the association between interhospital transfer and functional outcome and its consistency across Asian trauma systems.

**METHODS**: This cohort study used the Pan-Asian Trauma Outcome Study (PATOS) registry. We analyzed patients with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score > 15) in South Korea, Malaysia, and Vietnam (2015-2022). The exposure was interhospital transfer (Transfer) versus direct transport to a definitive-care hospital (Direct). The primary outcome was a favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≤3). The primary model was a country fixed-effect logistic regression estimating the total effect; country-specific estimates and a transport-pathway × country interaction were pre-specified.

**RESULTS**: Of 9857 patients (Direct, n = 6725; Transfer, n = 3132; 89.2% of transfers in South Korea), a favorable functional outcome occurred in 4701/6403 (73.4%) versus 1830/2991 (61.2%). Transfer was associated with lower odds overall (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.78-0.95), but estimates differed by country (South Korea 1.06, 0.95-1.18; Malaysia 0.53, 0.36-0.80; Vietnam 0.17, 0.11-0.25; interaction P < 0.001; I

**CONCLUSION**: Interhospital transfer was associated with a lower likelihood of a favorable functional outcome, but this was not uniform across the three trauma systems and was dominated by Korean data, in which no association was observed. These findings require confirmation in analyses anchored at injury or first medical contact.

articles.title: Injury patterns and early operative demand in a combined military and civilian casualty cohort: A single-centre study from the first 11 weeks of the 2023 Israel-Hamas war.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Modern asymmetric warfare and large-scale terror attacks produce distinctive wounding patterns that differ from conventional state-on-state conflict and impose specific early demands on receiving trauma systems. The 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel and the ensuing war generated a compressed surge of combined civilian and military casualties. We characterized injury patterns and linked them to early in-hospital resource use at a single tertiary trauma centre across the opening weeks of the conflict.

**METHODS**: We performed a retrospective descriptive cohort study of 192 consecutive trauma casualties admitted between 7 October and 24 December 2023. Demographics, mechanism of injury, injured anatomical regions, Injury Severity Score (ISS) and acute interventions were abstracted from the institutional trauma dataset. Mechanism and anatomical categories were not mutually exclusive. Variables were summarised as medians (IQR) or counts (percentages); missing data were not imputed and percentages were computed over non-missing observations.

**RESULTS**: Casualties were young (median age 24 years, IQR 21-35) and predominantly male (84.4%). Penetrating (43.2%) and shrapnel (31.2%) mechanisms predominated, followed by acoustic trauma (12.0%). Extremities were most often injured (lower limb 41.7%, upper limb 35.4%); 68.8% had at least one extremity injury and 37.0% had two or more injured regions. Median ISS was 9 (IQR 4-16); 26.5% of those with a recorded ISS had ISS ≥16. Blast and crush carried the highest median ISS (25 and 16). Early resource use was substantial: 23.4% required emergency surgery via direct emergency-room-to-operating-room transfer, 10.9% mechanical ventilation and 5.2% packed red-cell transfusion.

**CONCLUSIONS**: This extremity-predominant, penetrating-and-shrapnel profile, with a small but disproportionately severe blast and crush subgroup and frequent acoustic trauma, translated into early demand for emergency surgery, ventilation and transfusion. These patterns support resourcing limb-salvage and damage-control surgery, blood-bank and intensive-care readiness, and audiologic follow-up in military and mass-casualty trauma planning.

articles.title: Prehospital factors associated with calcium derangements upon arrival to the trauma center from scene - A subanalysis of a multicenter prospective study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Existing data suggests that hypocalcemia may be a factor in the lethal diamond of trauma. This could offer a potential opportunity for prehospital interventions to address these derangements. We performed a preplanned secondary analysis of data from a prospective multicenter study on calcium derangements in hemorrhage patients upon arrival at trauma centers.

**METHODS**: We conducted a prospective multicenter observational study of trauma patients admitted at the highest level of activation for three participating centers where an ionized calcium level was measured upon arrival. Data from the prehospital records were collected from the Emergency Medical Services reports. We compared study variables between patients who were hypocalcemic, eucalcemic, and hypercalcemic.

**RESULTS**: There were 1270 participants enrolled in our primary study, of whom 1047 arrived by EMS from the scene meeting inclusion for this analysis. Of these, 235 were hypocalcemic and 39 were hypercalcemic upon arrival. Patients with calcium derangements had lower survival compared to patients without derangements. Of those who were hypocalcemic, 32.8% received prehospital blood products, compared to 25.6% of those who were hypercalcemic upon arrival. There were 5 (12.8%) who were hypercalcemic that received prehospital calcium, potentially indicating iatrogenic hypercalcemia. Elevated prehospital shock indices were associated with both derangements. Of the 718 who received no fluids or blood, 116 (16.1%) were hypocalcemic and 27 (3.7%) were hypocalcemic with 2 hypercalcemic participants receiving calcium. Of those 136 that received a blood product prehospital, 77 were hypocalcemic (56.6%) with 1 receiving calcium, and 10 (7.4%) were hypercalcemic with 3 receiving calcium, and the remaining were eucalcemic with 4 (2.9%) receiving calcium.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Both hypocalcemia and hypercalcemia occurred in the setting of blood product and no blood product administration. Our study suggests that currently available assessment methods are inadequate for predicting the presence of a calcium derangement, both high and low.

**CLINICALTRIALS**: gov registration: NCT05885256.

articles.title: The blunt truth: The role of marijuana in PTSD after intentional traumatic injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Survivors of interpersonal violence experience high rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and rates of marijuana use are rising among young adults. There is however, limited understanding of marijuana use patterns among survivors of interpersonal violence with PTSD. We evaluated relationships between PTSD and marijuana use following injury and hypothesized that PTSD-positive patients would report elevated follow-up marijuana use.

**METHODS**: Between 10/2019 and 7/1/2024, we prospectively collected data on patient demographics, PTSD, substance use (including marijuana), and PROMIS-29 quality of life domains for adult trauma patients admitted to an urban, academic, level-1 trauma center. Participants were screened at baseline and at 6- or 12-month follow-up. Injury characteristics were collected from the institutional trauma registry. Among the intentionally injured, we compared patients by follow-up PTSD screening results. We excluded patients who screened positive for PTSD at baseline. Using multivariable logistic regression we assessed relationships between follow-up PTSD and marijuana use, including demographic and injury characteristics as covariates. Our primary outcome was dichotomized follow-up marijuana use.

**RESULTS**: Of 105 participants injured by intentional trauma with complete follow-up data, 69 screened negative for PTSD at baseline and therefore were included in this analysis. Patients who screened positive for PTSD at follow-up had greater marijuana use at baseline (29% vs 3%, p = 0.002) and follow-up (42% vs 13%, p = 0.007), and worse PROMIS-29 scores in all domains (p ≤ 0.01), compared to PTSD-negative patients. In multivariable analysis, screening positive for PTSD was associated with 7.1 times greater odds of marijuana use at follow-up (p = 0.007, CI:1.7, 29.5).

**CONCLUSIONS**: PTSD and marijuana use were closely associated in survivors of interpersonal violence. Screening efforts should account for marijuana use specifically. Routine screening for marijuana use could improve recognition of psychological challenges after trauma and could help identify patients at risk for development of PTSD.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Peripheral nerve blocks reduce opioid requirements in the first 24 h following surgical fixation of acute tibial shaft fractures.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To evaluate the effect of peripheral nerve blocks (PNB) on postoperative opioid use, length of stay (LOS), and incidence of acute compartment syndrome (ACS) in patients presenting with acute tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nail (IMN) fixation.

**METHODS**: Design: Retrospective cohort study Setting: Level 1 Academic Trauma Center from 2018 to 2022. Patient Selection Criteria: Patients aged 18-79 years with acute AO/OTA 42A-C tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN within 7 days of injury Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary outcome was postoperative opioid use, measured in morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during hospital stay, up to a maximum of 72 h after surgery. Patients who received a preoperative PNB were compared to those who did not receive a block. Secondary outcomes included postoperative LOS and incidence of ACS.

**RESULTS**: 246 patients were eligible for analysis of which 78 (32%) received a PNB (PNB=yes) and 168 (68%) did not (PNB=no). Mean MME were significantly lower in the PNB=yes group compared to the PNB=no group at 24 h (73 vs. 138, p < 0.001). Controlling for age, Injury Severity Score (ISS), and time to surgery, a multivariable regression model demonstrated a 36% reduction in MME per hour for patients that received PNBs. There were 3 cases of ACS in PNB=No and 1 in PNB=Yes. All 3 patients without a PNB were diagnosed within 2 days of surgery and underwent uncomplicated fasciotomies. One patient with a PNB re-presented to the hospital 5 days postoperatively, underwent fasciotomies, and was found to have anterior and lateral compartment necrosis.

**CONCLUSION**: PNBs for select acute tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN were associated with decreased opioid requirements in the first 24 h after surgery. No effect was noted beyond 24 h after surgery. Extreme vigilance is essential in patients with tibia fractures to monitor for ACS, especially when PNB is utilized.

articles.title: The downside of the pull-up: A 10-year national analysis of emergency department visits, 2015-2024.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: To characterize the epidemiology and clinical patterns of injuries related to pull-up and chin-up bars in a nationally representative emergency department (ED) dataset.

**METHODS**: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission National Electronic Injury Surveillance System from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024. Cases were identified using product code 3277 with narrative filters for "pull-up," "chin-up," and "doorway bar," excluding barbells and playground equipment. NEISS sampling weights produced national estimates. Annual totals with 95 % confidence intervals were calculated and reported. Injury characteristics were summarized by age group, body region, diagnosis, location, disposition, and a narrative-derived mechanism category (fall, struck by bar, slip or detachment, other).

**RESULTS**: An estimated 40,987 ED visits were attributed to pull-up bar injuries, averaging about 4000 per year, with a peak in 2024 (5421; 95 % CI, 5315-5527). Patients were predominantly male (66.1 %) with a bimodal age distribution centered on children 5-14 years and adults 18-34 years. Craniofacial trauma predominated, with head and face together comprising nearly one-half of presentations, followed by upper-extremity involvement, including shoulder, wrist, and forearm. Laceration, internal head injury, and fracture were the leading diagnoses, with sprain or strain and contusion also frequent. Most incidents occurred in the home, and 93.8 % of patients were treated and released. Falls were the most common mechanism, followed by struck-by events and a subset explicitly involving bar slip or detachment.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Pull-up bar injuries constitute a consistent national burden of craniofacial and upper-extremity trauma concentrated in youth and young adults, largely managed nonoperatively in acute care settings. Improved recognition of exercise-associated injury mechanisms may assist diagnostic accuracy and reduce the burden on emergency and orthopedic services.

articles.title: How the cause of surgical delay affects mortality in fragility hip fractures: A cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Prompt surgery for fragility hip fractures is a cornerstone of care and a key metric within the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) in the United Kingdom. Yet, since 2011, time to theatre has steadily increased, BPT adherence has fallen, and paradoxically, mortality has reduced. It is still unclear if surgical delay is an independent predictor of mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that the causes of surgical delays may be more important determinants of mortality than the delay itself.

**METHODS**: A cohort study of 1769 hip fracture patients above the age of 60 was conducted in a single centre in England. This study collected demographic data, timing to theatre (<36 h vs ≥36 h), reasons for any delays, 30-day mortality and 1-year mortality between March 2020 and December 2024.

**RESULTS**: The most common cause of delay was insufficient theatre capacity (N = 365, 20.6%), followed by delays awaiting medical stabilisation (N = 102, 5.8%). Age (Χ

**CONCLUSIONS**: While early surgery remains beneficial, patients delayed solely due to administrative reasons did not demonstrate an associated increase in mortality. Mortality associated with operative delay was primarily associated amongst patients with concurrent acute illnesses and co-morbidities, independently increasing risk. To improve mortality, the focus must remain on pre-operative optimisation and robust orthogeriatric assessment, rather than surgical timing alone. Future iterations of the BPT may benefit from incorporating the cause of delay and physiological risk stratification to surgical timing targets to better align national incentives with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: An anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide augments whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock in a rodent polytrauma model.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Severe trauma induces a cytokine storm that is associated with impaired resuscitation and recovery. We investigated the impact of AQB-565, an anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide, as a novel treatment adjunct for whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock using a rat polytrauma shock model.

**METHODS**: Hemorrhagic shock with polytrauma was induced in 64 Sprague-Dawley rats. The rats were randomized to receive one of four intravenous treatments at 15 minutes posthemorrhage (T15): saline control, AQB-565, tranexamic acid (TXA), or combined AQB-565+ TXA. The rats were given autologous transfusion of shed whole blood at 60 minutes and as needed thereafter to achieve mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 60 mm Hg for up to 3 hours. Survival, hemodynamics, cytokine profiles, and hemorrhage volumes were compared between groups.

**RESULTS**: There was a significant overall effect of treatment group on MAP (two-way rmANOVA p=0.02) that coincided with blood transfusion. MAP was significantly increased at T105 with AQB-565+TXA versus saline control (p=0.046). Inflammatory plasma cytokines, including interleukin-6, were significantly decreased with AQB-565 versus control groups (ANOVA p values ≤0.01). Seventeen (26.6%) rats died before 3 hours. There was a trend towards increased survival for treatments containing AQB-565 versus controls that was not statistically significant (Kaplan-Meier log rank p=0.06).

**CONCLUSIONS**: A melanocortin pathway-activating polypeptide suppressed inflammation and improved hemodynamic response to whole blood transfusion in this hemorrhagic shock model.

articles.title: Addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures reduces interfragmentary displacement - a biomechanical human cadaveric study.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: To investigate whether the addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures provides improved biomechanical construct stability and reduced interfragmentary displacement.

**METHODS**: A distal patellar pole fracture was simulated in sixteen fresh-frozen human cadaveric knees by a horizontal osteotomy in the distal third of the patella. Subsequently, locking plate fixation was performed. In a randomized half of the specimens, an additional McLaughlin wire cerclage was applied. The specimens were then subjected to 3000 cycles of extension starting at 90° of flexion under a maximum tensile load of 320 N. Using a Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system, the interfragmentary displacement between the proximal and distal fragments was measured at 1, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, and 3000 cycles. Statistical analysis was performed using repeated-measures ANOVA and Welch's unpaired t-t test at 3000 cycles.

**RESULTS**: An additional McLaughlin cerclage significantly reduced interfragmentary displacement under cyclic loading in comparison to locking plate fixation alone. After 3000 cycles, displacement was 2.27 ± 1.84 mm with plate fixation alone and 0.36 ± 0.22 mm with additional McLaughlin cerclage (mean difference 1.91 mm; 95% CI 0.38-3.45 mm; p = 0.0215).

**CONCLUSION**: An additional McLaughlin cerclage reduced interfragmentary displacement in distal patellar pole fractures. In cases of unstable distal pole patella fractures, the additional use of a McLaughlin cerclage may therefore be considered to enhance construct stability.

articles.title: Trauma care performance and patient outcomes - insights from a major trauma centre in Sweden.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Trauma is a leading cause of death among individuals under 45 years of age. Evaluating trauma system performance over time is important but inherently difficult due to concurrent changes in patient demographics, case-mix and care processes. The aim of this study was to describe temporal changes in patient demographics, injury severity and trauma care at a major trauma centre in Sweden from 2017 to 2023. We hypothesised that risk-adjusted 30-day mortality decreased and that time to computed tomography was reduced over the study period.

**METHODS**: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Karolinska Trauma Registry, including all trauma patients aged > 15 years fulfilling criteria for full trauma team activation, admitted between January 2017 and August 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess changes in 30-day mortality over time, adjusted for age, sex, injury severity category, ASA score and injury type. Time from arrival to computed tomography was analysed by linear regression and, because the distribution was skewed, by quantile (median) regression.

**RESULTS**: A total of 5,615 trauma patients were included. Over the study period, the patient population became older, and ASA scores increased, while injury severity and the proportion of penetrating injury remained unchanged. In multivariable logistic regression with 2017 as reference, the odds of 30-day mortality in 2022-2023 were lower (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43-0.88, P = 0.008) after adjusting for confounders. Median time to computed tomography decreased from 31 to 21 min; the adjusted difference in 2022-2023 compared with 2017 was - 7.5 min by linear regression (P = 0.014) and - 10.4 min by quantile regression (95% CI - 11.5 to - 9.2, P < 0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: Our findings are consistent with improvements in trauma care within a mature trauma system, with shorter median time to computed tomography and lower 30-day mortality despite an aging population with increasing comorbidity. However, the specific drivers of these changes are difficult to identify, and future studies should explore how individual components of pre-hospital and in-hospital care contribute to trauma outcomes.

articles.title: Embolization of the middle meningeal artery for non-acute subdural hematoma.
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of the embolization of the middle meningeal artery for non-acute subdural hematoma in adults. Secondary objectives To assess equity-related issues, including sex and gender, through subgroup analyses comparing the intervention's effects between male and female subjects, between younger and older adults, and across different pre-event functional status.

articles.title: Peripheral vascular trauma in a civilian Asian trauma centre: Epidemiology, management and outcomes over 9 years.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Peripheral vascular injuries (PVI) are uncommon but potentially limb-threatening complications of extremity trauma. Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore.

**METHODS**: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the institutional trauma registry of Tan Tock Seng Hospital between January 2013 and December 2021. Patients presenting with upper or lower extremity vascular injuries were identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) coding. Demographics, injury characteristics, anatomical injury patterns, interventions, and outcomes including limb salvage, complications, and inpatient mortality were analysed. Comparisons between upper and lower limb injuries were performed using appropriate statistical tests.

**RESULTS**: Among 77,990 trauma admissions, 180 patients sustained PVI (incidence 0.23%). Median age was 36 years and 87% were male. Overall, penetrating trauma was more common (58.9%), but lower limb injuries were predominantly due to blunt trauma (68%), particularly road traffic accidents. Lower limb PVIs were associated with higher injury severity than upper limb PVIs (p < 0.001). Operative management was required in most arterial and venous injuries. Primary repair and endovascular interventions demonstrated excellent limb salvage, whereas bypass procedures were associated with lower salvage rates. Overall limb salvage for lower limb PVI was 88%, with an amputation rate of 10% and mortality of 3%. Most (93%) were functionally independent at discharge.

**CONCLUSIONS**: PVI predominantly affects young male patients and are commonly associated with blunt trauma from road traffic accidents. Despite significant injury severity, favourable limb salvage and functional outcomes can be achieved with timely multidisciplinary management. These findings highlight the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary trauma care in optimizing outcomes following extremity vascular trauma.

articles.title: New developments in locking plate osteosynthesis - A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Plate osteosynthesis has evolved significantly, progressing from the first plates with externally protruding screws to anatomically precontoured systems designed for minimally invasive application. In this narrative review, we provide a brief recap of the history of locked plating and highlight the most relevant developments of the last two decades. These include anatomical innovations and mechanobiologically optimized plates, as well as emerging systems capable of monitoring the fracture healing progress.

articles.title: The use of PMMA bone cement in trauma surgery: A narrative review.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bone cement has been used for decades in orthopaedic surgery, primarily for fixation of endoprostheses. In trauma surgery, its role is more heterogeneous and often underappreciated.

**METHODS**: This narrative review summarizes the material properties, biological behavior, and clinical applications of PMMA in trauma surgery, including prosthesis fixation, screw augmentation, and its use as a temporary spacer. Finally, the use of PMMA used as a permanent spacer, including technical tips is described.

**RESULTS**: PMMA provides high compressive strength, minimal shrinkage, and reliable handling characteristics. Cement augmentation improves implant anchorage in osteoporotic bone. As a spacer, PMMA plays a key role in staged reconstruction. Finally, in selected patients and as a salvage procedure, PMMA may function as a permanent load-sharing implant when combined with stable internal fixation.

**CONCLUSION**: PMMA remains a versatile, inexpensive, and widely available tool in trauma surgery beyond its classical role in arthroplasty.

articles.title: Surface topography and nanostructural modifications for the prevention of bacterial infections.
articles.abstract: Implant-associated infections represent severe complications in orthopaedics and trauma surgery, largely driven by early bacterial adhesion and subsequent biofilm formation on device surfaces. The increasing incidence of multidrug-resistant pathogens further complicates management and underscores the urgent need for preventive, antibiotic-free strategies. Surface functionalization of implantable metals has emerged as a key approach to inhibit bacterial colonization at the implant-tissue interface while minimizing systemic toxicity and selective pressure for resistance. This review provides a comprehensive and clinically oriented overview of two major surface-based strategies: micro/nano-scale surface patterning (non-releasing approaches) and nanostructured antibacterial metallic coatings (releasing or contact-killing systems). Surface patterning modifies topography, wettability, and surface charge to reduce bacterial adhesion or induce mechanical disruption of bacterial membranes. Although highly promising in vitro and not reliant on the release of antimicrobial agents, hence not inserting compounds with potential toxicity, current evidence indicates that patterned surfaces alone often provide limited and transient protection in vivo, where protein adsorption and complex microbial communities may mask topographical effects. In contrast, nanostructured antibacterial metallic coatings offer broad-spectrum antibacterial and antibiofilm activity through ion release and/or contact-mediated mechanisms. Advances in plasma-assisted deposition technologies, including magnetron sputtering, pulsed laser deposition, and ionized jet deposition, enable precise control over coating thickness, morphology, and ion-release kinetics, thereby enhancing antibacterial efficacy while preserving biocompatibility and osteogenic potential. Recent in vivo data support the durability and safety of thin nanostructured coatings, highlighting their translational potential. Although not-yet clinically available, due to challenges in clinical translation of biomedical devices, these strategies can build a new generation of antibacterial device, with efficacy targeted to the microbial community and to tackling biofilm. Comparative observations suggest that while surface patterning represents a valuable complementary strategy, nanostructured metallic thin films currently provide more robust and clinically relevant antimicrobial performance. Future research should prioritize standardized antibiofilm testing models, validation in complex in vivo settings, combination strategies integrating patterning and coatings, and the rational tuning of multi-metal systems to address heterogeneous microbial communities.

articles.title: Cerclage wiring: Innovations and applications.
articles.abstract: Immediate full weight-bearing of osteosynthesis constructs is gaining increasing importance in modern trauma surgery. Many geriatric patients cannot reliably adhere to partial weight-bearing instructions, and younger patients may benefit from accelerated rehabilitation enabled by early full weight-bearing. In this context, an older technique of minimally invasive cerclage fixation of the tibia is receiving renewed attention. The surgical technique has been adapted to contemporary cerclage systems and biomechanically evaluated for the first time. Several studies using synthetic and cadaveric bone models have demonstrated that modern cable cerclages, particularly in spiral fractures, are capable of significantly increasing the stiffness of both locking plate and intramedullary nail osteosyntheses, provided that anatomical reduction is achieved through the cerclage. From a biomechanical standpoint, the additive cerclage thus enables immediate postoperative full weight-bearing. Early clinical studies suggest, that minimally invasive tibial cerclage can be applied without an increased complication rate and is associated with faster rehabilitation and higher patient satisfaction in the early postoperative phase. Although evidence is limited, the principle of additive cerclage appears to be transferable to humeral shaft spiral fractures.

articles.title: Overview and new developments in intramedullary and cephalomedullary nailing.
articles.abstract: The primary objectives of osteosynthetic fracture stabilization are accurate fracture reduction, restoration of the anatomical axis and rotational alignment, and the provision of adequate biomechanical and biological conditions to support bone healing. In fractures of long tubular bones, these goals can be optimally achieved by intramedullary nailing, which provides long-segment internal splinting along the anatomical axis of the bone combined with locking screws to ensure axial and rotational stability. In addition, intramedullary nailing is a tissue-preserving technique, as nail insertion is performed remote from the fracture site, thereby minimizing soft tissue trauma within the fracture zone. The indications for intramedullary nailing include epiphyseal and diaphyseal fractures of long bones, selected metaphyseal fractures that can be stabilized using anatomically contoured nails, as well as reconstructive procedures such as the treatment of nonunions, corrective osteotomies, and arthrodeses of the lower extremity. A major advantage of intramedullary nailing is the high primary stability of the implant, which generally allows early functional rehabilitation. The resulting biomechanical benefits permit early full weight bearing and, in the treatment of fracture healing disorders, are associated with high rates of osseous union. Continuous improvements in implant design and instrumentation, together with the introduction of anatomically contoured reconstruction nails, are expected to further expand the indications and effectiveness of intramedullary nailing. This narrative review summarizes historical milestones, biomechanical principles, technical aspects, and recent implant developments in intramedullary nailing, with a particular focus on cephalomedullary nailing for unstable trochanteric and subtrochanteric femoral fractures. Special emphasis is placed on fracture reduction quality, implant selection, and screw positioning, as these factors remain the strongest determinants of fixation stability and clinical outcome.

articles.title: Review of a "Bone Glue Fixation" development.
articles.abstract: The paper presents some of the background to the development of bone glues. Whilst there have been many attempts over the last 100 years to find a safe and effective biomimetic adhesive biomaterial it is only recently that promising and feasible candidates have been developed. In particular a formulation based on a combination of an amino acid, phosphoserine (PSer), together with calcium salts and water, has demonstrated the potential to meet clinically defined requirements for a bone adhesive (Osstic®). This bone glue has achieved first in human use after having demonstrated consistent preclinical performance.

articles.title: Alternate non-metallic implants in fracture care - A review.
articles.abstract: The use of implants in the treatment of fractures evolved over the last decades. Until today, most implant designs are based on metallic alloys such as Titanium or stainless steel. However, the global ageing population with increasing numbers of fragility and pathological fractures challenges current implant designs regarding stress shielding, fragile soft tissue and advanced demands like reduced imaging artefacts for radiotherapy planning. Therefore, alternative non-metallic implants that more closely resemble the mechanical properties of bone or provide additional stability as intramedullary augmentation have become available. This narrative-review summarizes the current available (2026) technology, biomechanical properties, clinical applications, outcomes and complications of CFR-PEEK implants and photodynamic bone stabilization implants in fracture management. In total n = 100 publications were taken into consideration for this narrative-review. Non-metallic-implants for fracture care are still a niche product in the treatment of fractures. However, with the ageing population and the increasing number of impaired bone quality and stability, these methods could help reduce stress shielding and force distribution comparable to physiological bone (CFR-PEEK implants) or allow additional augmentation (photodynamic bone stabilization) in reduced bone quality.

articles.title: Innovation in external fixation: Emerging hardware, software and automation technologies.
articles.abstract: External fixation remains a cornerstone of contemporary orthopaedic trauma and limb reconstruction surgery. While the biological principles for bone healing and regeneration established by Ilizarov continue to underpin modern practice, significant technological innovation has occurred over the past two decades. These developments have focused on improving construct stability, enhancing deformity correction accuracy, reducing technical complexity and improving the patient experience. Advances in hardware design have expanded fixation options and increased the adaptability of circular frames in complex trauma and reconstructive settings. Parallel developments in software have transformed deformity analysis, preoperative planning and correction execution through improved registration systems, virtual frame construction and cloud-based treatment platforms. More recently, remote patient support systems and automated strut technologies have sought to reduce the treatment burden associated with prolonged frame use. This review examines contemporary innovations in external fixation, focusing on developments in hardware, software, patient engagement technologies and automation. The available evidence is critically appraised and future directions explored. While many innovations demonstrate clear theoretical and practical advantages, robust clinical evidence remains limited for several emerging technologies. Nevertheless, the convergence of advanced engineering, digital health technologies and artificial intelligence is likely to fundamentally reshape the future of external fixation.

articles.title: Modernizing preoperative planning in orthopaedic trauma surgery.
articles.abstract: Preoperative planning in orthopaedic trauma remains largely experience-driven despite advances in imaging and predictive modeling. Although three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions improve fracture visualization, they do not routinely predict biomechanical stability across competing fixation strategies. Automated segmentation and finite element analysis (FEA) offer the potential to transition trauma planning from primarily anatomic to a method by which constructs may be optimized. This narrative review summarizes the current state of 3D planning and segmentation, describes the principles and established applications of FEA, delineates the workflow of finite element modeling in clinical practice, and integrates representative clinical cases to illustrate how plate positioning and screw configuration affect construct stability and works alongside the surgeon to help inform decisions. Broader implications for hospital systems, patients, and industry are discussed, along with future integration into navigation, robotics, and intraoperative 3D imaging workflows.

articles.title: Patient-specific instrument with 3D printing technology in orthopaedic trauma: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: 3D printing technology has been increasingly used in orthopaedic surgery. Current literature has demonstrated the benefits of applying 3D printing in orthopaedic trauma with the use of patient-specific instruments (PSI) including surgical guides and implants on selected bone fracture regions. This narrative review outlines the development of PSI including the navigation templates and implants using 3D printing technology. A comprehensive summary was presented for the application and effectiveness of PSI for fracture treatment in the upper extremities, pelvic region and lower extremities surgeries, particularly in regards to operative time, surgical accuracy and functional outcomes. 3D-printed patient-specific navigation guide had been used in reduction and fixation surgeries such as for navigating Kirschner wires (K-wire) insertion and screw placement in different bone fracture regions. PSI significantly increased surgical accuracy of K-wire insertion and screw placements, with significant reduction in operative time. For functional outcomes, 3D-printed navigation guide was comparable to conventional surgery. There are increasing studies exploring the clinical feasibility of patient-specific metal implant using 3D printing technology with advantage of high accuracy in fracture surgeries. Future studies to investigate the clinical efficacy of the patient-specific metal implants are warranted.

articles.title: Generation Z and engagement in orthopaedic trauma: A multigenerational qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Healthcare systems face increasing demand due to population ageing and workforce shortages. At the same time, Generation Z is entering surgical training. Their work values may differ from those of previous generations, potentially affecting engagement in demanding specialties such as orthopaedic trauma surgery. This study explores multigenerational perspectives on professional identity, work intensity, academic engagement, and work-life integration within orthopaedic trauma.

**METHODS**: Prior to the 2024 Leadership Forum of the Osteosynthesis and Trauma Care Foundation (OTCF), a standardized questionnaire consisting of declarative statements rated on a five-point Likert scale was distributed to orthopaedic trauma residents and senior consultants from international chapters. During the Forum, a moderated multigenerational discussion was conducted. The session was recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using thematic qualitative analysis.

**RESULTS**: Eight residents and fifteen consultants from Europe, North America, South America, Africa, and Asia participated. Across generations, intensive training was considered essential for achieving surgical mastery. However, younger participants emphasized work-life boundaries, institutional recognition of non-clinical work, and psychological safety. Senior surgeons more frequently described their profession as central to their identity and viewed unpaid academic engagement as intrinsic to surgical responsibility.

**CONCLUSION**: Generation Z trainees demonstrate strong commitment to orthopaedic trauma but differ from senior surgeons in expectations regarding professional identity, uncompensated academic work, and work-life integration. Recognition of evolving professional values is critical for workforce sustainability and intergenerational collaboration in trauma surgery.

articles.title: Tight rope fixation in fracture management.
articles.abstract: The use of tightrope fixation using metal buttons linked by suture material was first reported in 2005 when their use was suggested as an alternative to syndesmosis screws in ankle fractures associated with a diastasis. These implants are now used widely as a component of fixation in ankle fractures with a diastasis. The published results of their use in these injuries have shown that they are an effective method of treating diastasis of the ankle tibio-fibular syndesmosis with some evidence to suggest that they have a lower rate of malunion, fewer implant related complications, a reduced need for implant removal and in some trials better functional outcomes than screw fixation. Variations of these devices have also been used for fixation of lateral third clavicular fractures and acromioclavicular dislocations. Their use alone or in combination with plate fixation has been shown to be an effective method of fixation of lateral third clavicle fractures with a low rate of malunion and implant related problems. They have also shown to be an effective method of treatment for acromioclavicular dislocation, although there is still debate about the role of surgical treatment for these injuries. There are miscellaneous reports of their use for other fractures and dislocations in other anatomic locations notably for Lisfranc injuries in the foot. Better quality prospective clinical studies are still needed to define their exact role in fracture management.

articles.title: Adherent antimicrobial coatings for orthopaedic implants - A narrative review.
articles.abstract: There is a broad consensus among orthopaedic and trauma surgeons, as well as infection specialists, that antibacterial coatings represent an important tool for both the prevention and management of fracture-related infections. Nonetheless, the choice of commercially available implants fitted with an antibacterial coating remains limited. Intramedullary nails with resorbable, antibiotic eluting coatings have been commercially available for over a decade. Although multiple case series have shown evidence of efficacy of antimicrobial orthopaedic implants, randomized controlled trials are still lacking and their uptake in everyday clinical practice has been slow. More recently, nails with galvanic noble metal coatings were introduced, with encouraging clinical results. The most widely used coatings with the longest clinical track record are silver coated joint replacement endoprostheses, which have been successfully employed in revision surgeries and in patients undergoing tumor-related procedures. Silver coated plates are on the verge of market introduction and will represent the first of their kind to be broadly available. Overall, adherent antibacterial coatings are showing beneficial outcomes in terms of safety and efficacy. Health-technology assessments show cost effectiveness, demonstrating that in higher risk patient populations, the additional cost of using a coated implant is significantly less than the cost of treating an infection. Regulatory hurdles remain high, especially in the USA, where, to be best of our knowledge, coated implants have not been approved yet. Driven by the clear clinical need, we anticipate a dynamic near future in this field, with progress moving toward establishing coated implants as the standard of care for appropriate patient populations and expanding the range of available coating solutions. Such developments will ultimately benefit patients, surgeons, and the overall healthcare system.

articles.title: Distal femur plate-nail constructs. Belt and suspenders?
articles.abstract: Given the inherent complexity of distal femoral fractures and non-unions, management should be directed by an experienced orthopaedic trauma surgeon to ensure optimal reduction and stable fixation. This report describes the surgical technique of three cases managed with dual nail-plate fixation, supplemented by a review of contemporary literature regarding this hybrid construct. Evidence from meta-analyses suggests that combined fixation significantly minimizes total complications and reoperations compared to single-construct fixation in distal femur fractures. Notably, these clinical benefits are achieved without a significant increase in operative duration, blood loss, or hospital stay. However, the current literature is restricted to retrospective studies, underscoring the imperative for prospective randomized controlled trials to validate these clinical benefits.

articles.title: Past, present and future of distal radius corrective osteotomy: From 2D based reconstruction to 3D data-driven, patient specific care.
articles.abstract: Corrective osteotomy for distal radius malunion has evolved from two-dimensional (2D) radiograph based planning and surgeon performed geometric analysis to advanced three-dimensional (3D) virtual surgical planning (VSP). Historically guided by predefined radiographic parameters, contemporary practice increasingly emphasizes symptom severity and patient-specific functional goals. CT-based 3D models, contralateral surface matching, and patient-specific guides and implants have improved the accuracy of deformity correction. However, greater anatomical precision does not automatically translate into superior functional outcomes. Future progress depends on standardized evaluation frameworks, multicenter data collection, and predictive models to determine the clinical value of virtual surgical planning (VSP) and patient-specific implants (PSI) in delivering individualized, cost-effective and function-oriented care across the entire treatment pathway.

articles.title: 3D printed scaffolds for reconstruction of segmental long bone defects: A mini narrative review.
articles.abstract: Large segmental bone defects remain a major challenge in orthopedic reconstruction because successful healing requires both mechanical stability and coordinated biological regeneration. Although autologous bone grafting remains the clinical gold standard due to its osteogenic, osteoinductive, and osteoconductive properties, its application is limited by donor site morbidity, restricted graft availability, and increased operative burden. These limitations have stimulated the development of scaffold-based regenerative strategies aimed at restoring structural integrity while promoting bone regeneration. Recent advances in additive manufacturing have enabled the fabrication of patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) scaffolds with controlled architecture, porosity, and mechanical properties that approximate native bone structure. This mini-review summarizes recent developments in 3D-printed scaffolds for the reconstruction of long bone defects, with particular emphasis on differences between non-biodegradable metallic constructs and biodegradable polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials.
